ukberi-tibyan:147-147.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا كَانَ قَوْلَهُمْ إِلَّا أَنْ قَالُوا رَبَّنَا اغْفِرْ لَنَا ذُنُوبَنَا وَإِسْرَافَنَا فِي أَمْرِنَا وَثَبِّتْ أَقْدَامَنَا وَانْصُرْنَا عَلَى الْقَوْمِ الْكَافِرِينَ (١٤٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَمَا كَانَ قَوْلَهُمْ): the majority read it with fatḥa on the lām, on the view that the noun (ism) of كَانَ is what comes after «إِلَّا». This is stronger than making it the khabar (predicate) and the first the noun, for two reasons. The first: that (أَنْ قَالُوا) resembles the pronoun in that it cannot be described [by an adjective] [Translator's note: the text reads لَا يُضْمَرُ, "it is not made into a pronoun"; the usual wording of this argument is لَا يُوصَفُ, "it is not qualified by an adjective"], so it is more definite.
The second: that what comes after إِلَّا is affirmed, and the meaning is: their saying «رَبَّنَا اغْفِرْ لَنَا» was their habit in supplication. It is also read with the first in the nominative, on the view that it is the noun of كَانَ, and what comes after إِلَّا is the khabar. (فِي أَمْرِنَا): it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to the maṣdar (verbal noun), which is إِسْرَافُنَا; and it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from it, i.e. "an excess occurring in our affair".

ukberi-tibyan:150-150.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (بَلِ اللَّهُ مَوْلَاكُمْ وَهُوَ خَيْرُ النَّاصِرِينَ (١٥٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بَلِ اللَّهُ مَوْلَاكُمْ): a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). Al-Farrāʾ permitted the accusative, and it is a reading; the implied form is: "Rather, obey Allah" (بَلْ أَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ).

ukberi-tibyan:151-151.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (سَنُلْقِي فِي قُلُوبِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا الرُّعْبَ بِمَا أَشْرَكُوا بِاللَّهِ مَا لَمْ يُنَزِّلْ بِهِ سُلْطَانًا وَمَأْوَاهُمُ النَّارُ وَبِئْسَ مَثْوَى الظَّالِمِينَ (١٥١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الرُّعْبَ): it is read with sukūn on the ʿayn and with ḍamma on it, and they are two dialectal forms. (بِمَا أَشْرَكُوا): the bāʾ is attached (mutaʿalliq) to نُلْقِي, and the fact that «فِي» is also attached to it does not prevent this, because فِي is locative while the bāʾ has the sense of cause, so the two are different. مَا is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), and the second [مَا] is an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective, or has the sense of الَّذِي ("that which"), and is not maṣdariyya. (وَبِئْسَ مَثْوَى الظَّالِمِينَ): i.e. the Fire; so the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted. مَثْوَى is a mafʿal from ثَوَيْتُ ("I dwelt"), and its final radical (lām) is a yāʾ.

ukberi-tibyan:152-152.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَقَدْ صَدَقَكُمُ اللَّهُ وَعْدَهُ إِذْ تَحُسُّونَهُمْ بِإِذْنِهِ حَتَّى إِذَا فَشِلْتُمْ وَتَنَازَعْتُمْ فِي الْأَمْرِ وَعَصَيْتُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا أَرَاكُمْ مَا تُحِبُّونَ مِنْكُمْ مَنْ يُرِيدُ الدُّنْيَا وَمِنْكُمْ مَنْ يُرِيدُ الْآخِرَةَ ثُمَّ صَرَفَكُمْ عَنْهُمْ لِيَبْتَلِيَكُمْ وَلَقَدْ عَفَا عَنْكُمْ وَاللَّهُ ذُو فَضْلٍ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ (١٥٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (صَدَقَكُمُ اللَّهُ وَعْدَهُ): صَدَقَ is transitive to two objects in a construction like this one, and it may be transitive to the second by means of a preposition, so one says صَدَقْتَ زَيْدًا فِي الْحَدِيثِ ("you told Zayd the truth in the account"). (إِذْ): an adverb (ẓarf) for صَدَقَ, and it may be an adverb for الْوَعْد. (حَتَّى): it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted verb, its implied form being: "that continued until the time of your faltering". The correct view is that in a construction like this it is not attached to anything, and that it is not a preposition; rather, it is a particle that enters upon the clause with the meaning of limit (ghāya), just as the fāʾ and the wāw enter upon clauses. The apodosis (jawāb) of «إِذَا» is omitted, its implied form being: "your affair became clear"
and the like; what indicates the omitted element is His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْكُمْ مَنْ يُرِيدُ الدُّنْيَا وَمِنْكُمْ مَنْ يُرِيدُ الْآخِرَةَ). (ثُمَّ صَرَفَكُمْ): conjoined to the omitted verb.

ukberi-tibyan:153-153.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِذْ تُصْعِدُونَ وَلَا تَلْوُونَ عَلَى أَحَدٍ وَالرَّسُولُ يَدْعُوكُمْ فِي أُخْرَاكُمْ فَأَثَابَكُمْ غَمًّا بِغَمٍّ لِكَيْلَا تَحْزَنُوا عَلَى مَا فَاتَكُمْ وَلَا مَا أَصَابَكُمْ وَاللَّهُ خَبِيرٌ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ (١٥٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِذْ تُصْعِدُونَ): its implied form is: "Remember when" (اذْكُرُوا إِذْ); and it may be an adverb (ẓarf) for عَصَيْتُمْ, or تَنَازَعْتُمْ, or فَشِلْتُمْ. (وَلَا تَلْوُونَ): the majority read it with fatḥa on the tāʾ, and we have mentioned it at His saying: (يَلْوُونَ أَلْسِنَتَهُمْ). It is also read with ḍamma on the tāʾ, its past tense being أَلْوَى, and that is a dialectal form. It is also read: (عَلَى أُحُدٍ) with two ḍammas, and that is the mountain. [Translator's note: the text shows the word as أَحَدٍ with its usual vowelling; the reading meant is أُحُد, the mountain.]
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَالرَّسُولُ يَدْعُوكُمْ): a clause in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). (بِغَمٍّ): the implied form is: "after grief" (بَعْدَ غَمٍّ); on this view it is in the position of the accusative as an adjective of غَمًّا. It is also said: the meaning is "because of the grief", so it would be a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). It is also said: the implied form is "in exchange for grief" (بَدَلَ غَمٍّ), so it would also be an adjective of غَمًّا.
(لِكَيْلَا تَحْزَنُوا): it is said that «لَا» is redundant (zāʾida), because the meaning is that He grieved them in order to sadden them, as a punishment for their abandoning their positions. It is also said that it is not redundant, and the meaning is the negation of sadness from them through repentance. كَيْ here is the one that governs by itself, because of the lām before it.

ukberi-tibyan:154-154.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ثُمَّ أَنْزَلَ عَلَيْكُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ الْغَمِّ أَمَنَةً نُعَاسًا يَغْشَى طَائِفَةً مِنْكُمْ وَطَائِفَةٌ قَدْ أَهَمَّتْهُمْ أَنْفُسُهُمْ يَظُنُّونَ بِاللَّهِ غَيْرَ الْحَقِّ ظَنَّ الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ يَقُولُونَ هَلْ لَنَا مِنَ الْأَمْرِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ قُلْ إِنَّ الْأَمْرَ كُلَّهُ لِلَّهِ يُخْفُونَ فِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ مَا لَا يُبْدُونَ لَكَ يَقُولُونَ لَوْ كَانَ لَنَا مِنَ الْأَمْرِ شَيْءٌ مَا قُتِلْنَا هَاهُنَا قُلْ لَوْ كُنْتُمْ فِي بُيُوتِكُمْ لَبَرَزَ الَّذِينَ كُتِبَ عَلَيْهِمُ الْقَتْلُ إِلَى مَضَاجِعِهِمْ وَلِيَبْتَلِيَ اللَّهُ مَا فِي صُدُورِكُمْ وَلِيُمَحِّصَ مَا فِي قُلُوبِكُمْ وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِذَاتِ الصُّدُورِ (١٥٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَمَنَةً): the well-known reading has fatḥa on the mīm, and it is a noun for "security" (al-amn). It is also read with sukūn on it, and it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) like الْأَمْر. (نُعَاسًا): a badal (substitute); it may be an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition). It may also be that نُعَاسًا is the object and أَمَنَةً a ḥāl (circumstantial) from it, the original being "He sent down upon you drowsiness possessing security" (نُعَاسًا ذَا أَمَنَةٍ), because drowsiness is not itself security; rather, it is that through which security came about. It may also be that أَمَنَة is an object [Translator's note: the text has أَمَنَةٌ in the nominative here, as a cited word]. (يَغْشَى): it is read with the yāʾ, on the view that it is the drowsiness [that overcomes], and with the tāʾ, referring to the أَمَنَة; it is in the position of the accusative as an adjective of what precedes it. (طَائِفَةٌ) [Translator's note: the text vowels it طَائِفَةً in the accusative here, but it is discussing the nominative طَائِفَةٌ of the verse]: a mubtadaʾ (subject), and (قَدْ أَهَمَّتْهُمْ) is its khabar (predicate); «يَظُنُّونَ» is a ḥāl from the pronoun in أَهَمَّتْهُمْ. It may also be that أَهَمَّتْهُمْ is an adjective and يَظُنُّونَ the khabar, and the clause is a ḥāl, the governing word being يَغْشَى; this wāw is called the wāw of the ḥāl. It is also said that the wāw has the sense of إِذْ ("when"), but that amounts to nothing.
(غَيْرَ الْحَقِّ): the first object, i.e. "a matter other than the truth", and بِاللَّهِ is the second. (ظَنَّ الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ): a maṣdar, its implied form being: "a supposition resembling the supposition of the Jāhiliyya" [Translator's note: the text reads يُمَثِّلُ; the expected wording is مِثْلَ, "like"]. (مِنْ شَيْءٍ): مِنْ is redundant (zāʾida), and its position is nominative as a mubtadaʾ. On the khabar there are two views. The first: it is لَنَا, so on this view مِنَ الْأَمْرِ is a ḥāl, since the original is "Is there anything of the matter?" (هَلْ شَيْءٌ مِنَ الْأَمْرِ). The second: that مِنَ الْأَمْرِ is the khabar and لَنَا is for clarification (tabyīn), and the meaning is complete, as in His saying: (وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ كُفُوًا أَحَدٌ). (كُلَّهُ لِلَّهِ): it is read in the accusative as a tawkīd (emphasis) or a badal, with لِلَّهِ as the khabar; and in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, with لِلَّهِ as the khabar and the clause as the khabar of إِنَّ. (يَقُولُونَ): a ḥāl from the pronoun in يُخْفُونَ. (شَيْءٌ): the noun of كَانَ, and the khabar is لَنَا, or مِنَ الْأَمْرِ, as in «هَلْ لَنَا». (لَبَرَزَ الَّذِينَ): with fatḥa and without doubling [of the rāʾ]; and it is read with doubling (لَبُرِّزَ) as a verb whose agent is not named (passive), i.e. "they were brought out by the command of Allah".

ukberi-tibyan:156-156.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تَكُونُوا كَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَقَالُوا لِإِخْوَانِهِمْ إِذَا ضَرَبُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ أَوْ كَانُوا غُزًّى لَوْ كَانُوا عِنْدَنَا مَا مَاتُوا وَمَا قُتِلُوا لِيَجْعَلَ اللَّهُ ذَلِكَ حَسْرَةً فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ وَاللَّهُ يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ وَاللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ (١٥٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِذَا ضَرَبُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ): it may be that إِذَا here is used to narrate their state, so the future is not necessarily intended by it; on this view قَالُوا may govern it, though it is past. It may also be that كَفَرُوا and قَالُوا are past [in form] while the future is intended by them, the present state being narrated through it; on this view the implied form is: "they disbelieve and say to their brothers".
(أَوْ كَانُوا غُزًّى): the majority read it with doubling of the zāy, and it is the plural of غَازٍ ("one who goes raiding"). The regular form would be غُزَاةٌ, like قَاضٍ and قُضَاةٌ, but it came on the pattern fuʿʿal by analogy with the sound [root], as in شَاهِدٌ / شُهَّدٌ and صَائِمٌ / صُوَّمٌ. It is also read with the zāy undoubled (غُزًى), and there are two views on it. The first: that its origin is غُزَاةٌ, and the hāʾ [i.e. the tāʾ marbūṭa] was dropped for lightness, because the tāʾ is an indication of the plural, and that has already been obtained from the adjective form itself. The second: that he intended the reading of the majority, and dropped one of the two zāys out of dislike for doubling.
(لِيَجْعَلَ اللَّهُ): the lām is attached (mutaʿalliq) to something omitted, i.e. "He made them regret", or "He cast that into their hearts, in order to make it an anguish"; جَعَلَ here has the sense of صَيَّرَ ("to make into"). It is also said: the lām here is the lām of consequence (lām al-ʿāqiba), i.e. their affair came to that, as in His saying: (فَالْتَقَطَهُ آلُ فِرْعَوْنَ لِيَكُونَ لَهُمْ عَدُوًّا).

ukberi-tibyan:157-157.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَئِنْ قُتِلْتُمْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ أَوْ مُتُّمْ لَمَغْفِرَةٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَرَحْمَةٌ خَيْرٌ مِمَّا يَجْمَعُونَ (١٥٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَوْ مُتُّمْ): the majority read it with ḍamma on the mīm, and that is the basic form, because its verb is يَمُوتُ. It is also read with kasra (مِتُّمْ), and that is a dialectal form: one says مَاتَ يَمَاتُ, like خَافَ يَخَافُ; so just as you say خِفْتَ, you say مِتَّ. (لَمَغْفِرَةٌ): a mubtadaʾ (subject), and (مِنَ اللَّهِ) is its adjective (ṣifa). (وَرَحْمَةٌ): conjoined to it, and the implied form is: "and mercy for them". «خَيْرٌ» is the khabar (predicate). مَا has the sense of الَّذِي ("that which"), or is an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective, and the returning pronoun (al-ʿāʾid) is omitted. It may also be maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), in which case the object is omitted, i.e. "than their amassing wealth".

ukberi-tibyan:158-158.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَئِنْ مُتُّمْ أَوْ قُتِلْتُمْ لَإِلَى اللَّهِ تُحْشَرُونَ (١٥٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَإِلَى اللَّهِ): the lām is the answer to an omitted oath; and because it enters upon the preposition, it is permissible for «يُحْشَرُونَ» to come without being made emphatic with the nūn. The original is لَتُحْشَرُونَ إِلَى اللَّهِ. [Translator's note: the text writes «يُحْشَرُونَ» with yāʾ; the verse reads تُحْشَرُونَ.]

ukberi-tibyan:159-159.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَبِمَا رَحْمَةٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ لِنْتَ لَهُمْ وَلَوْ كُنْتَ فَظًّا غَلِيظَ الْقَلْبِ لَانْفَضُّوا مِنْ حَوْلِكَ فَاعْفُ عَنْهُمْ وَاسْتَغْفِرْ لَهُمْ وَشَاوِرْهُمْ فِي الْأَمْرِ فَإِذَا عَزَمْتَ فَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى اللَّهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الْمُتَوَكِّلِينَ (١٥٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَبِمَا رَحْمَةٍ): مَا is redundant (zāʾida). Al-Akhfash and others said: it may be an indefinite noun meaning "a thing" (شَيْء), with (رَحْمَةٍ) a badal (substitute) for it. The bāʾ is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «لِنْتَ». (وَشَاوِرْهُمْ فِي الْأَمْرِ): الْأَمْر here is generic; it is general [in form] but specific in what is intended, because he was not commanded to consult them about the obligatory duties. For that reason Ibn ʿAbbās read: «فِي بَعْضِ الْأَمْرِ» ("in some of the matter"). (فَإِذَا عَزَمْتَ): the majority read it with fatḥa on the zāy [Translator's note: so in the text; the vowel in question is that of the final tāʾ, as the next sentence shows], i.e. when you have chosen a course through consultation and resolved to carry it out, «فَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى اللَّهِ» ("then put your trust in Allah").
It is also read with ḍamma on the tāʾ (عَزَمْتُ), i.e. "when I command you to do something, then put your trust in Me"; so the overt noun was put in place of the pronoun.

ukberi-tibyan:160-160.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنْ يَنْصُرْكُمُ اللَّهُ فَلَا غَالِبَ لَكُمْ وَإِنْ يَخْذُلْكُمْ فَمَنْ ذَا الَّذِي يَنْصُرُكُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِهِ وَعَلَى اللَّهِ فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ (١٦٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَمَنْ ذَا الَّذِي): it is like «مَنْ ذَا الَّذِي يُقْرِضُ», and it has been mentioned. (مِنْ بَعْدِهِ): i.e. after His forsaking [you], so the muḍāf was omitted. It may also be that the hāʾ is the pronoun of the forsaking, i.e. after the forsaking.

ukberi-tibyan:161-161.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا كَانَ لِنَبِيٍّ أَنْ يَغُلَّ وَمَنْ يَغْلُلْ يَأْتِ بِمَا غَلَّ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ ثُمَّ تُوَفَّى كُلُّ نَفْسٍ مَا كَسَبَتْ وَهُمْ لَا يُظْلَمُونَ (١٦١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَنْ يَغُلَّ): it is read with fatḥa on the yāʾ and ḍamma on the ghayn, attributing the act to the Prophet, i.e. that is not possible for him; this is indicated by His saying: (يَأْتِ بِمَا غَلَّ). The object of يَغُلُّ is omitted, i.e. "to embezzle the spoils" or "the wealth".
It is also read with ḍamma on the yāʾ and fatḥa on the ghayn (يُغَلَّ), as a verb whose agent is not named (passive). On its meaning there are three views. The first: that its past tense is أَغْلَلْتُهُ, i.e. "I attributed embezzlement (ghulūl) to him", just as you say أَكْذَبْتُهُ when you attribute lying to him; i.e. it is not to be said of him that he embezzles, i.e. betrays. The second: it is from أَغْلَلْتُهُ when you find him to be an embezzler, as you say أَحْمَدْتُ الرَّجُلَ when you find the man praiseworthy. The third: its meaning is that someone else embezzles from him, i.e. it is not for a prophet to be betrayed. (وَمَنْ يَغْلُلْ): resumptive. It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial), and the implied sense would be: "in the state of the embezzler's knowing the punishment for embezzlement".

ukberi-tibyan:162-162.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَفَمَنِ اتَّبَعَ رِضْوَانَ اللَّهِ كَمَنْ بَاءَ بِسَخَطٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَمَأْوَاهُ جَهَنَّمُ وَبِئْسَ الْمَصِيرُ (١٦٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَفَمَنِ اتَّبَعَ): مَنْ has the sense of الَّذِي ("the one who") and is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «كَمَنْ» is the khabar (predicate). It cannot be conditional, because كَمَنْ is not fit to be an apodosis (jawāb). (بِسَخَطٍ): a ḥāl (circumstantial).

ukberi-tibyan:163-163.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (هُمْ دَرَجَاتٌ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ وَاللَّهُ بَصِيرٌ بِمَا يَعْمَلُونَ (١٦٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (هُمْ دَرَجَاتٌ): a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), and the implied form is: "possessors of degrees" (ذُو دَرَجَاتٍ), so the muḍāf was omitted. (عِنْدَ اللَّهِ): an adverb (ẓarf) for the meaning of دَرَجَاتٌ, as though He said: "they differ in rank with Allah". It may also be an adjective of دَرَجَاتٌ.

ukberi-tibyan:164-164.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَقَدْ مَنَّ اللَّهُ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ إِذْ بَعَثَ فِيهِمْ رَسُولًا مِنْ أَنْفُسِهِمْ يَتْلُو عَلَيْهِمْ آيَاتِهِ وَيُزَكِّيهِمْ وَيُعَلِّمُهُمُ الْكِتَابَ وَالْحِكْمَةَ وَإِنْ كَانُوا مِنْ قَبْلُ لَفِي ضَلَالٍ مُبِينٍ (١٦٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْ أَنْفُسِهِمْ): in the position of the accusative as an adjective of رَسُولًا; it may also be attached (mutaʿalliq) to بَعَثَ. What is in this verse has been mentioned, in a similar form, at His saying: (رَبَّنَا وَابْعَثْ فِيهِمْ رَسُولًا مِنْهُمْ) [al-Baqara: 129].

ukberi-tibyan:165-165.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَوَلَمَّا أَصَابَتْكُمْ مُصِيبَةٌ قَدْ أَصَبْتُمْ مِثْلَيْهَا قُلْتُمْ أَنَّى هَذَا قُلْ هُوَ مِنْ عِنْدِ أَنْفُسِكُمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ (١٦٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (قَدْ أَصَبْتُمْ مِثْلَيْهَا): in the position of the nominative as an adjective of مُصِيبَةٌ.

ukberi-tibyan:1-2.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (الم (١) اللَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ (٢)).
(الم): discussion of it has already preceded at the beginning of al-Baqara. The mīm of «ميم» was given a vowel because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, namely the mīm and the lām of definiteness in the name Allah. It was not given a vowel because of its own sukūn together with the sukūn of the yāʾ before it, because all these letters of this pattern are quiescent when no quiescent letter meets them after them, as in His saying لام ميم ذلك الكتاب, and «حم», «طس», «ق» and «ك». It was given fatḥa for two reasons. The first: the frequent use of the name Allah after it. The second: the heaviness of a kasra after a yāʾ and a kasra. Al-Akhfash allowed giving it kasra, and that has the ugliness we have mentioned.
It has been said that it was given fatḥa because the vowel of the hamza of Allah was thrown onto it. This is far-fetched, because the connecting hamza (hamzat al-waṣl) has no share in remaining in continuous speech such that its vowel could be thrown onto something else.
It has also been said that the hamza in Allah is a disjunctive hamza (hamzat al-qaṭʿ) and was only dropped because of frequent use; therefore its vowel was thrown onto the mīm, since it deserves to remain. This holds according to the view of those who make the instrument of definiteness أل.
(اللَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ): its i'rab has been mentioned at the Verse of the Throne (āyat al-kursī).

ukberi-tibyan:3-4.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (نَزَّلَ عَلَيْكَ الْكِتَابَ بِالْحَقِّ مُصَدِّقًا لِمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ وَأَنْزَلَ التَّوْرَاةَ وَالْإِنْجِيلَ (٣) مِنْ قَبْلُ هُدًى لِلنَّاسِ وَأَنْزَلَ الْفُرْقَانَ إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ شَدِيدٌ وَاللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ ذُو انْتِقَامٍ (٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (نَزَّلَ عَلَيْكَ): it is another khabar (predicate), and what we mentioned at His saying (لَا تَأْخُذُهُ) applies likewise here.
It has been read «نَزَلَ» عليك without doubling, with «الكتابُ» in the nominative. There are two views on the clause:
The first: it is cut off [from what precedes]. The second: it is connected to what precedes it, and the pronoun is omitted, its implied form being: "from Him".
(بِالْحَقِّ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الكتاب. (مُصَدِّقًا): if you wish you make it a second ḥāl; if you wish you make it a badal (substitute) from the position of His saying «بالحق»; and if you wish you make it a ḥāl from the pronoun in the genitive phrase.
(التَّوْرَاةَ): on the pattern fawʿala, from وَرَى الزَّنْدُ يَرِي, said when fire comes out of the fire-stick; so it is as if the Torah were a light out of error. Its origin is وَوْرَيَة; the first wāw was changed into tāʾ, as they said تَوْلَج whose origin is وَوْلَج, and the yāʾ was changed into alif because it is vowelled and what precedes it has fatḥa.
Al-Farrāʾ said: its origin is تَوْرِيَة on the pattern tafʿila, like تَوْصِيَة; then the kasra was replaced by fatḥa, so the yāʾ turned into an alif, as they said ناصاة for ناصية. It may be pronounced with imāla, because the origin of its alif is a yāʾ.
(وَالْإِنْجِيلَ): on the pattern ifʿīl, from النَّجْل, which is the root from which other things branch out; hence a child is called نَجْل, and one says استنجل الوادي when its water seeps out.
It has been said that it is from [the meaning of] spaciousness, from their saying نجلتُ الإهاب ("I slit the hide"); and from it [comes] عين نجلاء, an eye wide of opening. So the Injīl, which is the book of Jesus, contained a latitude that the Jews did not have.
Al-Ḥasan read «الأَنجيل» with fatḥa on the hamza; no parallel to it is known, since there is no afʿīl pattern in the language. However, al-Ḥasan is trustworthy, so it may be that he heard it.
(مِنْ قَبْلُ) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to أنزل. «قبلُ» was made indeclinable (mabnī) because it was cut off from construct; the origin is من قبل ذلك, so قبل has the status of part of a noun, and part of a noun does not merit declension.
(هُدًى): a ḥāl from الإنجيل and التوراة; it was not put in the dual because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun).
And it may be a ḥāl from الإنجيل, indicating an omitted ḥāl for التوراة, just as one of two khabars indicates the other. (لِلنَّاسِ) may be a naʿt (adjective) of هدى, and may be attached to it.
(الْفُرْقَانَ): on the pattern fuʿlān from الفَرْق; it is originally a maṣdar, so it may mean "the one that separates" or "the thing separated", and the implied form may be: "the possessor of the Furqān".
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ): mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar in the position of the khabar of إنّ; and العذاب may be nominative by the adverbial phrase (ẓarf).

ukberi-tibyan:5-5.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَخْفَى عَلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلَا فِي السَّمَاءِ (٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فِي الْأَرْضِ): it may be a naʿt (adjective) of شيء, and it may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to يخفى.

ukberi-tibyan:6-6.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (هُوَ الَّذِي يُصَوِّرُكُمْ فِي الْأَرْحَامِ كَيْفَ يَشَاءُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ (٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فِي الْأَرْحَامِ): في is attached (mutaʿalliq) to يصوّر.
And it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the kāf and mīm, i.e. "He shapes you while you are lumps of flesh in the wombs".
(كَيْفَ يَشَاءُ): كيف is in the position of the accusative by يشاء; it is a ḥāl, and the object is omitted, its implied form being: "[as] He wills your shaping".
It has been said that كيف is an adverb (ẓarf) for يشاء, and the position of the clause is a ḥāl, its implied form being: "He shapes you according to His will", i.e. willing; on this view it is a ḥāl from the pronoun of the name of Allah.
And it may be a ḥāl from the kāf and mīm, i.e. "He shapes you as you pass through stages according to His will".
(لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ): it is like His saying (لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الرَّحْمَنُ الرَّحِيمُ).

ukberi-tibyan:47-47.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالَتْ رَبِّ أَنَّى يَكُونُ لِي وَلَدٌ وَلَمْ يَمْسَسْنِي بَشَرٌ قَالَ كَذَلِكِ اللَّهُ يَخْلُقُ مَا يَشَاءُ إِذَا قَضَى أَمْرًا فَإِنَّمَا يَقُولُ لَهُ كُنْ فَيَكُونُ (٤٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (كَذَلِكِ اللَّهُ يَخْلُقُ): this has been treated under His saying (كَذَلِكَ اللَّهُ يَفْعَلُ مَا يَشَاءُ), in the story of Zakariyyā.
And (إِذَا قَضَى أَمْرًا) is explained in al-Baqara.

ukberi-tibyan:48-49.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَيُعَلِّمُهُ الْكِتَابَ وَالْحِكْمَةَ وَالتَّوْرَاةَ وَالْإِنْجِيلَ (٤٨) وَرَسُولًا إِلَى بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ أَنِّي قَدْ جِئْتُكُمْ بِآيَةٍ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ أَنِّي أَخْلُقُ لَكُمْ مِنَ الطِّينِ كَهَيْئَةِ الطَّيْرِ فَأَنْفُخُ فِيهِ فَيَكُونُ طَيْرًا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ وَأُبْرِئُ الْأَكْمَهَ وَالْأَبْرَصَ وَأُحْيِي الْمَوْتَى بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ وَأُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِمَا تَأْكُلُونَ وَمَا تَدَّخِرُونَ فِي بُيُوتِكُمْ إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَآيَةً لَكُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ (٤٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَيُعَلِّمُهُ): it is read with nūn, by analogy with His saying (ذَلِكَ مِنْ أَنْبَاءِ الْغَيْبِ نُوحِيهِ إِلَيْكَ), and it is read with yāʾ, by analogy with «يُبَشِّرُكَ». Its position is that of a ḥāl (circumstantial) conjoined to (وَجِيهًا).
(وَرَسُولًا): there are two views on it. The first: it is an adjective, like صَبُور and شَكُور, so it is likewise a ḥāl; or it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) on the implied wording "and He will make him a messenger". Faʿūl here has the sense of mufʿal, i.e. مُرْسَلًا ("sent").
The second: that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), as the poet said:
أَبْلِغْ أَبَا سَلْمَى رَسُولًا تُرَوِّعُهُ.
("Convey to Abū Salmā a message that will alarm him.")
On this view it may be a maṣdar in the position of a ḥāl, or an object conjoined to الْكِتَابَ, i.e. "We will teach him a message (رِسَالَةً)". On both views, «إِلَى» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to رَسُول, because both of them (the adjective and the maṣdar) operate as the verb operates. It is also possible for «إِلَى» to be a naʿt (adjective) of رَسُول, in which case it is attached to something omitted.
(أَنِّي): there are three views on the position of the clause. The first: genitive, i.e. «بِأَنِّي»; this is the doctrine of al-Khalīl. Were the bāʾ overt, it would be attached to رَسُول, or to something omitted that is an adjective of رَسُول, i.e. "speaking (نَاطِقًا) of the fact that I…", or "informing (مُخْبِرًا)".
The second: its position is accusative, on account of the position (after removal of the preposition), which is the doctrine of Sībawayh; or on the implied wording "he mentions that I…". It may also be a badal (substitute) of رَسُول if you make that a maṣdar, the implied wording being: "and We will teach him that I have come to you".
The third: its position is nominative, i.e. "it is that I have come to you" — again if you make رَسُولًا a maṣdar.
(بِآيَةٍ): in the position of a ḥāl, i.e. "arguing by means of a sign".
(مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ): it may be an adjective of آيَة, or attached to جِئْتُ.
(أَنِّي أَخْلُقُ): it is read with fatḥa on the hamza, and there are three views on its position. The first: genitive, as a badal of آيَة. The second: nominative, i.e. "it is that I…". The third: that it is a badal of the first «أَنِّي».
It is also read with kasra on the hamza, as a new sentence (istiʾnāf), or on the implied ellipsis of the verb "to say".
(كَهَيْئَةِ): the kāf is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt of an omitted object, i.e. "a shape like the shape of the bird". «الْهَيْئَة» is a maṣdar in the sense of «الْمُهَيَّأ» (the thing shaped), just as «الْخَلْق» is used in the sense of «الْمَخْلُوق» (the thing created).
It is also said: «الْهَيْئَة» is a noun for the state of a thing and is not a maṣdar; the maṣdar is «التَّهَيُّؤ» and «التَّهْيِئَة».
It is also read (كَهَيْئَةِ الطَّيْرِ) by transferring the vowel of the hamza onto the yāʾ and dropping the hamza. [Translator's note: the variant is printed here with the same spelling as the standard reading; what is meant is the form with the hamza dropped, «كَهَيَةِ».] The derivation of الطَّيْر and its rules have been mentioned in al-Baqara. The hāʾ in (فِيهِ) refers back to the meaning of «الْهَيْئَة», because it has the sense of «الْمُهَيَّأ».
It may also refer back to the kāf, because it is a noun meaning "like" (مِثْل); or to الطَّيْر; or to the omitted object.
(فَيَكُونُ): i.e. "and it becomes". So كَانَ here may be the complete (tāmma) one, since its meaning is صَارَ ("became"), and صَارَ in the sense of "moved (from one state to another)". It may also be the incomplete (nāqiṣa) one. On the first view «طَائِرًا» is a ḥāl, and on the second it is the khabar (predicate). [Translator's note: the author cites «طَائِرًا», which is the reading of Nāfiʿ (and others); the text quoted above has «طَيْرًا».]
And (بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ) is attached to يَكُونُ. (بِمَا تَأْكُلُونَ): «مَا» may be in the sense of «الَّذِي» (a relative noun), an indefinite qualified noun, or maṣdariyya (verbal-noun-forming); and likewise the other «مَا». The original form of (تَدَّخِرُونَ) is تَذْدَخِرُونَ; but the dhāl is voiced (majhūra) and the tāʾ is voiceless (mahmūsa), so they could not stand together. The tāʾ was therefore changed to dāl, because dāl is from its point of articulation, so as to approach the dhāl; then the dhāl was changed to dāl and assimilated. Some of the Arabs change the tāʾ to dhāl and assimilate (giving تَذَّخِرُونَ). It is also read with a light (unassimilated) dhāl and fatḥa on the khāʾ, and its past tense is ذَخُرَ.

ukberi-tibyan:50-50.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمُصَدِّقًا لِمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيَّ مِنَ التَّوْرَاةِ وَلِأُحِلَّ لَكُمْ بَعْضَ الَّذِي حُرِّمَ عَلَيْكُمْ وَجِئْتُكُمْ بِآيَةٍ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ (٥٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَمُصَدِّقًا): a ḥāl (circumstantial) conjoined to His saying «بِآيَةٍ», i.e. "I have come to you with a sign and confirming «لِمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيَّ»". It cannot be conjoined to وَجِيهًا, because that would require it to be «وَمُصَدِّقًا لِمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ» in the third person. «مِنَ التَّوْرَاةِ» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl of the latent (mustatir) pronoun in the adverb, which is «بَيْنَ»; what governs it is the notion of settledness (al-istiqrār), or the adverb itself. It may also be a ḥāl of «مَا», in which case what governs it is «مُصَدِّقًا».
(وَلِأُحِلَّ): it is conjoined to something omitted, its implied form being "so that I may lighten (your burden)", or the like.
(وَجِئْتُكُمْ بِآيَةٍ): this is a repetition for emphasis, because this meaning has already come in the preceding verse.

ukberi-tibyan:52-52.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَلَمَّا أَحَسَّ عِيسَى مِنْهُمُ الْكُفْرَ قَالَ مَنْ أَنْصَارِي إِلَى اللَّهِ قَالَ الْحَوَارِيُّونَ نَحْنُ أَنْصَارُ اللَّهِ آمَنَّا بِاللَّهِ وَاشْهَدْ بِأَنَّا مُسْلِمُونَ (٥٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْهُمُ الْكُفْرَ): «مِنْ» may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to أَحَسَّ, or be a ḥāl (circumstantial) of الْكُفْر. (أَنْصَارِي): it is the plural of نَصِير, like شَرِيف and أَشْرَاف.
Some said: it is the plural of نَصْر, but this is weak, unless you assume the omission of a muḍāf in it, i.e. "who are the possessors of my help", or you make it a maṣdar (verbal noun) used as a description. And (إِلَى) is in the position of a ḥāl, attached to something omitted, its implied form being: "who are my helpers, joined (مُضَافًا) to Allah", or "to the helpers of Allah". It is also said that it means «مَعَ» ("with"), but this is nothing, for «إِلَى» is not fit to mean «مَعَ», and no analogy supports it.
(الْحَوَارِيُّونَ): the majority read it with a doubled yāʾ, which is the original, because it is the yāʾ of relation (nisba).
It is also read with a light yāʾ, because (the reader) fled from the doubling of the yāʾ, and made the ḍamma on the remaining yāʾ an indication of the original — just as they read (يَسْتَهْزِئُونَ), even though a ḍamma on a yāʾ after a kasra is felt to be heavy. [Translator's note: the source has «دَلِيلٌ» in the nominative where the accusative «دَلِيلًا» is expected; translated as intended.]
The derivation of the word is from al-ḥawar, which is whiteness; the disciples used to bleach (wash white) garments.
It is also said: its derivation is from حَارَ يَحُورُ, when one returns, so it is as though they are those returning to Allah. And it is said: it is derived from purity of heart, its sincerity and its truthfulness.

ukberi-tibyan:53-53.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (رَبَّنَا آمَنَّا بِمَا أَنْزَلْتَ وَاتَّبَعْنَا الرَّسُولَ فَاكْتُبْنَا مَعَ الشَّاهِدِينَ (٥٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَاكْتُبْنَا مَعَ الشَّاهِدِينَ): there is an omission in the wording, its implied form being: "with those who bear witness to You of (Your) Oneness".

ukberi-tibyan:54-54.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَكَرُوا وَمَكَرَ اللَّهُ وَاللَّهُ خَيْرُ الْمَاكِرِينَ (٥٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَاللَّهُ خَيْرُ الْمَاكِرِينَ): He put the overt noun in the place of the pronoun for magnification; the original is «وَهُوَ خَيْرُ الْمَاكِرِينَ».

ukberi-tibyan:55-55.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِذْ قَالَ اللَّهُ يَا عِيسَى إِنِّي مُتَوَفِّيكَ وَرَافِعُكَ إِلَيَّ وَمُطَهِّرُكَ مِنَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَجَاعِلُ الَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوكَ فَوْقَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا إِلَى يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ ثُمَّ إِلَيَّ مَرْجِعُكُمْ فَأَحْكُمُ بَيْنَكُمْ فِيمَا كُنْتُمْ فِيهِ تَخْتَلِفُونَ (٥٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مُتَوَفِّيكَ وَرَافِعُكَ إِلَيَّ): both refer to the future and do not become definite through the genitive construct (iḍāfa). The implied order is: «رَافِعُكَ إِلَيَّ وَمُتَوَفِّيكَ», because he was raised to heaven and will die after that.
It is also said: the wāw is for joining (without order), so there is no difference between putting first and putting last.
It is also said: «مُتَوَفِّيكَ» (means taking you) from among them, and «رَافِعُكَ» (means raising you) to heaven, so there is no putting forward or back in it.
(وَجَاعِلُ الَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوكَ): it is said that it is an address to our Prophet, upon him be blessing and peace, so the preceding speech is complete in itself. It is also said that it is to ʿĪsā, and the meaning is that those who followed him are victorious over the Jews and other disbelievers until just before the Day of Resurrection, through dominion and supremacy. As for the Day of Resurrection, He will judge between them and recompense each according to his deeds.

ukberi-tibyan:56-57.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا فَأُعَذِّبُهُمْ عَذَابًا شَدِيدًا فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ وَمَا لَهُمْ مِنْ نَاصِرِينَ (٥٦) وَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ فَيُوَفِّيهِمْ أُجُورَهُمْ وَاللَّهُ لَا يُحِبُّ الظَّالِمِينَ (٥٧).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا): «الَّذِينَ» may be a mubtadaʾ (subject), with «فَأُعَذِّبُهُمْ» its khabar (predicate).
«الَّذِينَ» may also be in the position of the accusative, governed by an omitted verb that «فَأُعَذِّبُهُمْ» explains, its implied form being «فَأُعَذِّبُ» without an object pronoun, because it governs the overt noun before it. It was then omitted, and the verb occupied with the pronoun was made its explanation. The position of the omitted verb is after the ṣila (relative clause). [Translator's note: the source says «الْمَشْغُولَ بِضَمِيرِ الْفَاعِلِ» ("occupied with the pronoun of the agent"); the occupying pronoun here is the object pronoun هُم, so «الْمَفْعُولِ» may be intended.]
The verb cannot be assumed before «الَّذِينَ», because «أَمَّا» is not followed directly by a verb. Like it is: (وَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ فَيُوَفِّيهِمْ), and (وَأَمَّا ثَمُودُ فَهَدَيْنَاهُمْ) in the reading of those who read it in the accusative.

ukberi-tibyan:58-58.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ذَلِكَ نَتْلُوهُ عَليْكَ مِنَ الْآيَاتِ وَالذِّكْرِ الْحَكِيمِ (٥٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (ذَلِكَ نَتْلُوهُ): there are three views on it. The first: «ذَلِكَ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «نَتْلُوهُ» its khabar (predicate).
The second: the mubtadaʾ is omitted and «ذَلِكَ» is its khabar, i.e. "the matter is that"; and «نَتْلُوهُ» is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "the matter pointed to, being recited"; and «مِنَ الْآيَاتِ» is a ḥāl of the hāʾ.
The third: «ذَلِكَ» is a mubtadaʾ, «مِنَ الْآيَاتِ» its khabar, and «نَتْلُوهُ» a ḥāl, governed by the meaning of pointing (in the demonstrative). «ذَلِكَ» may also be in the position of the accusative, governed by a verb indicated by «نَتْلُوهُ», its implied form being «نَتْلُو ذَلِكَ»; «مِنَ الْآيَاتِ» would then likewise be a ḥāl of the hāʾ. And (الْحَكِيمِ) here means «الْمُحْكَم» ("made firm").

ukberi-tibyan:59-59.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ مَثَلَ عِيسَى عِنْدَ اللَّهِ كَمَثَلِ آدَمَ خَلَقَهُ مِنْ تُرَابٍ ثُمَّ قَالَ لَهُ كُنْ فَيَكُونُ (٥٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (خَلَقَهُ مِنْ تُرَابٍ): this clause is an explanation of the likeness (al-mathal), so it has no grammatical position. It is also said: its position is that of a ḥāl (circumstantial) of آدَم, with «قَدْ» implied along with it, and what governs it is the meaning of comparison. The hāʾ refers to آدَم, and «مِنْ» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «خَلَقَ». It is weak for it (the prepositional phrase) to be a ḥāl, because the implied wording would become "He created him, being from dust", and that is not the meaning. (ثُمَّ قَالَ لَهُ): «ثُمَّ» here is for ordering the report, not for ordering what is reported, because His saying «كُنْ» did not come later than His creating him; rather, in meaning it is an explanation of the meaning of creating. «ثُمَّ» has come without being restricted to the order of what is reported, as in His saying (فَإِلَيْنَا مَرْجِعُهُمْ ثُمَّ اللَّهُ شَهِيدٌ), and you say: «زَيْدٌ عَالِمٌ، ثُمَّ هُوَ كَرِيمٌ» ("Zayd is learned, and moreover he is generous"). It may also be for ordering what is reported, on the basis that the meaning is: He formed him as clay, then said to him: "Be flesh and blood."

ukberi-tibyan:61-61.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَمَنْ حَاجَّكَ فِيهِ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا جَاءَكَ مِنَ الْعِلْمِ فَقُلْ تَعَالَوْا نَدْعُ أَبْنَاءَنَا وَأَبْنَاءَكُمْ وَنِسَاءَنَا وَنِسَاءَكُمْ وَأَنْفُسَنَا وَأَنْفُسَكُمْ ثُمَّ نَبْتَهِلْ فَنَجْعَلْ لَعْنَةَ اللَّهِ عَلَى الْكَاذِبِينَ (٦١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَمَنْ حَاجَّكَ فِيهِ): the hāʾ is the pronoun of ʿĪsā; «مَنْ» is conditional, and the past verb has the sense of the future. «مَا» is in the sense of «الَّذِي» (a relative noun), and «مِنَ الْعِلْمِ» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun of the agent. «مَا» cannot be maṣdariyya (verbal-noun-forming) according to Sībawayh and the majority, because no pronoun refers back to maṣdariyya «مَا», and in «حَاجَّكَ» there is a pronoun of the fāʿil (agent), since there is nothing after it that could properly be the agent; and «الْعِلْم» cannot properly be the agent, because «مِنْ» is not added (as redundant) in the jawāb. [Translator's note: the argument concerns the verb «جَاءَكَ», whose agent pronoun must refer to «مَا»; «حَاجَّكَ» appears to be a slip for «جَاءَكَ». Likewise «فِي الْجَوَابِ» is probably a corruption of «فِي الْوَاجِبِ», i.e. "in affirmative speech", where Sībawayh does not allow redundant «مِنْ».] On the view of al-Akhfash it can be construed as maṣdariyya, with «مِنْ» redundant (zāʾida), the implied wording being: "after the coming of knowledge to you".
The original form of (تَعَالَوْا) is تَعَالَيُوا, because the original past tense is تَعَالَى, and its yāʾ is changed from wāw, since it is from al-ʿuluww ("height"). The wāw was changed to yāʾ because it fell in fourth position, then the yāʾ was changed to alif. When the wāw of the plural comes, (the alif) is dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, and the fatḥa remains to indicate it.
And (نَدْعُ) is the apodosis of an omitted condition, and (نَبْتَهِلْ) and (نَجْعَلْ) are conjoined to it. «نَجْعَل» is the one that takes two objects, i.e. "we make (something into something)", and the second object is «عَلَى الْكَاذِبِينَ».

ukberi-tibyan:62-62.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ هَذَا لَهُوَ الْقَصَصُ الْحَقُّ وَمَا مِنْ إِلَهٍ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ (٦٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَهُوَ الْقَصَصُ): a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) in the position of the khabar of «إِنَّ». (إِلَّا اللَّهُ): the khabar of «مِنْ إِلَهٍ», its implied form being «وَمَا إِلَهٌ إِلَّا اللَّهُ».

ukberi-tibyan:63-63.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ بِالْمُفْسِدِينَ (٦٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا): the form may be a past verb, and it may be an imperfect, its implied form being «يَتَوَلَّوْا»; al-Naḥḥās mentioned this, but it is weak, because the prefix of the imperfect is not dropped.

ukberi-tibyan:64-64.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قُلْ يَا أَهْلَ الْكِتَابِ تَعَالَوْا إِلَى كَلِمَةٍ سَوَاءٍ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَكُمْ أَلَّا نَعْبُدَ إِلَّا اللَّهَ وَلَا نُشْرِكَ بِهِ شَيْئًا وَلَا يَتَّخِذَ بَعْضُنَا بَعْضًا أَرْبَابًا مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ فَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا فَقُولُوا اشْهَدُوا بِأَنَّا مُسْلِمُونَ (٦٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (سَوَاءٍ): the majority read it in the genitive, and it is a naʿt (adjective) of «كَلِمَة». It is also read «سَوَاءً» in the accusative, as a maṣdar (verbal noun). And «كِلْمَةٍ» is read with kasra on the kāf and a sukūn on the lām, by lightening and transfer (of the vowel), like فَخْذ and كَبْد. (بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَكُمْ): an adverb of «سَوَاء», i.e. "so that the word may be equal between us". «سَوَاء» was not made feminine though it describes a feminine noun, because it is a maṣdar used as a description. As for His saying (أَلَّا نَعْبُدَ), there are two views on its position. The first: genitive, as a badal (substitute) of «سَوَاء» or of «كَلِمَة», its implied form being: "Come to abandoning the worship of other than Allah". The second: it is nominative, its implied form being: "it is that we worship none but Allah", and «أَنْ» is the maṣdariyya one. It is also said: the speech is complete at «سَوَاء», then a new sentence begins: «بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَكُمْ أَنْ لَا نَعْبُدَ», i.e. "between us and you is (the affirmation of) Oneness". On this view (أَلَّا نَعْبُدَ) may be a mubtadaʾ (subject) with the adverb as its khabar (predicate), the clause being an adjective of «كَلِمَة»; and «أَلَّا نَعْبُدَ» may also be made nominative by the adverb. (فَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا): it is a past verb, and it cannot be assumed to be «يَتَوَلَّوْا», because the meaning would be corrupted: His saying «فَقُولُوا اشْهَدُوا» is an address to the believers, while «يَتَوَلَّوْا» would refer to the polytheists, and in that case no apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) would remain in the speech. The implied wording is: "then say to them".

ukberi-tibyan:65-65.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا أَهْلَ الْكِتَابِ لِمَ تُحَاجُّونَ فِي إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَمَا أُنْزِلَتِ التَّوْرَاةُ وَالْإِنْجِيلُ إِلَّا مِنْ بَعْدِهِ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ (٦٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لِمَ تُحَاجُّونَ): the original is «لِمَا»; the alif was dropped for the reason we mentioned under His saying (فَلِمَ تَقْتُلُونَ). The lām is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «تُحَاجُّونَ». (إِلَّا مِنْ بَعْدِهِ): «مِنْ» is attached to «أُنْزِلَتْ», and the implied wording is: "after his death".

ukberi-tibyan:66-66.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (هَا أَنْتُمْ هَؤُلَاءِ حَاجَجْتُمْ فِيمَا لَكُمْ بِهِ عِلْمٌ فَلِمَ تُحَاجُّونَ فِيمَا لَيْسَ لَكُمْ بِهِ عِلْمٌ وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ وَأَنْتُمْ لَا تَعْلَمُونَ (٦٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (هَا أَنْتُمْ): «هَا» is for calling attention (tanbīh). It is also said: it is a substitute for the hamza of interrogation.
It is read with full pronunciation of the hamza and lengthening (madd), with softening of the hamza and lengthening, and with shortening (qaṣr) and the hamza. We have mentioned the iʿrāb of this phrase under His saying (ثُمَّ أَنْتُمْ هَؤُلَاءِ تَقْتُلُونَ). (فِيمَا): «مَا» is in the sense of «الَّذِي» (a relative noun), or an indefinite qualified noun. And (عِلْمٌ) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), «لَكُمْ» its khabar (predicate), and «بِهِ» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), because it was originally an adjective of «عِلْم» that was put before it. The bāʾ cannot be attached to «عِلْم», since that would put part of the ṣila before the governing (maṣdar) it belongs to. [Translator's note: the source says «تَقْدِيمُ الصِّلَةِ عَلَى الْمَوْصُولِ» ("putting the ṣila before the mawṣūl"); a maṣdar is treated like a relative with its complement as its "ṣila".] If you attach it to something omitted that the maṣdar explains, it is permissible; this is what is called tabyīn ("clarification").

ukberi-tibyan:68-68.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ أَوْلَى النَّاسِ بِإِبْرَاهِيمَ لَلَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوهُ وَهَذَا النَّبِيُّ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَاللَّهُ وَلِيُّ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ (٦٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بِإِبْرَاهِيمَ): the bāʾ is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «أَوْلَى», and the khabar (predicate) of «إِنَّ» is «لَلَّذِينِ اتَّبَعُوهُ». «أَوْلَى» is the afʿal (elative) form from وَلِيَ يَلِي, and its alif is changed from yāʾ, because its first radical is wāw, so its final radical cannot be wāw, since there is no word in the language whose first and final radicals are both wāw except «وَاو» (the name of the letter). (وَهَذَا النَّبِيُّ): conjoined to the khabar of «إِنَّ».
It is also read «النَّبِيَّ» in the accusative, i.e. "and they followed this Prophet".

ukberi-tibyan:72-72.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَقَالَتْ طَائِفَةٌ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ آمِنُوا بِالَّذِي أُنْزِلَ عَلَى الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَجْهَ النَّهَارِ وَاكْفُرُوا آخِرَهُ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ (٧٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَجْهَ النَّهَارِ): «وَجْهَ» is an adverb (ẓarf) of «آمِنُوا», as shown by His saying «وَاكْفُرُوا آخِرَهُ».
It may also be an adverb of «أُنْزِلَ».

ukberi-tibyan:73-73.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَا تُؤْمِنُوا إِلَّا لِمَنْ تَبِعَ دِينَكُمْ قُلْ إِنَّ الْهُدَى هُدَى اللَّهِ أَنْ يُؤْتَى أَحَدٌ مِثْلَ مَا أُوتِيتُمْ أَوْ يُحَاجُّوكُمْ عِنْدَ رَبِّكُمْ قُلْ إِنَّ الْفَضْلَ بِيَدِ اللَّهِ يُؤْتِيهِ مَنْ يَشَاءُ وَاللَّهُ وَاسِعٌ عَلِيمٌ (٧٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِلَّا لِمَنْ تَبِعَ): there are two views on it. The first: it is an exception from what precedes it, the implied wording being: "and do not acknowledge (anything) except to one who follows"; on this view the lām is not redundant.
It may also be redundant (zāʾida), and (the phrase) is then construed according to the meaning, i.e. "reject everyone except one who follows".
The second: that the intended order is postponement, the implied wording being: "and do not believe that anyone will be given the like of what you were given, except one who follows your religion". On this view the lām is redundant, and «مَنْ» is in the position of the accusative as an exception from «أَحَد». As for His saying (قُلْ إِنَّ الْهُدَى), it is parenthetical between the two parts of the speech, because it is emphatic (musaddad). [Translator's note: the source has «مُشَدَّدٌ»; the sense is probably «مُسَدِّدٌ» / «مُشَدِّدٌ», i.e. that the parenthesis reinforces the meaning.] This view is far-fetched, because it involves putting the excepted before the thing excepted from and before what governs it, and putting part of the ṣila of «أَنْ» before it. On this view, there are three views on the position of «أَنْ يُؤْتَى». The first: genitive, its implied form being: "and do not believe in (بِأَنْ) anyone being given". The second: that it is accusative on the assumption that the preposition has been dropped. The third: that it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), its implied form being: "and do not believe except one who follows your religion, for fear that anyone be given". It is also said: «أَنْ يُؤْتَى» is connected to His saying «قُلْ إِنَّ الْهُدَى هُدَى اللَّهِ», the implied wording being «أَنْ لَا يُؤْتَى», i.e. "it is that no one is given", so it is in the position of the nominative. (أَوْ يُحَاجُّوكُمْ): conjoined to «يُؤْتَى». The pronoun is plural for «أَحَد», because «أَحَد» carries the sense of a plural, as He said (لَا نُفَرِّقُ بَيْنَ أَحَدٍ مِنْهُمْ). And «أَنْ يُؤْتَى» is read as a new sentence (istiʾnāf), its position being nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), the implied wording being: "that anyone be given the like of what you were given — is it possible, or is it to be believed?" [Translator's note: this reading is the interrogative «آنْ يُؤْتَى» (Ibn Kathīr); the printed text does not show the interrogative madda.] It may also be in the position of the accusative, governed by an omitted verb, its implied form being: "do you believe that anyone be given?" or "do you spread (the report)?". And «أَنْ يُؤْتَى» is read as an irregular (shādhdh) reading with the agent named (active voice), «أَحَد» being its agent and the object omitted, i.e. «أَنْ يُؤْتِيَ أَحَدٌ أَحَدًا» ("that anyone give anyone"). [Translator's note: the printed text again shows «يُؤْتَى»; the active form «يُؤْتِيَ» is meant.]
(يُؤْتِيهِ مَنْ يَشَاءُ): it may be a new sentence; or the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "He gives it"; or a second khabar.

ukberi-tibyan:7-7.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (هُوَ الَّذِي أَنْزَلَ عَلَيْكَ الْكِتَابَ مِنْهُ آيَاتٌ مُحْكَمَاتٌ هُنَّ أُمُّ الْكِتَابِ وَأُخَرُ مُتَشَابِهَاتٌ فَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ زَيْغٌ فَيَتَّبِعُونَ مَا تَشَابَهَ مِنْهُ ابْتِغَاءَ الْفِتْنَةِ وَابْتِغَاءَ تَأْوِيلِهِ وَمَا يَعْلَمُ تَأْوِيلَهُ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَالرَّاسِخُونَ فِي الْعِلْمِ يَقُولُونَ آمَنَّا بِهِ كُلٌّ مِنْ عِنْدِ رَبِّنَا وَمَا يَذَّكَّرُ إِلَّا أُولُو الْأَلْبَابِ (٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْهُ آيَاتٌ): the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الكتاب.
You may make آيات nominative by the adverbial phrase (ẓarf), because it is supported [by what precedes it]; and you may make it nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), the adverbial phrase being its khabar (predicate).
(هُنَّ أُمُّ الْكِتَابِ): in the position of the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of آيات. (أُمُّ) was made singular although it is a khabar about a plural only because the meaning is that all the verses are like a single verse, so it was made singular according to the meaning.
It may also be that the singular was put in place of the plural, as we mentioned at His saying (وَعَلَى سَمْعِهِمْ). And the meaning may be "each one of them is the mother of the Book", as Allah the Exalted said: (فَاجْلِدُوهُمْ ثَمَانِينَ), i.e. "flog each one of them".
(وَأُخَرُ): conjoined (maʿṭūf) to آيات.
(مُتَشَابِهَاتٌ): a naʿt of أخر.
If it is said: the singular of متشابهات is متشابهة, and the singular of أخر is أخرى, and the singular here cannot validly be described by this singular — one does not say أخرى متشابهة, unless parts of the single [verse] resemble one another, and that is not the meaning; the meaning is only that every verse resembles another verse. So how is it valid to describe this plural with this plural, when its singular is not described with its singular?
It is said: resemblance only exists between two or more. When resembling things come together, each of them resembles the other. So since resemblance is only valid in the state of being together, the plural was described with the plural, because each one of its individual members resembles the rest; as for the single one, this meaning is not valid in it.
A parallel is His saying, Exalted is He: (فَوَجَدَ فِيهَا رَجُلَيْنِ يَقْتَتِلَانِ): He put the pronoun in the dual, even though one does not say of a single person يقتتل ("fights [with another]"). (مَا تَشَابَهَ مِنْهُ): ما means الذي, and منه is a ḥāl from the pronoun of the fāʿil (agent); the hāʾ refers to الكتاب. (ابْتِغَاءَ): a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose). التأويل is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of أوّل يؤوّل, and its origin is from آل يؤول, when something reaches its end.
(الرَّاسِخُونَ): conjoined to the name of Allah, the meaning being that they also know its interpretation.
And (يَقُولُونَ) is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl.
It has been said that الراسخون is a mubtadaʾ and يقولون the khabar.
The meaning [on this view] is that those firmly grounded do not know its interpretation, but rather believe in it.
(كُلٌّ): a mubtadaʾ, i.e. "all of it" or "each of it".
And (مِنْ عِنْدِ) is the khabar. The position of «آمنا» and كل من عند ربنا is accusative by يقولون.

ukberi-tibyan:8-8.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (رَبَّنَا لَا تُزِغْ قُلُوبَنَا بَعْدَ إِذْ هَدَيْتَنَا وَهَبْ لَنَا مِنْ لَدُنْكَ رَحْمَةً إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْوَهَّابُ (٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَا تُزِغْ قُلُوبَنَا): the majority read it with ḍamma on the tāʾ and القلوب in the accusative; one says زاغ القلب ("the heart swerved") and أزاغه الله ("Allah made it swerve"). It has been read with fatḥa on the tāʾ and القلوب in the nominative, attributing the verb to them.
(إِذْ هَدَيْتَنَا): it is not an adverb (ẓarf), because بعد has been put in construct with it.
(مِنْ لَدُنْكَ): لدن is indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, and it is [still indeclinable while] in construct, because the cause of its indeclinability is present after the construct, and the ruling follows the cause. That cause is that لدن means «عند» in the sense of being in contact with the thing. For عند, when it is mentioned, is not specific to proximity, whereas لدن is a specific عند. So a meaning has come to be in it that the adverb does not indicate; rather it is of the kind of thing that a particle conveys, so it became as though it included the particle that ought to have been set up as an indicator of nearness. Similar to it are ثَمَّ and هنا, because they were made indeclinable when they included the particle of pointing.
There are several dialectal forms of it, of which this is one: fatḥa on the lām, ḍamma on the dāl and sukūn on the nūn.
The second: likewise, except that the dāl is quiescent; that is a lightening, as عضد is lightened.
The third: with ḍamma on the lām and sukūn on the dāl.
The fourth: لدى.
The fifth: لَدُ, with fatḥa on the lām and ḍamma on the dāl, without nūn.
The sixth: with fatḥa on the lām and sukūn on the dāl, with nothing after the dāl.

ukberi-tibyan:9-9.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (رَبَّنَا إِنَّكَ جَامِعُ النَّاسِ لِيَوْمٍ لَا رَيْبَ فِيهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُخْلِفُ الْمِيعَادَ (٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (جَامِعُ النَّاسِ): the construct (iḍāfa) is not pure (ghayr maḥḍa), because it refers to the future; the implied form is جامعٌ الناسَ. (لِيَوْمٍ): its implied form is "for the presentation of a day" or "the reckoning of a day".
It has been said that the lām means في, i.e. "on a day". The hāʾ in «فيه» refers to the day; or, if you wish, to the gathering; or, if you wish, to the reckoning or the presentation. (لَا رَيْبَ) is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of يوم. (إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُخْلِفُ): He repeated the mention of Allah overtly for magnification; had He said إنك لا تخلف, it would have been sound. It may also be resumptive, and not reported from those who spoke before.
(الْمِيعَادَ): on the pattern mifʿāl, from الوعد; its wāw was changed into yāʾ because it is quiescent and what precedes it has kasra.

ukberi-tibyan:10-10.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَنْ تُغْنِيَ عَنْهُمْ أَمْوَالُهُمْ وَلَا أَوْلَادُهُمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ شَيْئًا وَأُولَئِكَ هُمْ وَقُودُ النَّارِ (١٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَنْ تُغْنِيَ): the majority read it with tāʾ because the fāʿil (agent) is feminine; and it is read with yāʾ because the femininity of the fāʿil is not real, and also because they have been separated.
(مِنَ اللَّهِ): in the position of the accusative, because the implied form is "from the punishment of Allah"; the meaning is: wealth will not ward off from them the punishment of Allah. (شَيْئًا) on this view is in the position of the maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being "any availing".
And شيئًا may be a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) according to the meaning, because the meaning of تغني عنهم is "ward off"; then من الله is originally a naʿt (adjective) of شيء which was placed first and so became a ḥāl (circumstantial), the implied form being: "wealth will not ward off from them anything of the punishment of Allah".
الوَقود with fatḥa is firewood, and with ḍamma it is burning; it has also been said that they are two dialectal forms with one meaning.

ukberi-tibyan:166-167.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا أَصَابَكُمْ يَوْمَ الْتَقَى الْجَمْعَانِ فَبِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ وَلِيَعْلَمَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ (١٦٦) وَلِيَعْلَمَ الَّذِينَ نَافَقُوا وَقِيلَ لَهُمْ تَعَالَوْا قَاتِلُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ أَوِ ادْفَعُوا قَالُوا لَوْ نَعْلَمُ قِتَالًا لَاتَّبَعْنَاكُمْ هُمْ لِلْكُفْرِ يَوْمَئِذٍ أَقْرَبُ مِنْهُمْ لِلْإِيمَانِ يَقُولُونَ بِأَفْواهِهِمْ مَا لَيْسَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا يَكْتُمُونَ (١٦٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَمَا أَصَابَكُمْ): مَا has the sense of الَّذِي ("that which"), and it is a mubtadaʾ (subject); the khabar (predicate) is «فَبِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ», i.e. "is occurring by the permission of Allah". (وَلِيَعْلَمَ): the lām is attached (mutaʿalliq) to something omitted, i.e. "and so that Allah might know, this befell you". It may also be conjoined to the meaning of فَبِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ, its implied form being: "by the permission of Allah, and in order that Allah might know".
(تَعَالَوْا قَاتِلُوا): the conjunction was not brought only because He wished to make each of the two clauses intended in itself. It may also be said that what is intended is the command to fight, and تَعَالَوْا mentions something which, had it been left unsaid, there would still have been an indication of it in the speech. It is also said: the second imperative is a ḥāl (circumstantial).
(هُمْ لِلْكُفْرِ): the lām in His saying «لِلْكُفْرِ» and «لِلْإِيمَانِ» is attached to أَقْرَبُ. It is permissible for أَقْرَبُ to govern both of them because they resemble the adverb (ẓarf), just as أَطْيَبُ governs the two implied adverbs in their saying هَذَا بُسْرًا أَطْيَبُ مِنْهُ رُطَبًا ("this, as unripe dates, is better than it as ripe dates"). This is because the pattern afʿal indicates two meanings, the basic sense of the verb and its increase, so it governs each of the two by a meaning other than the other. Its implied sense is therefore: "their nearness to disbelief exceeds their nearness to faith". The lām here has its usual meaning; it is also said that it has the sense of إِلَى ("to"). (يَقُولُونَ): resumptive; it may also be a ḥāl from the pronoun in أَقْرَبُ, i.e. "they drew near to disbelief, saying".

ukberi-tibyan:168-168.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الَّذِينَ قَالُوا لِإِخْوَانِهِمْ وَقَعَدُوا لَوْ أَطَاعُونَا مَا قُتِلُوا قُلْ فَادْرَءُوا عَنْ أَنْفُسِكُمُ الْمَوْتَ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ (١٦٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الَّذِينَ قَالُوا): it may be in the position of the nominative by an implied أَعْنِي ("I mean") [Translator's note: so in the text; an implied أَعْنِي normally entails the accusative], or an adjective of الَّذِينَ نَافَقُوا, or a badal (substitute) from it; and in the position of the genitive as a badal from the genitive [pronoun] in أَفْوَاهِهِمْ or قُلُوبِهِمْ. It may also be a mubtadaʾ (subject) with the khabar (predicate) «قُلْ فَادْرَءُوا», the implied form being: "say to them". (وَقَعَدُوا): it may be conjoined to the ṣila (relative clause), interposed between قَالُوا and what it governs, which is «لَوْ أَطَاعُونَا»; or it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial), with قَدْ intended.

ukberi-tibyan:169-169.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَا تَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ قُتِلُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ أَمْوَاتًا بَلْ أَحْيَاءٌ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ يُرْزَقُونَ (١٦٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بَلْ أَحْيَاءٌ): i.e. "rather, they are alive". It is also read in the accusative (أَحْيَاءً), conjoined to (أَمْوَاتًا), as you say: ظَنَنْتُ زَيْدًا قَائِمًا بَلْ قَاعِدًا ("I thought Zayd standing, rather sitting"). It is also said that the verb is implied, its implied form being: "rather, reckon them alive", and that was omitted because something indicating it came before. (عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ): an adjective of أَحْيَاءٌ. It may be an adverb (ẓarf) for أَحْيَاءٌ, because the meaning is "they live with Allah". It may be an adverb for «يُرْزَقُونَ», with يُرْزَقُونَ an adjective of أَحْيَاءٌ. It [يُرْزَقُونَ] may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in أَحْيَاءٌ, i.e. "they live, being provided for"; and it may be a ḥāl from the pronoun in the adverb if you make it an adjective.

ukberi-tibyan:170-170.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَرِحِينَ بِمَا آتَاهُمُ اللَّهُ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ وَيَسْتَبْشِرُونَ بِالَّذِينَ لَمْ يَلْحَقُوا بِهِمْ مِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ أَلَّا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ (١٧٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَرِحِينَ): it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in يُرْزَقُونَ. It may be an adjective of أَحْيَاءٌ when that is read in the accusative. It may be accusative by way of praise (ʿalā al-madḥ). It may also be [a ḥāl] from the pronoun in أَحْيَاءٌ, or from the pronoun in the adverb (ẓarf). (مِنْ فَضْلِهِ): a ḥāl from the omitted returning pronoun (al-ʿāʾid) in the adverb [Translator's note: so in the text («فِي الظَّرْفِ»); the omitted returning pronoun is in the ṣila of مَا], its implied form being: "with what He gave them, being from His bounty" (بِمَا آتَاهُمُوهُ كَائِنًا مِنْ فَضْلِهِ).
(وَيَسْتَبْشِرُونَ): conjoined to فَرِحِينَ, because the active participle here resembles the imperfect verb. The implied form may also be: "and they rejoice", so that the clause is a ḥāl from the pronoun in فَرِحِينَ, or from the object pronoun in آتَاهُمْ. (مِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ): attached (mutaʿalliq) to يَلْحَقُوا; it may also be a ḥāl, its implied form being: "staying behind them". (أَلَّا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ): i.e. "that there is no fear upon them" (بِأَنْ لَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ); so أَنْ is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), and the position of the clause is a badal (substitute) from الَّذِينَ, a badal of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl), i.e. "they rejoice at the safety of those who have not joined them". The implied form may also be: "because there is no fear upon them", so it would be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose).

ukberi-tibyan:171-172.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَسْتَبْشِرُونَ بِنِعْمَةٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَفَضْلٍ وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُضِيعُ أَجْرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ (١٧١) الَّذِينَ اسْتَجَابُوا لِلَّهِ وَالرَّسُولِ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا أَصَابَهُمُ الْقَرْحُ لِلَّذِينَ أَحْسَنُوا مِنْهُمْ وَاتَّقَوْا أَجْرٌ عَظِيمٌ (١٧٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَيَسْتَبْشِرُونَ): it is resumptive, repeated for emphasis. (وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ): with fatḥa, conjoined to بِنِعْمَةٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ, i.e. "and at [the fact] that Allah…"; and with kasra (وَإِنَّ) as a new, resumptive sentence.
His saying, Exalted is He: (الَّذِينَ اسْتَجَابُوا): in the position of the genitive as an adjective of الْمُؤْمِنِينَ; or of the accusative by an implied أَعْنِي ("I mean"); or of the nominative by an implied «هُمْ» ("they are"); or it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is «لِلَّذِينَ أَحْسَنُوا مِنْهُمْ وَاتَّقَوْا», and مِنْهُمْ is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in أَحْسَنُوا.

ukberi-tibyan:173-173.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الَّذِينَ قَالَ لَهُمُ النَّاسُ إِنَّ النَّاسَ قَدْ جَمَعُوا لَكُمْ فَاخْشَوْهُمْ فَزَادَهُمْ إِيمَانًا وَقَالُوا حَسْبُنَا اللَّهُ وَنِعْمَ الْوَكِيلُ (١٧٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الَّذِينَ قَالَ لَهُمُ النَّاسُ): a badal (substitute) from الَّذِينَ اسْتَجَابُوا, or an adjective.
(فَزَادَهُمْ إِيمَانًا): the fāʿil (agent) is an implied pronoun, its implied form being: "the saying increased them". (حَسْبُنَا اللَّهُ): a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). حَسْبُ is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of an active participle; its implied form is: "so our sufficer is Allah", i.e. "the one who suffices us" (كَافِينَا). One says أَحْسَبَنِي الشَّيْءُ, i.e. "the thing sufficed me".

ukberi-tibyan:174-174.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَانْقَلَبُوا بِنِعْمَةٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَفَضْلٍ لَمْ يَمْسَسْهُمْ سُوءٌ وَاتَّبَعُوا رِضْوَانَ اللَّهِ وَاللَّهُ ذُو فَضْلٍ عَظِيمٍ (١٧٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بِنِعْمَةٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ): in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial).
It may also be a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (لَمْ يَمْسَسْهُمْ): also a ḥāl, from the pronoun in انْقَلَبُوا. It may also be that what governs it is بِنِعْمَةٍ, the one whose state is described (ṣāḥib al-ḥāl) being the pronoun in the ḥāl; its implied sense is: "so they returned blessed, free of any harm". (وَاتَّبَعُوا): conjoined to انْقَلَبُوا; it may also be a ḥāl, i.e. "having followed" (وَقَدِ اتَّبَعُوا).

ukberi-tibyan:175-175.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّمَا ذَلِكُمُ الشَّيْطَانُ يُخَوِّفُ أَوْلِيَاءَهُ فَلَا تَخَافُوهُمْ وَخَافُونِ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ (١٧٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (ذَلِكُمُ): a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «الشَّيْطَانُ» is its khabar (predicate).
(يُخَوِّفُ): it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الشَّيْطَانُ, the governing element being the [sense of] pointing. It may also be that الشَّيْطَانُ is a badal (substitute) or an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition), and يُخَوِّفُ the khabar. The implied form is: "he frightens you by means of his allies" (يُخَوِّفُكُمْ بِأَوْلِيَائِهِ). It was read, as an irregular (shādhdh) reading, «يُخَوِّفُكُمْ أَوْلِيَاؤُهُ». It is also said that there is no omission in it, and the meaning is: he frightens whoever follows him; as for the one who puts his trust in Allah, he does not fear him. (فَلَا تَخَافُوهُمْ): the pronoun was made plural only because الشَّيْطَانُ is generic; the pronoun may also refer to the allies.

ukberi-tibyan:176-176.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَا يَحْزُنْكَ الَّذِينَ يُسَارِعُونَ فِي الْكُفْرِ إِنَّهُمْ لَنْ يَضُرُّوا اللَّهَ شَيْئًا يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ أَلَّا يَجْعَلَ لَهُمْ حَظًّا فِي الْآخِرَةِ وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ (١٧٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَا يَحْزُنْكَ): the majority read it with fatḥa on the yāʾ and ḍamma on the zāy, and the past tense is حَزِنَهُ [Translator's note: so vowelled in the text; the transitive past tense is usually vowelled حَزَنَهُ, as below].
It is also read with ḍamma on the yāʾ and kasra on the zāy (يُحْزِنْكَ), the past tense being أَحْزَنَ, and that is a rare dialectal form. It is also said: حَزِنَ means sorrow came about in him; حَزَنَتْهُ means "it caused sorrow in him"; and أَحْزَنَتْهُ means "it exposed him to sorrow". (يُسَارِعُونَ): it is read with imāla (inclination of the vowel towards i) and with tafkhīm (full pronunciation); and it is read يُسْرِعُونَ without alif, from أَسْرَعَ. (شَيْئًا): in the position of the maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "any harm".

ukberi-tibyan:11-11.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (كَدَأْبِ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ وَالَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ كَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِنَا فَأَخَذَهُمُ اللَّهُ بِذُنُوبِهِمْ وَاللَّهُ شَدِيدُ الْعِقَابِ (١١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (كَدَأْبِ): the kāf is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), and there are several views on that omitted [element].
The first: its implied form is "they disbelieved with a disbelief like the habit of the family of Pharaoh". The verb supplied here is not the one in the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين, because that verb's connection to the kāf has been cut off, since الذين has received its full khabar (predicate); rather it is [governed] by a verb indicated by «كفروا», which is the ṣila.
The second: its implied form is "they were punished with a punishment like the habit of the family of Pharaoh", indicated by أولئك هم وقود النار.
The third: its implied form is "their benefiting from wealth and children came to nothing, like the habit of the family of Pharaoh".
The fourth: its implied form is "they denied with a denial like the habit of the family of Pharaoh"; on this view the pronoun in كذبوا refers to them [the disbelievers addressed], and in that is a warning to them, because of their knowledge of what befell the family of Pharaoh, and of His seizing of the family of Pharaoh.
(وَالَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ) on this view is in the position of the genitive, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to آل فرعون.
It has been said that the kāf is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being: "their habit in that is like the habit of the family of Pharaoh". On this view two views are possible regarding (وَالَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ). The first: it is also genitive by conjunction, and كذبوا is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), with «قد» intended along with it; or it may be resumptive, with no position, mentioned to explain their state.
The other view: that the speech is complete at فرعون, and الذين من قبلهم is a mubtadaʾ with «كذبوا» its khabar. (شَدِيدُ الْعِقَابِ): its implied form is "severe is His punishment", so the construct is not pure (ghayr maḥḍa).
It has been said that شديد here means مُشَدِّد ("one who makes severe"); on this view it is the construct of an active participle with its object. The faʿīl pattern has come with the meaning of mufʿil and mufʿal.

ukberi-tibyan:12-12.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قُلْ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا سَتُغْلَبُونَ وَتُحْشَرُونَ إِلَى جَهَنَّمَ وَبِئْسَ الْمِهَادُ (١٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (سَتُغْلَبُونَ وَتُحْشَرُونَ): both are read with tāʾ, as second-person address, i.e. "confront them with that"; and with yāʾ, its implied form being: "inform them of their states, for they will be overcome and gathered".
(وَبِئْسَ الْمِهَادُ): i.e. Hell; the noun specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) has been omitted.

ukberi-tibyan:13-13.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَدْ كَانَ لَكُمْ آيَةٌ فِي فِئَتَيْنِ الْتَقَتَا فِئَةٌ تُقَاتِلُ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَأُخْرَى كَافِرَةٌ يَرَوْنَهُمْ مِثْلَيْهِمْ رَأْيَ الْعَيْنِ وَاللَّهُ يُؤَيِّدُ بِنَصْرِهِ مَنْ يَشَاءُ إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَعِبْرَةً لِأُولِي الْأَبْصَارِ (١٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (قَدْ كَانَ لَكُمْ آيَةٌ): آية is the noun of كان. [The verb] was not made feminine because the femininity is not real, because there is a separation, and because آية and دليل ("proof") have the same meaning. There are two views on the khabar (predicate). The first: «لكم», with «فئتين» a naʿt (adjective) of آية.
The second: that the khabar is «في فئتين», and لكم is attached (mutaʿalliq) to كان.
And لكم may be in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), on the basis that it is [originally] a naʿt of آية, i.e. "a sign being for you", so it is attached to an omitted [word].
(الْتَقَتَا) is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt of فئتين. (فِئَةٌ) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "one of them is a group".
(وَأُخْرَى): a naʿt of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being: "and another group" [is] «كافرة».
If it is said: if you supplied إحداهما as the mubtadaʾ in the first, analogy would require it to be والأخرى, i.e. "and the other is a disbelieving group".
It is said: since it is known that the division here is of the very dual mentioned before, definiteness and indefiniteness were the same.
It is read, among the irregular (shādhdh) readings, «فئةٍ تقاتل، وأخرى كافرةٍ» in the genitive in both, on the basis that it is a badal (substitute) from فئتين.
It is also read in the accusative in both, on the basis of being a ḥāl from the pronoun in التقتا, its implied form being: "they met, a believing one and a disbelieving one"; فئة and أخرى on this view are for the ḥāl.
It has been said that فئة and what is conjoined to it, on the reading of those who use the nominative, are a badal from the pronoun in التقتا.
(تَرَوْنَهُمْ) [Translator's note: so in the text, with tāʾ; the Quranic wording quoted above is يَرَوْنَهُمْ]: it is read with an open tāʾ, and it is from seeing with the eye.
(مِثْلَيْهِمْ) is a ḥāl, and (رَأْيَ الْعَيْنِ) is an emphatic maṣdar (verbal noun).
It is read, among the irregular readings, «تُرَوْنهم» with ḍamma on the tāʾ, in the passive, and it is from أورى [Translator's note: so in the text; presumably أَرَى is meant] when someone else shows it to him, as in your saying أريتُك هذا الثوب ("I showed you this garment"). And it is read in the well-known [reading] with yāʾ, in the third person.
As for the reading with tāʾ, it is because the beginning of the verse is an address; the position of the clause on this view may be a naʿt — an adjective — of فئتين, because there is in it a pronoun referring back to them; and it may be a ḥāl from the kāf in لكم.
As for the reading with yāʾ, it may have the meaning of the tāʾ, except that He turned from address to the third person, the meaning being the same; something similar has been mentioned.
And it may be resumptive. It is not permissible, on any of the views, for it to be from seeing with the heart, for two reasons. The first: His saying رأي العين ("seeing of the eye").
The second: that seeing with the heart is knowledge, and it is impossible to know a thing as being two things.
(يُؤَيِّدُ): it is read with hamza, according to the origin, and with lightening. Lightening the hamza here means making it a pure wāw, because of the ḍamma before it; it is not valid to make it "between-between" (bayna bayna), because of its closeness to the alif.
And what precedes an alif can only have fatḥa; for that reason an initial hamza is not made "between-between", owing to the impossibility of beginning with an alif.

ukberi-tibyan:14-14.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (زُيِّنَ لِلنَّاسِ حُبُّ الشَّهَوَاتِ مِنَ النِّسَاءِ وَالْبَنِينَ وَالْقَنَاطِيرِ الْمُقَنْطَرَةِ مِنَ الذَّهَبِ وَالْفِضَّةِ وَالْخَيْلِ الْمُسَوَّمَةِ وَالْأَنْعَامِ وَالْحَرْثِ ذَلِكَ مَتَاعُ الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا وَاللَّهُ عِنْدَهُ حُسْنُ الْمَآبِ (١٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (زُيِّنَ): the majority read it with ḍamma on the zāy and «حبّ» in the nominative.
It is read with fatḥa and حبّ in the accusative, its implied form being: "Satan made [it] attractive to people", as came explicitly in the other verse. The hāʾ in «الشهوات» was given a vowel because it is a noun, not an adjective.
(مِنَ النِّسَاءِ) is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الشهوات. The nūn in القنطار is radical, and its pattern is fiʿlāl, like حِملاق. It has been said that it is extra, and its derivation is from قطر يقطر, when it flows; gold and silver are likened to water in abundance and speed of changing hands.
And {مِنَ الذَّهَبِ} is in the position of a ḥāl from المقنطرة.
(وَالْخَيْلِ): conjoined (maʿṭūf) to النساء, not to الذهب and الفضة, because they [horses] are not called a qinṭār. The singular of الخيل is خائل, and it is derived from الخُيَلاء ("pride"), like طير and طائر.
Some said it has no singular from its own wording; rather it is a collective noun (ism jamʿ), the singular being فرس, and its form is the form of a maṣdar (verbal noun).
And it may be lightened from خَيِّل. «الحرث» was not made plural because it is a maṣdar with the meaning of the passive participle. Most people hold that it is not permissible to assimilate the thāʾ into the dhāl here, lest two quiescent letters be combined, because the rāʾ is quiescent; as for assimilation in His saying «يَلْهَثْ ذَلِكَ», it is permissible.
(الْمَآبِ): on the pattern mafʿal, from آب يؤوب; the origin is مَأْوَب. Since the wāw was vowelled and what preceded it had fatḥa in the origin, which is آب, it was changed into alif.

ukberi-tibyan:75-75.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ مَنْ إِنْ تَأْمَنْهُ بِقِنْطَارٍ يُؤَدِّهِ إِلَيْكَ وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ إِنْ تَأْمَنْهُ بِدِينَارٍ لَا يُؤَدِّهِ إِلَيْكَ إِلَّا مَا دُمْتَ عَلَيْهِ قَائِمًا ذَلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ قَالُوا لَيْسَ عَلَيْنَا فِي الْأُمِّيِّينَ سَبِيلٌ وَيَقُولُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ الْكَذِبَ وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ (٧٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَنْ إِنْ تَأْمَنْهُ): «مَنْ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ» its khabar (predicate); the condition and its apodosis are a naʿt (adjective) of «مَنْ», because it is indefinite. Just as a conditional sentence occurs as a khabar, it occurs as a ṣila (relative clause), an adjective and a ḥāl (circumstantial). Abū al-Ashhab al-ʿUṭāridī read «تِأْمَنْهُ» with kasra on the imperfect prefix. And (بِقِنْطَارٍ): the bāʾ is in the sense of «فِي», i.e. "in (the safekeeping of) a qinṭār"; it is also said that the bāʾ is in the sense of «عَلَى». (يُؤَدِّهِ): there are five readings of it. The first: kasra on the hāʾ, joined with a yāʾ in pronunciation; we have mentioned the reason for this at the beginning of the book. The second: kasra on the hāʾ without a yāʾ, the kasra sufficing for the yāʾ because it indicates it, and because the principle is that nothing is added to the hāʾ, as with the other pronouns. The third: a sukūn on the hāʾ; this is because continuous speech was treated like the pause, and it is weak, since the hāʾ of the pronoun is entitled to a vowel, and only the hāʾ of pausing (hāʾ al-sakt) takes sukūn. The fourth: ḍamma on the hāʾ, joined with a wāw in pronunciation, to make the hāʾ with ḍamma clear by means of the wāw, since it is of the same kind as the ḍamma, just as the hāʾ with kasra is made clear by the yāʾ. The fifth: ḍamma on the hāʾ without a wāw, because the ḍamma indicates it and because it is the original. It is permissible to pronounce the hamza fully or to change it to wāw because of the ḍamma before it. (إِلَّا مَا دُمْتَ): «مَا» is in the position of the accusative as an adverb (ẓarf), i.e. "except for the duration of your continuing".
It may also be a ḥāl, because «مَا» is maṣdariyya (verbal-noun-forming) and a maṣdar (verbal noun) may occur as a ḥāl; the implied wording is "except in the state of your staying close to him". The majority read with ḍamma on the dāl (دُمْتَ); its past is دَامَ يَدُومُ, like قَالَ يَقُولُ. It is also read with kasra on the dāl (دِمْتَ), whose past is «دِمْتَ تَدَامُ», like «خِفْتَ تَخَافُ»; it is a dialectal form. (ذَلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ): i.e. "that is deserved because they…". (فِي الْأُمِّيِّينَ): an adjective of «سَبِيلٌ» that was put before it and so became a ḥāl. It may also be an adverb of the notion of settledness (al-istiqrār) in «عَلَيْنَا». Some held that «لَيْسَ» governs (words) in the ḥāl (i.e. adverbial elements).
On this view it may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to it, with «سَبِيلٌ» the noun of «لَيْسَ» and «عَلَيْنَا» the khabar. «سَبِيلٌ» may also be made nominative by «عَلَيْنَا», in which case «لَيْسَ» contains the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn). (وَيَقُولُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ): «عَلَى» may be attached to «يَقُولُونَ», because it has the sense of «يَفْتَرُونَ» ("they fabricate"). It may also be a ḥāl of «الْكَذِبَ» put before it. It cannot be attached to «الْكَذِبَ», because the ṣila does not precede the mawṣūl (i.e. the complement of a maṣdar does not precede it); but this is permissible by way of tabyīn ("clarification"). (وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ): a clause in the position of a ḥāl.

ukberi-tibyan:76-76.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (بَلَى مَنْ أَوْفَى بِعَهْدِهِ وَاتَّقَى فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الْمُتَّقِينَ (٧٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بَلَى): there is an omission in the wording, its implied form being: "Yes indeed, there is a way (of blame) against them". Then He began anew, saying «مَنْ أَوْفَى», which is a condition, and «فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ» is its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). The meaning is "then Allah loves them", so the overt noun was put in the place of the pronoun.

ukberi-tibyan:78-78.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِنَّ مِنْهُمْ لَفَرِيقًا يَلْوُونَ أَلْسِنَتَهُمْ بِالْكِتَابِ لتحسبوه من الْكتاب وَمَا هُوَ من الْكتاب (٧٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يَلْوُونَ): it is in the position of the accusative as an adjective of «فَرِيق»; it is plural according to the meaning, and were it singular, that would be permissible according to the form. The majority read with a sukūn on the lām and two wāws after it. It is also read with fatḥa on the lām, a doubled wāw and ḍamma on the yāʾ (يُلَوُّونَ), expressing intensity. It is also read with ḍamma on the lām and a single quiescent wāw (يَلُونَ); the original is «يَلْوُونَ», as in the reading of the majority, except that the wāw was given a hamza because of its ḍamma, and then its vowel was transferred to the lām. «الْأَلْسِنَة» is the plural of «لِسَان»; this is according to the dialect of those who treat «اللِّسَان» as masculine; as for those who treat it as feminine, they make its plural «أَلْسُن».
And (بِالْكِتَابِ) is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «الْأَلْسِنَة», i.e. "involved with the Book" or "uttering the Book".
And (مِنَ الْكِتَابِ) is the second object of «حَسِبَ».

ukberi-tibyan:79-79.t:
