Allah the Exalted said: (مَا كَانَ لِبَشَرٍ أَنْ يُؤْتِيَهُ اللَّهُ الْكِتَابَ وَالْحُكْمَ وَالنُّبُوَّةَ ثُمَّ يَقُولَ لِلنَّاسِ كُونُوا عِبَادًا لِي مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ وَلَكِنْ كُونُوا رَبَّانِيِّينَ بِمَا كُنْتُمْ تُعَلِّمُونَ الْكِتَابَ وَبِمَا كُنْتُمْ تَدْرُسُونَ (٧٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (ثُمَّ يَقُولَ): it is conjoined to «يُؤْتِيَهُ». It is also read in the nominative, as a new sentence. (بِمَا كُنْتُمْ): in the position of an adjective of «رَبَّانِيِّينَ». The bāʾ may also be causal, in which case it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «كَانَ», and «مَا» is maṣdariyya (verbal-noun-forming), i.e. "(because of) your teaching the Book". The bāʾ may also be attached to «رَبَّانِيِّينَ». (تَعْلَمُونَ): read with the light form, i.e. "you know", and with the doubled form, i.e. "you teach it to others".
(تَدْرُسُونَ): read with the light form, i.e. "you study the Book", so the object is omitted; and it is read with the doubled form and ḍamma on the tāʾ, i.e. "you teach people the Book (تُدَرِّسُونَ)".

ukberi-tibyan:80-80.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَا يَأْمُرَكُمْ أَنْ تَتَّخِذُوا الْمَلَائِكَةَ وَالنَّبِيِّينَ أَرْبَابًا أَيَأْمُرُكُمْ بِالْكُفْرِ بَعْدَ إِذْ أَنْتُمْ مُسْلِمُونَ (٨٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَلَا يَأْمُرَكُمْ): it is read in the nominative, i.e. "and Allah (or the Prophet) does not command you", so it is a new sentence; and it is read in the accusative, conjoined to «يَقُولَ», in which case the agent is the pronoun of the Prophet or of the human being. It is also read with a sukūn on the rāʾ, to avoid a succession of vowels; this has been mentioned in al-Baqara. (إِذْ): in the position of the genitive, because «بَعْدَ» is put in construct with it. (أَنْتُمْ مُسْلِمُونَ): in the position of the genitive, because «إِذْ» is put in construct with it.

ukberi-tibyan:81-81.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذْ أَخَذَ اللَّهُ مِيثَاقَ النَّبِيِّينَ لَمَا آتَيْتُكُمْ مِنْ كِتَابٍ وَحِكْمَةٍ ثُمَّ جَاءَكُمْ رَسُولٌ مُصَدِّقٌ لِمَا مَعَكُمْ لَتُؤْمِنُنَّ بِهِ وَلَتَنْصُرُنَّهُ قَالَ أَأَقْرَرْتُمْ وَأَخَذْتُمْ عَلَى ذَلِكُمْ إِصْرِي قَالُوا أَقْرَرْنَا قَالَ فَاشْهَدُوا وَأَنَا مَعَكُمْ مِنَ الشَّاهِدِينَ (٨١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَمَا آتَيْتُكُمْ): it is read with kasra on the lām (لِمَا), and there are two views on what it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to. The first: «أَخَذَ», i.e. "for this purpose", with an omitted muḍāf, its implied form being "for the observance of what I have given you". The second: that it is attached to «الْمِيثَاق», because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "We took a covenant from them for that". «مَا» is in the sense of «الَّذِي» (a relative noun), or an indefinite qualified noun, and the referring pronoun is omitted. And (مِنْ كِتَابٍ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the omitted (pronoun), or of «الَّذِي». It is also read with fatḥa (on the lām) and a light «مَا» (لَمَا), and there are two views on it.
The first: that «مَا» is in the sense of «الَّذِي», its position being nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); the lām is the lām of commencement (lām al-ibtidāʾ), which entered to emphasise the meaning of the oath.
On its khabar (predicate) there are two views. The first: «مِنْ كِتَابٍ وَحِكْمَةٍ», i.e. "what you have been given is of the Book", the indefinite here being like the definite. The second: the khabar is «لَتُؤْمِنُنَّ بِهِ», the hāʾ referring back to the mubtadaʾ and the lām being the answer to the oath, because taking the covenant is an oath in meaning. As for His saying (ثُمَّ جَاءَكُمْ), it is conjoined to «مَا آتَيْتُكُمْ», and on the pronoun in this conjoined clause referring back to «مَا» there are two views. The first: its implied form is «ثُمَّ جَاءَكُمْ بِهِ», and making it overt was dispensed with because of His saying «بِهِ» afterwards. The second: that His saying «لِمَا مَعَكُمْ» stands in the place of the pronoun, its implied form being "confirming it", because what is with them is what He gave them. The referring element may also be the pronoun of settledness (al-istiqrār) that governs «مَعَ». The hāʾ in «بِهِ» may also refer back to the Messenger, with the pronoun referring back to the mubtadaʾ omitted; what allowed this is the length of the speech, and the fact that believing the Messenger is believing what he was given. The second view is that «مَا» is conditional, and the lām before it is for receiving the oath (al-lām al-muwaṭṭiʾa), like the one in His saying (لَئِنْ لَمْ يَنْتَهِ الْمُنَافِقُونَ); it is not obligatory, as shown by His saying (وَإِنْ لَمْ يَنْتَهُوا عَمَّا يَقُولُونَ). On this view «مَا» is in the position of the accusative governed by «آتَيْتُ», the second object being the pronoun of the addressees, and «مِنْ كِتَابٍ» is like «مِنْ آيَةٍ» in His saying (مَا نَنْسَخْ مِنْ آيَةٍ); the rest of the speech on this view is clear. And «لَمَّا» is read with fatḥa on the lām and a doubled mīm, and there are two views on it. The first: that it is the temporal one, i.e. "We took their covenant when We gave them something of the Book and wisdom", and (the speech) turned from the third person to the second, in their customary manner. The second: that he intended «لِمَنْ مَا»; then he changed the nūn to mīm because of its resemblance to it, so three mīms came in succession, and he dropped the second because it was weak, being a substitute, and because the repetition occurred through it. Ibn Jinnī mentioned this meaning in al-Muḥtasab. And «آتَيْتُكُمْ» is read in the singular, which agrees with His saying (وَإِذْ أَخَذَ اللَّهُ) and with His saying «إِصْرِي».
It is also read «آتَيْنَاكُمْ» in the plural, for majesty.
(أَأَقْرَرْتُمْ): there is an omission in it, i.e. "to that".
And (إِصْرِي): with kasra and with ḍamma (on the hamza) — two dialectal forms, both of which have been read.

ukberi-tibyan:82-82.t:
Allah the Exalted said {فَمن تولى بعد ذَلِك فَأُولَئِك هم الْفَاسِقُونَ}
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَمَنْ تَوَلَّى): «مَنْ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject); it may be in the sense of «الَّذِي» (a relative noun), or it may be conditional. (فَأُولَئِكَ): a second mubtadaʾ. And (هُمُ الْفَاسِقُونَ): a mubtadaʾ and its khabar (predicate); «هُمْ» may also be a separating pronoun (faṣl).

ukberi-tibyan:83-83.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَفَغَيْرَ دِينِ اللَّهِ يَبْغُونَ وَلَهُ أَسْلَمَ مَنْ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ طَوْعًا وَكَرْهًا وَإِلَيْهِ يُرْجَعُونَ (٨٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَفَغَيْرَ): accusative, governed by «يَبْغُونَ». It is read with yāʾ, in the third person, like what precedes it, and with tāʾ, in the second person, the implied wording being "say to them". (طَوْعًا وَكَرْهًا): two maṣdars (verbal nouns) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). They may also be two maṣdars not derived from the verb's own root (i.e. absolute objects in sense), because «أَسْلَمَ» means "submitted and obeyed". [Translator's note: the source has «عَلَى غَيْرِ الصَّدْرِ», evidently for «عَلَى غَيْرِ الْمَصْدَرِ» / «عَلَى غَيْرِ لَفْظِ الْفِعْلِ».] (تُرْجَعُونَ): with tāʾ, in the second person, and with yāʾ, in the third person. [Translator's note: the verse number printed in the heading is (٨٢); this verse is 3:83.]

ukberi-tibyan:84-84.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قُلْ آمَنَّا بِاللَّهِ وَمَا أُنْزِلَ عَلَيْنَا وَمَا أُنْزِلَ عَلَى إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَإِسْمَاعِيلَ وَإِسْحَاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ وَالْأَسْبَاطِ وَمَا أُوتِيَ مُوسَى وَعِيسَى وَالنَّبِيُّونَ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ لَا نُفَرِّقُ بَيْنَ أَحَدٍ مِنْهُمْ وَنَحْنُ لَهُ مُسْلِمُونَ (٨٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (قُلْ آمَنَّا): its implied form is "Say, O Muḥammad: we believe", i.e. "I and those with me", or "I and the prophets". It is also said that the implied wording is "Say to them: say, we believe".

ukberi-tibyan:85-85.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَنْ يَبْتَغِ غَيْرَ الْإِسْلَامِ دِينًا فَلَنْ يُقْبَلَ مِنْهُ وَهُوَ فِي الْآخِرَةِ مِنَ الْخَاسِرِينَ (٨٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَمَنْ يَبْتَغِ غَيْرَ): the majority pronounce both ghayns distinctly, and assimilation is reported from Abū ʿAmr; it is weak, because the kasra of the first ghayn indicates the omitted yāʾ. And (دِينًا) is a tamyīz (specification); it may also be the object of «يَبْتَغِ». And (غَيْرَ) is then an adjective put before it, which thereby became a ḥāl (circumstantial). (وَهُوَ فِي الْآخِرَةِ مِنَ الْخَاسِرِينَ): in iʿrāb it is like His saying (وَإِنَّهُ فِي الْآخِرَةِ لَمِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ), which has been mentioned.

ukberi-tibyan:86-86.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (كَيْفَ يَهْدِي اللَّهُ قَوْمًا كَفَرُوا بَعْدَ إِيمَانِهِمْ وَشَهِدُوا أَنَّ الرَّسُولَ حَقٌّ وَجَاءَهُمُ الْبَيِّنَاتُ وَاللَّهُ لَا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الظَّالِمِينَ (٨٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (كَيْفَ يَهْدِي اللَّهُ): «كَيْفَ» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) or an adverb (ẓarf), governed by «يَهْدِي»; its parallel has preceded. (وَشَهِدُوا): there are three views on it. The first: it is a ḥāl of the pronoun in «كَفَرُوا», with «قَدْ» implied along with it. What governs it cannot be «يَهْدِي», because He does guide one who «شَهِدَ أَنَّ الرَّسُولَ حَقٌّ» ("bore witness that the Messenger is true"). The second: that it is conjoined to «كَفَرُوا», i.e. "how will He guide them after the two things have come together?" The third: that the implied wording is «وَأَنْ شَهِدُوا», i.e. "after they believed and (after) they bore witness", so it is in the position of the genitive.

ukberi-tibyan:87-87.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أُولَئِكَ جَزَاؤُهُمْ أَنَّ عَلَيْهِمْ لَعْنَةَ اللَّهِ وَالْمَلَائِكَةِ وَالنَّاسِ أَجْمَعِينَ (٨٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أُولَئِكَ): a mubtadaʾ (subject), and (جَزَاؤُهُمْ) a second mubtadaʾ; and (أَنَّ عَلَيْهِمْ لَعْنَةَ اللَّهِ): «أَنَّ» with its noun and its khabar is the khabar (predicate) of «جَزَاء», i.e. "their recompense is the curse".
«جَزَاؤُهُمْ» may also be a badal (substitute) of «أُولَئِكَ», a badal of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl).

ukberi-tibyan:88-88.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا لَا يُخَفَّفُ عَنْهُمُ الْعَذَابُ وَلَا هُمْ يُنْظَرُونَ (٨٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا): a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the hāʾ and mīm in «عَلَيْهِمْ»; what governs it is the preposition, or what the preposition is attached to. «فِيهَا» means: in the curse.

ukberi-tibyan:91-91.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَمَاتُوا وَهُمْ كُفَّارٌ فَلَنْ يُقْبَلَ مِنْ أَحَدِهِمْ مِلْءُ الْأَرْضِ ذَهَبًا وَلَوِ افْتَدَى بِهِ أُولَئِكَ لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ وَمَا لَهُمْ مِنْ نَاصِرِينَ (٩١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (ذَهَبًا): a tamyīz (specification). The hāʾ in «بِهِ» refers back to «الْمِلْء» ("the fill") or to «ذَهَب».

ukberi-tibyan:92-92.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَنْ تَنَالُوا الْبِرَّ حَتَّى تُنْفِقُوا مِمَّا تُحِبُّونَ وَمَا تُنْفِقُوا مِنْ شَيْءٍ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ بِهِ عَلِيمٌ (٩٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِمَّا تُحِبُّونَ): «مَا» is in the sense of «الَّذِي» (a relative noun), or an indefinite qualified noun. It cannot be maṣdariyya (verbal-noun-forming), because love is not something spent. If you make the maṣdar have the sense of the passive participle (the thing loved), it is permissible according to the opinion of Abū ʿAlī (al-Fārisī). (وَمَا تُنْفِقُوا مِنْ شَيْءٍ): its parallel has been mentioned in al-Baqara. The hāʾ in «بِهِ» refers back to «مَا» or to «شَيْء».

ukberi-tibyan:93-93.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (كُلُّ الطَّعَامِ كَانَ حِلًّا لِبَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ إِلَّا مَا حَرَّمَ إِسْرَائِيلُ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ تُنَزَّلَ التَّوْرَاةُ قُلْ فَأْتُوا بِالتَّوْرَاةِ فَاتْلُوهَا إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ (٩٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (حِلًّا): i.e. «حَلَالًا» ("lawful"), and the meaning is "all of it was lawful". (إِلَّا مَا حَرَّمَ): in the position of the accusative, because it is an exception from the noun of «كَانَ», and what governs it is «كَانَ».
It may also be governed by «حِلًّا», which would contain a pronoun from which the exception is made, because «حِلّ» and «حَلَال» stand in the place of an active participle meaning "permissible" and "allowed". (مِنْ قَبْلِ): attached (mutaʿalliq) to «حَرَّمَ».

ukberi-tibyan:94-94.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَمَنِ افْتَرَى عَلَى اللَّهِ الْكَذِبَ مِنْ بَعْدِ ذَلِكَ فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الظَّالِمُونَ (٩٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْ بَعْدِ ذَلِكَ): it may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to «افْتَرَى», or to «الْكَذِب».

ukberi-tibyan:95-95.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قُلْ صَدَقَ اللَّهُ فَاتَّبِعُوا مِلَّةَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ حَنِيفًا وَمَا كَانَ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ (٩٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (قُلْ صَدَقَ اللَّهُ): the majority pronounce the lām distinctly, which is the original; and it is read with assimilation (of the lām of «قُلْ» into the ṣād), because the ṣād has spreading (inbisāṭ) and the lām has spreading, such that their edges meet, and so they became close to each other. The implied wording is "say to them: Allah has spoken the truth".
(حَنِيفًا): it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «إِبْرَاهِيم» or of «الْمِلَّة»; it is masculine because «الْمِلَّة» and «الدِّين» are one.

ukberi-tibyan:96-96.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ أَوَّلَ بَيْتٍ وُضِعَ لِلنَّاسِ لَلَّذِي بِبَكَّةَ مُبَارَكًا وَهُدًى لِلْعَالَمِينَ (٩٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وُضِعَ لِلنَّاسِ): the clause is in the position of the genitive as an adjective of «بَيْت», and the khabar (predicate) (of «إِنَّ») is «لَلَّذِي».
And (مُبَارَكًا وَهُدًى) are two ḥāls (circumstantials) of the pronoun in «وُضِعَ», or, if you wish, of the (pronoun in the) preposition (بِبَكَّةَ); what governs them is the notion of settledness (al-istiqrār).

ukberi-tibyan:178-178.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَا يَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا أَنَّمَا نُمْلِي لَهُمْ خَيْرٌ لِأَنْفُسِهِمْ إِنَّمَا نُمْلِي لَهُمْ لِيَزْدَادُوا إِثْمًا وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ مُهِينٌ (١٧٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَلَا يَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا): it is read with the yāʾ, and its fāʿil (agent) is الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا. As for the two objects, what stands in their place is His saying «أَنَّمَا نُمْلِي لَهُمْ خَيْرٌ لِأَنْفُسِهِمْ», for أَنَّ together with what it governs fills the place of the two objects according to Sībawayh. According to al-Akhfash the second object is omitted, its implied form being "beneficial" (نَافِعًا) or the like. On «مَا» there are two views. The first: it has the sense of الَّذِي ("that which").
The second: it is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun). It cannot be the restraining (kāffa) مَا nor the redundant (zāʾida) one, since if it were so, خَيْرٌ would be made accusative by نُمْلِي, and أَنَّ would need a khabar (predicate) if مَا were redundant, or else a verb would be implied as following it; and both are impossible. It has been read, as an irregular (shādhdh) reading, in the accusative (خَيْرًا), on the view that لِأَنْفُسِهِمْ is the khabar of أَنَّ, and لَهُمْ is for clarification (tabyīn) or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from خَيْرًا. It has also been read, among the irregular readings, with kasra on إِنَّ (إِنَّمَا), and it is the answer to an omitted oath, the oath and its answer together filling the place of the two objects.
Ḥamza read (تَحْسَبَنَّ) with the tāʾ, as an address to the Prophet. الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا is the first object, and on the second object there are two views. The first: it is the clause made up of أَنَّ and what it governs. The second: that the first object is omitted, and the muḍāf ilayhi has been put in its place [Translator's note: so in the text; this second view concerns the first object, and the clause then fills the place of both objects], the implied form being: "do not reckon the respite given to those who disbelieve" (وَلَا تَحْسَبَنَّ إِمْلَاءَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا). His saying أَنَّمَا نُمْلِي لَهُمْ is then a badal (substitute) from the omitted muḍāf, and the clause fills the place of the two objects; the implied form is: "do not reckon that the respite given to those who disbelieve is better for them". You may also make أَنَّ and what it governs a badal from الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا, a badal of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl), and the clause fills the place of the two objects.
(إِنَّمَا نُمْلِي لَهُمْ لِيَزْدَادُوا): resumptive. It is also said: أَنَّمَا نُمْلِي لَهُمْ is a repetition of the first, and لِيَزْدَادُوا is the second object of تَحْسَبَ on the reading with the tāʾ, the implied sense being: "Do not reckon, O Muhammad, that the respite given to those who disbelieve is good so that they may increase in faith; rather, it is so that they may increase in sin". It is related of one of the Companions that he read it in that way.

ukberi-tibyan:179-179.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (مَا كَانَ اللَّهُ لِيَذَرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَى مَا أَنْتُمْ عَلَيْهِ حَتَّى يَمِيزَ الْخَبِيثَ مِنَ الطَّيِّبِ وَمَا كَانَ اللَّهُ لِيُطْلِعَكُمْ عَلَى الْغَيْبِ وَلَكِنَّ اللَّهَ يَجْتَبِي مِنْ رُسُلِهِ مَنْ يَشَاءُ فَآمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرُسُلِهِ وَإِنْ تُؤْمِنُوا وَتَتَّقُوا فَلَكُمْ أَجْرٌ عَظِيمٌ (١٧٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَا كَانَ اللَّهُ لِيَذَرَ): the khabar (predicate) of كَانَ is omitted, its implied form being: "Allah was not intending to leave" (مَا كَانَ اللَّهُ مُرِيدًا لِأَنْ يَذَرَ). The khabar cannot be لِيَذَرَ, because the verb after the lām is made accusative by [an implied] أَنْ, so the implied form would become: "Allah was not [the act of] leaving the believers in the state you are in" [Translator's note: the text reads لِيَتْرُكَ, but the argument requires the maṣdar, i.e. "Allah was not the leaving…"]; and the khabar of كَانَ is, in meaning, its noun, whereas the leaving is not Allah the Exalted. The Kufans said: the lām is redundant (zāʾida) and the khabar is the verb. This is weak, because what comes after it has become accusative: if the accusative is due to the lām itself, then it is not redundant; and if the accusative is due to أَنْ, it is unsound for the reason we have mentioned.
The origin of يَذَرُ is يَوْذَرُ, and the wāw was dropped by analogy with يَدَعُ, because it has its meaning. There is no [phonological] cause for the dropping of the wāw in يَذَرُ, since it does not fall between a yāʾ and a kasra, nor what stands for a kasra, unlike يَدَعُ, whose origin is يَوْدَعُ, where the wāw was dropped because it falls between the yāʾ and what stands for a kasra, since the original is يَوْدِعُ, like يَوْعِدُ. The dāl of يَدَعُ was given fatḥa only because its final radical is a guttural letter, so what precedes it is given fatḥa for its sake; similar are يَسَعُ, يَطَأُ, يَقَعُ and the like. No past tense of يَذَرُ is used, تَرَكَ being sufficient in its place.
(يَمِيزَ): it is read with sukūn on the yāʾ (يَمِيزَ), its past tense being مَازَ; and with doubling of it (يُمَيِّزَ), its past tense being مَيَّزَ; both have one meaning. The doubling is not to make the verb transitive, as in فَرِحَ and فَرَّحْتُهُ, because مَازَ and مَيَّزَ are both transitive to one object.

ukberi-tibyan:180-180.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَا يَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ يَبْخَلُونَ بِمَا آتَاهُمُ اللَّهُ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ هُوَ خَيْرًا لَهُمْ بَلْ هُوَ شَرٌّ لَهُمْ سَيُطَوَّقُونَ مَا بَخِلُوا بِهِ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ وَلِلَّهِ مِيرَاثُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَاللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرٌ (١٨٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَلَا يَحْسَبَنَّ): it is read with the yāʾ, in the third person, and «الَّذِينَ يَبْخَلُونَ» is the fāʿil (agent). On the first object there are two views:
The first: it is «هُوَ», which is the pronoun of the stinginess indicated by يَبْخَلُونَ. The second: it is omitted, its implied form being "the stinginess" (الْبُخْلُ), and «هُوَ» on this view is a separating pronoun (faṣl).
It is also read «تَحْسَبَنَّ» with the tāʾ, as an address, and the implied form is: "Do not reckon, O Muhammad, the stinginess of those who are stingy…", so the muḍāf was omitted. This is weak, because it involves implying the stinginess before mentioning what indicates it; on this view هُوَ is a faṣl or a tawkīd (emphasis).
The origin of (مِيرَاثُ) is مِوْرَاثٌ; the wāw was changed into yāʾ because of the kasra before it. الْمِيرَاثُ is a maṣdar (verbal noun), like الْمِيعَادُ.

ukberi-tibyan:181-181.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَقَدْ سَمِعَ اللَّهُ قَوْلَ الَّذِينَ قَالُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ فَقِيرٌ وَنَحْنُ أَغْنِيَاءُ سَنَكْتُبُ مَا قَالُوا وَقَتْلَهُمُ الْأَنْبِيَاءَ بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ وَنَقُولُ ذُوقُوا عَذَابَ الْحَرِيقِ (١٨١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَقَدْ سَمِعَ اللَّهُ قَوْلَ الَّذِينَ قَالُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ فَقِيرٌ): what governs the position of إِنَّ and what it governs is قَالُوا, and it is what is reported by it. It may also be governed by the قَوْلَ that is in the genitive construct (muḍāf), because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun); this follows the view of the Kufans that the first [of two competing governors] is given the government. That is a weak principle, and it is weaker still here, because the second is a verb and the first a maṣdar, and giving government to the verb is stronger. (سَنَكْتُبُ مَا قَالُوا): it is read with the nūn, and مَا قَالُوا is accusative by it. (وَقَتْلَهُمُ): conjoined to it; مَا is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun) or has the sense of الَّذِي. It is read with the yāʾ, naming the agent (سَيَكْتُبُ); and it is read with the yāʾ as a verb whose agent is not named (passive) (سَيُكْتَبُ), with قَتْلُهُمْ in the nominative, which is clear. (وَنَقُولُ): with the nūn and with the yāʾ (وَيَقُولُ).

ukberi-tibyan:182-182.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ذَلِكَ بِمَا قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيكُمْ وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ لَيْسَ بِظَلَّامٍ لِلْعَبِيدِ (١٨٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (ذَلِكَ): a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «بِمَا» is its khabar (predicate); the implied form is: "deserved because of what [your hands] sent forth".
(ظَلَّامٍ): faʿʿāl from الظُّلْم ("wrongdoing"). If it is said: the pattern faʿʿāl is for intensiveness (taktīr), and negating much wrongdoing does not entail negating little wrongdoing; had He said بِظَالِمٍ, it would have been a stronger indication of negating wrongdoing, little and much.
The answer to this is from three angles. The first: that faʿʿāl has occurred without abundance being intended by it, as in the saying of Ṭarafa:
وَلَسْتُ بِحَلَّالِ التِّلَاعِ مَخَافَةً ... وَلَكِنْ مَتَى يَسْتَرْفِدُ الْقَوْمُ أَرْفُدِ
("I am not one who camps in the hollows for fear [of guests]; rather, whenever the people seek my help, I help.")
He does not mean here that he may camp in the hollows a little, because that is repelled by his saying «مَتَى يَسْتَرْفِدُ الْقَوْمُ أَرْفُدِ», and this indicates the negation of stinginess in every situation; and because complete praise is not achieved if he intended abundance. The second: that ظَلَّامٍ here is for abundance because it is set against الْعَبِيد, and among the servants there is abundance; when wrongdoing is set against them it would be much.
The third: that when He negates much wrongdoing, little wrongdoing is necessarily negated, because whoever does wrong does so only to benefit from the wrongdoing; so if one for whom benefit and harm are possible abandons much wrongdoing despite its greater benefit, he is all the more likely to abandon wrongdoing of little benefit.
There is a fourth view on it: that it is by way of attribution (nasab), i.e. He is not to be associated with wrongdoing; so it is of the type of بَزَّازٌ ("cloth-merchant") and عَطَّارٌ ("perfumer").

ukberi-tibyan:15-15.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قُلْ أَؤُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِخَيْرٍ مِنْ ذَلِكُمْ لِلَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ جَنَّاتٌ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا وَأَزْوَاجٌ مُطَهَّرَةٌ وَرِضْوَانٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَاللَّهُ بَصِيرٌ بِالْعِبَادِ (١٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (قُلْ أَؤُنَبِّئُكُمْ): it is read with both hamzas fully pronounced, according to the origin; the second is changed into a pure wāw because of its ḍamma; and [it is read] with softening (talyīn) of it, which is making it between the wāw and the hamza — what permitted that being the fatḥa of what precedes it.
(بِخَيْرٍ مِنْ ذَلِكُمْ): «من» is in the position of the accusative by خير, its implied form being: "of what surpasses that". It is not permissible for it to be a naʿt (adjective) of خير, because that would require Paradise and what is in it, of what they desired, to be a part of what they renounced, such as wealth and the like. (لِلَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا): the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject), which is «جنات». (تَجْرِي) is a naʿt of it.
(عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ) admits two views. The first: that it is an adverb (ẓarf) for the [implied] settledness (istiqrār).
The second: that it is originally a naʿt of the gardens, which was placed first and so became accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); and the operator may be تجري. (مِنْ تَحْتِهَا) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to تجري, and it may be a ḥāl from الأنهار, i.e. "the rivers flow, being beneath it". جنات is read with kasra on the tāʾ, and there are two views on it. The first: it is genitive as a badal (substitute) from خير, and للذين اتقوا on this view is a naʿt of خير.
The second: that it is accusative with an implied أعني ("I mean"), or as a badal from the position of بخير.
And the nominative may be as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it is gardens"; similar to it is (بِشَرٍّ مِنْ ذَلِكُمُ النَّارُ), which will be mentioned in its place, if Allah the Exalted wills.
(خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا): a ḥāl, if you wish from the hāʾ in تحتها, and if you wish from the pronoun in اتقوا; the operator is the [implied] settledness, and it is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara).
(وَأَزْوَاجٌ): conjoined (maʿṭūf) to جنات in the nominative. As for the other reading, it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, its implied form being «ولهم أزواج» ("and they have spouses"). (وَرِضْوَانٌ): it is read with kasra on the rāʾ and with ḍamma; they are two dialectal forms. It is a maṣdar (verbal noun); parallels of the kasra form are الإتيان and الحرمان, and parallels of the ḍamma form are الشكران and الكفران.

ukberi-tibyan:183-183.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الَّذِينَ قَالُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَهِدَ إِلَيْنَا أَلَّا نُؤْمِنَ لِرَسُولٍ حَتَّى يَأْتِيَنَا بِقُرْبَانٍ تَأْكُلُهُ النَّارُ قُلْ قَدْ جَاءَكُمْ رُسُلٌ مِنْ قَبْلِي بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ وَبِالَّذِي قُلْتُمْ فَلِمَ قَتَلْتُمُوهُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ (١٨٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الَّذِينَ قَالُوا): it is in the position of the genitive as a badal (substitute) from His saying: (الَّذِينَ قَالُوا) [i.e. in verse 181]. It may also be accusative by an implied أَعْنِي ("I mean"), or nominative by an implied «هُمْ» ("they are"). (أَلَّا نُؤْمِنَ): it may be in the position of the genitive, with the implied form "that we should not believe" (بِأَنْ لَا نُؤْمِنَ), because the meaning of عَهِدَ is "enjoined" (وَصَّى). It may be in the position of the accusative, with the preposition implied and the verb reaching it directly. It may also be accusative by عَهِدَ itself, because you say عَهِدْتُ إِلَيْهِ عَهْدًا not as a maṣdar (verbal noun), since its meaning is "I bound him to [it]". أَنْ may be written separately (أَنْ لَا) or joined (أَلَّا); and some drop it [i.e. the nūn] in writing, the doubling being sufficient.
(حَتَّى يَأْتِيَنَا بِقُرْبَانٍ): there is an omitted muḍāf in it, its implied form being: "with the offering of a sacrifice" (بِتَقْرِيبِ قُرْبَانٍ), i.e. he legislates that for us.

ukberi-tibyan:16-16.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (الَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَا إِنَّنَا آمَنَّا فَاغْفِرْ لَنَا ذُنُوبَنَا وَقِنَا عَذَابَ النَّارِ (١٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ): it may be in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of الذين اتقوا, or a badal (substitute) from it.
It is weak for it to be a naʿt of العباد, because that involves restricting Allah's knowledge; it is permissible despite its weakness, and the justification for it would be informing them that He knows the measure of their hardship in worship, so He will reward them for it, as He said: (وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِإِيمَانِكُمْ). It may be in the position of the accusative with an implied أعني ("I mean"), and in the position of the nominative with an implied «هم» ("they are").

ukberi-tibyan:184-184.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَإِنْ كَذَّبُوكَ فَقَدْ كُذِّبَ رُسُلٌ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ جَاءُوا بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ وَالزُّبُرِ وَالْكِتَابِ الْمُنِيرِ (١٨٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَالزُّبُرِ): it is read without the bāʾ, the conjunction being sufficient, and with the bāʾ (وَبِالزُّبُرِ), repeating the preposition. الزُّبُرُ is the plural of زَبُورٌ, like رَسُولٌ and رُسُلٌ. (وَالْكِتَابِ): generic.

ukberi-tibyan:17-17.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (الصَّابِرِينَ وَالصَّادِقِينَ وَالْقَانِتِينَ وَالْمُنْفِقِينَ وَالْمُسْتَغْفِرِينَ بِالْأَسْحَارِ (١٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الصَّابِرِينَ) and what follows it may be genitive, and may be accusative, as a naʿt (adjective) of الذين, if you put that in the position of the genitive or the accusative. If you make الذين nominative, you put الصابرين in the accusative by [an implied] أعني ("I mean").
If it is said: why did the wāw enter these, when all of them are of one group?
There are two answers. The first: when adjectives are repeated, some of them may be conjoined to others with wāw, even if the one described by them is one, and the entry of the wāw in this kind is for magnification, because it signals that each adjective independently merits praise. The second answer: that these qualities are distributed among them — some of them are patient, some truthful — so those described by them are several.

ukberi-tibyan:18-18.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (شَهِدَ اللَّهُ أَنَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ وَالْمَلَائِكَةُ وَأُولُو الْعِلْمِ قَائِمًا بِالْقِسْطِ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ (١٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (شَهِدَ اللَّهُ): the majority hold that it is a verb and its fāʿil (agent).
It is read «شهداءَ لله», plural of شهيد or شاهد, with fatḥa on the hamza and an added lām with the name of Allah; it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from يستغفرون [Translator's note: so in the text; the preceding verse has المستغفرين]. It is also read the same way except in the nominative, on the implied form: "they are witnesses".
And it is read «شهداءُ الله» in the nominative and in construct.
(أَنَّهُ): i.e. بأنه, in the position of the accusative or the genitive, according to the disagreement we have mentioned in more than one place. (قَائِمًا): a ḥāl from هو, its operator being the meaning of the clause, i.e. "He is singled out [as] maintaining".
It has been said that it is a ḥāl from the name of Allah, i.e. He bore witness to His own oneness. On both views it is an emphatic ḥāl (ḥāl muʾakkida). Ibn Masʿūd read القائمُ, on the basis that it is a badal (substitute) or the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject).
(الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ): like الرحمن الرحيم in His saying (وَإِلَهُكُمْ إِلَهٌ وَاحِدٌ), which has been mentioned.

ukberi-tibyan:19-19.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنَّ الدِّينَ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ الْإِسْلَامُ وَمَا اخْتَلَفَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ إِلَّا مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا جَاءَهُمُ الْعِلْمُ بَغْيًا بَيْنَهُمْ وَمَنْ يَكْفُرْ بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ سَرِيعُ الْحِسَابِ (١٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِنَّ الدِّينَ): the majority read it with kasra on the hamza, as a resumption (istiʾnāf). It is read with fatḥa, on the basis that the clause is a maṣdar (verbal noun) whose position is genitive as a badal (substitute) from أنه لا إله إلا هو, i.e. "Allah bore witness to His oneness, that the religion…". It has been said that it is a badal from القسط.
It has also been said that it is in the position of the accusative as a badal from the position. The badal on all these views is the substitution of a thing for a thing, being the same thing; and a badal of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl) is also possible. (عِنْدَ اللَّهِ): an adverb (ẓarf) whose operator is الدين; it is not a ḥāl (circumstantial) from it, because أن operates on the ḥāl [Translator's note: so in the text; the sense seems to require "because إنّ does not operate on a ḥāl"]. (بَغْيًا): a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), the implied form being: "they differed after knowledge came to them, out of transgression".
And it may be a maṣdar in the position of a ḥāl. (وَمَنْ يَكْفُرْ): «من» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is يكفر. It has been said that the clause made up of the condition and its response is the khabar.
It has also been said that the khabar is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), the implied form being: "swift in reckoning for him".

ukberi-tibyan:20-20.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَإِنْ حَاجُّوكَ فَقُلْ أَسْلَمْتُ وَجْهِيَ لِلَّهِ وَمَنِ اتَّبَعَنِ وَقُلْ لِلَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ وَالْأُمِّيِّينَ أَأَسْلَمْتُمْ فَإِنْ أَسْلَمُوا فَقَدِ اهْتَدَوْا وَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا فَإِنَّمَا عَلَيْكَ الْبَلَاغُ وَاللَّهُ بَصِيرٌ بِالْعِبَادِ (٢٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَمَنِ اتَّبَعَنِ): «من» is in the position of the nominative, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the tāʾ in أسلمت, i.e. "and those who follow me have submitted their faces to Allah".
It has been said that it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the khabar (predicate) is omitted, i.e. "likewise".
It is permissible to keep the yāʾ, according to the origin, and to drop it, likening it to verse-endings and rhymes, as in the saying of al-Aʿshā:
فَهَلْ يَمْنَعَنِّي ارْتِيَادِي الْبِلَا ... دَ مِنْ حَذَرِ الْمَوْتِ أَنْ يَأْتِيَنْ
(Will my roaming the lands, for fear of death, prevent it from coming to me?)
This is common in their speech. (أَأَسْلَمْتُمْ): it carries the meaning of a command, i.e. "submit!", as in His saying (فَهَلْ أَنْتُمْ مُنْتَهُونَ), i.e. "desist!".

ukberi-tibyan:21-21.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَكْفُرُونَ بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ وَيَقْتُلُونَ النَّبِيِّينَ بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ وَيَقْتُلُونَ الَّذِينَ يَأْمُرُونَ بِالْقِسْطِ مِنَ النَّاسِ فَبَشِّرْهُمْ بِعَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ (٢١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَبَشِّرْهُمْ): it is the khabar (predicate) of إنّ. The fāʾ entered it because the ṣila (relative clause) of الذي is a verb, and that signals that the tidings of punishment are deserved as recompense for disbelief. إنّ does not prevent the fāʾ from entering the khabar, because it does not alter the meaning of the mubtadaʾ (subject) [construction] but rather emphasises it; had «كأنّ» or «ليت» entered on الذي, the entry of the fāʾ into the khabar would not have been permissible. It is read (وَيُقَاتِلُونَ النَّبِيِّينَ), and (وَيَقْتُلُونَ) is the well-known [reading]; their meanings are close.

ukberi-tibyan:23-23.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا نَصِيبًا مِنَ الْكِتَابِ يُدْعَوْنَ إِلَى كِتَابِ اللَّهِ لِيَحْكُمَ بَيْنَهُمْ ثُمَّ يَتَوَلَّى فَرِيقٌ مِنْهُمْ وَهُمْ مُعْرِضُونَ (٢٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يُدْعَوْنَ): in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الذين. (وَهُمْ مُعْرِضُونَ): in the position of the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of فريق, or a ḥāl from the pronoun in the prepositional phrase. We have mentioned that at His saying (أَنْ تَكْرَهُوا شَيْئًا وَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ).

ukberi-tibyan:24-24.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (ذَلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ قَالُوا لَنْ تَمَسَّنَا النَّارُ إِلَّا أَيَّامًا مَعْدُودَاتٍ وَغَرَّهُمْ فِي دِينِهِمْ مَا كَانُوا يَفْتَرُونَ (٢٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (ذَلِكَ): it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "the matter is that". On this view His saying (بِأَنَّهُمْ قَالُوا) is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the meaning of pointing in ذا, i.e. "that matter [being] deserved because of their saying". This is weak; the good [view] is that ذلك is a mubtadaʾ and بأنهم its khabar, i.e. "that punishment is deserved because of their saying".

ukberi-tibyan:25-25.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَكَيْفَ إِذَا جَمَعْنَاهُمْ لِيَوْمٍ لَا رَيْبَ فِيهِ وَوُفِّيَتْ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ مَا كَسَبَتْ وَهُمْ لَا يُظْلَمُونَ (٢٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَكَيْفَ إِذَا جَمَعْنَاهُمْ): كيف is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and its operator is omitted, its implied form being: "how will they fare?" or "how will they be?".
It has been said that كيف is an adverb (ẓarf) for this omitted [verb], and إذا is also an adverb for the omitted [verb].

ukberi-tibyan:26-26.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قُلِ اللَّهُمَّ مَالِكَ الْمُلْكِ تُؤْتِي الْمُلْكَ مَنْ تَشَاءُ وَتَنْزِعُ الْمُلْكَ مِمَّنْ تَشَاءُ وَتُعِزُّ مَنْ تَشَاءُ وَتُذِلُّ مَنْ تَشَاءُ بِيَدِكَ الْخَيْرُ إِنَّكَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ (٢٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (قُلِ اللَّهُمَّ): the doubled mīm is a compensation for [the vocative] yā. Al-Farrāʾ said: the origin is يا الله أُمَّنا بخير ("O Allah, direct us with good"); that is a weak doctrine, and the place for explaining its weakness is other than this. (مَالِكَ الْمُلْكِ): it is a second vocative, i.e. "O Owner of sovereignty".
According to Sībawayh it is not permissible for it to be a naʿt (adjective) according to the position, because the mīm at the end of the one addressed prevents that in his view. Al-Mubarrad and al-Zajjāj allowed it to be a naʿt.
(تُؤْتِي الْمُلْكَ): it, and what follows it of conjoined [verbs], is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "You". It has been said that it is resumptive.
It has also been said that the clause is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the one addressed — and the accusative of a ḥāl from the one addressed is disputed. The implied form is: "whom You will to give it to", and "whom You will to take it from".
(بِيَدِكَ الْخَيْرُ): resumptive.
It has been said that its ruling is the ruling of the clauses before it.

ukberi-tibyan:27-27.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (تُولِجُ اللَّيْلَ فِي النَّهَارِ وَتُولِجُ النَّهَارَ فِي اللَّيْلِ وَتُخْرِجُ الْحَيَّ مِنَ الْمَيِّتِ وَتُخْرِجُ الْمَيِّتَ مِنَ الْحَيِّ وَتَرْزُقُ مَنْ تَشَاءُ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ (٢٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الْمَيِّتَ مِنَ الْحَيِّ): it is read without doubling and with doubling; we have mentioned it at His saying (إِنَّمَا حَرَّمَ عَلَيْكُمُ الْمَيْتَةَ). (بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ): it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the omitted object, i.e. "You provide for whom You will, without his being called to account". It may be a ḥāl from the pronoun of the fāʿil (agent), i.e. "You will, not reckoning with him" or "not straitening him". And it may be a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun) or an omitted object, i.e. "a provision not small".

ukberi-tibyan:185-185.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذَائِقَةُ الْمَوْتِ وَإِنَّمَا تُوَفَّوْنَ أُجُورَكُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ فَمَنْ زُحْزِحَ عَنِ النَّارِ وَأُدْخِلَ الْجَنَّةَ فَقَدْ فَازَ وَمَا الْحَيَاةُ الدُّنْيَا إِلَّا مَتَاعُ الْغُرُورِ (١٨٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (كُلُّ نَفْسٍ): a mubtadaʾ (subject); this is permissible even though it is indefinite because of the generality in it. (ذَائِقَةُ الْمَوْتِ): the khabar (predicate). It is made feminine according to the meaning of كُلّ, because "every soul" is souls; had it been made masculine according to the wording of كُلّ, that would have been permissible. The genitive construct of (ذَائِقَةُ) is non-genuine (ghayr maḥḍa), because it is indefinite, describing a state [Translator's note: literally "by which the state is narrated"]. It was read as an irregular (shādhdh) reading: «ذَائِقَةٌ الْمَوْتَ», with nunation and with [the participle] governing. It is also read irregularly «ذَائِقُهُ الْمَوْتُ», making the hāʾ a pronoun for كُلّ according to its wording; and it is [then] a mubtadaʾ and khabar.
(وَإِنَّمَا): «مَا» here is restraining (kāffa); that is why «أُجُورَكُمْ» is accusative by the verb. Had it had the sense of الَّذِي or been maṣdariyya, أُجُورُكُمْ would have been nominative.

ukberi-tibyan:186-186.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَتُبْلَوُنَّ فِي أَمْوَالِكُمْ وَأَنْفُسِكُمْ وَلَتَسْمَعُنَّ مِنَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ وَمِنَ الَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوا أَذًى كَثِيرًا وَإِنْ تَصْبِرُوا وَتَتَّقُوا فَإِنَّ ذَلِكَ مِنْ عَزْمِ الْأُمُورِ (١٨٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَتُبْلَوُنَّ): the wāw in it is not the final radical (lām) of the word but the wāw of the plural, given a vowel because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; the ḍamma of the wāw is an indication of what was dropped. The wāw was not changed into alif, despite its being vowelled and preceded by fatḥa, because that [vowel] is incidental; for the same reason it is not permissible to change it into hamza despite its having ḍamma, whereas had [the ḍamma] been inherent, that would have been permissible.

ukberi-tibyan:187-187.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذْ أَخَذَ اللَّهُ مِيثَاقَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ لَتُبَيِّنُنَّهُ لِلنَّاسِ وَلَا تَكْتُمُونَهُ فَنَبَذُوهُ وَرَاءَ ظُهُورِهِمْ وَاشْتَرَوْا بِهِ ثَمَنًا قَلِيلًا فَبِئْسَ مَا يَشْتَرُونَ (١٨٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَتُبَيِّنُنَّهُ), (وَلَا تَكْتُمُونَهُ): both are read with the yāʾ, in the third person, because what the pronoun refers back to is an overt noun, and every overt noun is referred to by a third-person pronoun.
Both are also read with the tāʾ, as an address, its implied form being: "and We said to them: you shall surely make it clear".
Since the taking of the covenant has the sense of an oath, He brought the lām and the nūn in the verb; and He did not bring them in يَكْتُمُونَ, the emphasis in the first verb being sufficient, because تَكْتُمُونَهُ is an emphasis [of it].

ukberi-tibyan:188-188.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَا تَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ يَفْرَحُونَ بِمَا أَتَوْا وَيُحِبُّونَ أَنْ يُحْمَدُوا بِمَا لَمْ يَفْعَلُوا فَلَا تَحْسَبَنَّهُمْ بِمَفَازَةٍ مِنَ الْعَذَابِ وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ (١٨٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَا تَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ يَفْرَحُونَ): it is read with the yāʾ, in the third person (لَا يَحْسَبَنَّ), and likewise (فَلَا تَحْسَبَنَّهُمْ) with the yāʾ and ḍamma on the bāʾ (فَلَا يَحْسَبُنَّهُمْ). The fāʿil (agent) of the first is الَّذِينَ يَفْرَحُونَ; as for its two objects, they are omitted,
the two objects of تَحْسَبَنَّهُمْ being sufficient, because the agent in both is one; so the second verb is a repetition of the first, and this is good because the speech connected to the first has become long. The fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), so it is neither for conjunction nor for an apodosis. Some said: بِمَفَازَةٍ is the first object of the first حَسِبَ [Translator's note: so in the text; from what follows, the meaning is that بِمَفَازَةٍ is the second object of the first verb, and its first object is omitted], and its second object is omitted, indicated by the second object of the second حَسِبَ; because the implied form is: "Let not those who rejoice reckon themselves to be in safety", and هُمْ in «فَلَا تَحْسَبَنَّهُمْ» is أَنْفُسَهُمْ, i.e. "let them not reckon themselves"; and بِمَفَازَةٍ, which is the object of the first, made it unnecessary to mention it a second time for the second حَسِبَ.
This is a weak, forced view, and there is no need for it given what we mentioned in the first view.
It is read with the tāʾ in both, as an address, and with fatḥa on the bāʾ in both, the address being to the Prophet ﷺ. The account of it is that الَّذِينَ يَفْرَحُونَ is the first object, and the second is omitted because the second object of the second حَسِبَ indicates it. It is also said: the implied form is "Do not reckon those who rejoice to be in safety", and the second object here made it unnecessary to mention it for the second حَسِبَ; the second حَسِبَ is repeated, or a badal (substitute), for the reason we mentioned in the reading with the yāʾ in both, since the agent in both is also one, namely the Prophet.
It is also read with the yāʾ in the first and the tāʾ in the second. Then for the tāʾ in the second verb there are two views: one is the fatḥa [on the bāʾ], on the view that it is an address to one person, and the [other is] ḍamma, on the view that it is to a group. On this [reading] the two objects of the first verb are omitted because the two objects of the second indicate them; the fāʾ is also redundant, and the second verb is neither a badal nor a repetition, because its agent is other than the agent of the first. الْمَفَازَةُ is a mafʿala from الْفَوْز ("success, escape").
(مِنَ الْعَذَابِ): attached (mutaʿalliq) to something omitted, because it is an adjective of الْمَفَازَة, since الْمَفَازَة is a place, and a noun of place does not govern. It may also be that الْمَفَازَة is a maṣdar (verbal noun), so that «مِنَ» is attached to it, and the implied sense would be: "do not reckon them escaping", the maṣdar standing in place of the active participle.

ukberi-tibyan:191-192.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الَّذِينَ يَذْكُرُونَ اللَّهَ قِيَامًا وَقُعُودًا وَعَلَى جُنُوبِهِمْ وَيَتَفَكَّرُونَ فِي خَلْقِ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ رَبَّنَا مَا خَلَقْتَ هَذَا بَاطِلًا سُبْحَانَكَ فَقِنَا عَذَابَ النَّارِ (١٩١) رَبَّنَا إِنَّكَ مَنْ تُدْخِلِ النَّارَ فَقَدْ أَخْزَيْتَهُ وَمَا لِلظَّالِمِينَ مِنْ أَنْصَارٍ) (١٩٢).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الَّذِينَ يَذْكُرُونَ): in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of «أُولِي» [in the preceding verse]; or in the position of the accusative by an implied أَعْنِي ("I mean"); or of the nominative by an implied «هُمْ» ("they are"). It may also be a mubtadaʾ (subject) with the khabar (predicate) omitted, its implied form being: "they say: Our Lord". (قِيَامًا وَقُعُودًا): two ḥāls (circumstantials) from the agent pronoun in «يَذْكُرُونَ». (وَعَلَى جُنُوبِهِمْ): also a ḥāl; the preposition is attached (mutaʿalliq) to something omitted which is originally the ḥāl, its implied form being: "and lying on their sides". (وَيَتَفَكَّرُونَ): conjoined to يَذْكُرُونَ; it may also be a ḥāl, i.e. "they remember Allah, reflecting".
(بَاطِلًا): a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); الْبَاطِل here is a fāʿil-pattern word with the meaning of a maṣdar (verbal noun), like الْعَاقِبَة and الْعَافِيَة; the meaning is: "I did not create them in vain" [Translator's note: so in the text, «مَا خَلَقْتُهُمَا»]. It may be a ḥāl, its implied form being: "I did not create this devoid of wisdom". It may also be a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "a vain creating".
If it is asked: how did He say هَذَا, when what precedes is the mention of the heavens and the earth, and the pointing to them would be with هَذِهِ? There are three views on that. The first: that the pointing is to the creation (al-khalq) mentioned in His saying: (خَلْقِ السَّمَاوَاتِ); on this view الْخَلْق may be a maṣdar, or may mean "the created things", and it is then of the type of annexing a thing to what is itself in meaning. The second: that the heavens and the earth have the sense of "the whole" (al-jamʿ), so the pointing referred to that. The third: that the meaning is: "You did not create this thing mentioned", or "this created thing".
(فَقِنَا): the fāʾ entered for the sense of requital (jazāʾ), so the implied form is: "when we have declared You transcendent, or affirmed Your oneness, then protect us".
(مَنْ تُدْخِلِ النَّارَ): in the position of the accusative by تُدْخِلِ.
Some permitted it to be accusative by a verb indicated by the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), namely «فَقَدْ أَخْزَيْتَهُ».
And some permitted (مَنْ) to be a mubtadaʾ, with the condition and its apodosis as the khabar. On all the views, the whole sentence is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of إِنَّ.

ukberi-tibyan:28-28.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (لَا يَتَّخِذِ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ الْكَافِرِينَ أَوْلِيَاءَ مِنْ دُونِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَمَنْ يَفْعَلْ ذَلِكَ فَلَيْسَ مِنَ اللَّهِ فِي شَيْءٍ إِلَّا أَنْ تَتَّقُوا مِنْهُمْ تُقَاةً وَيُحَذِّرُكُمُ اللَّهُ نَفْسَهُ وَإِلَى اللَّهِ الْمَصِيرُ (٢٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَا يَتَّخِذِ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ): it is a prohibition. Al-Kisāʾī allowed the nominative in it as a statement, the meaning being "it is not proper [for them] to seek". (مِنْ دُونِ): in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of أولياء. (فَلَيْسَ مِنَ اللَّهِ فِي شَيْءٍ): the implied form is "then he is not in anything of the religion of Allah"; so من الله is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), because it is a naʿt of the indefinite noun placed before it.
(إِلَّا أَنْ تَتَّقُوا): this is a return from the third person to address. The position of أن تتقوا is accusative, because it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). The origin of (تُقَاةً) is وُقَيَة; the wāw was changed into tāʾ because it bears a permanent ḍamma, like تُجاه, and the yāʾ was changed into alif because it is vowelled and what precedes it has fatḥa. Its accusative is as a ḥāl. It is also read تَقِيَّة, on the pattern faʿīla, the [first] yāʾ also being a substitute for the wāw.
(وَيُحَذِّرُكُمُ اللَّهُ نَفْسَهُ): i.e. the punishment of Himself — so said al-Zajjāj. Others said there is no omission here.

ukberi-tibyan:29-29.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قُلْ إِنْ تُخْفُوا مَا فِي صُدُورِكُمْ أَوْ تُبْدُوهُ يَعْلَمْهُ اللَّهُ وَيَعْلَمُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَاللَّهُ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ (٢٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَيَعْلَمُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ): it is resumptive, and not part of the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), because He knows what is in them absolutely.

ukberi-tibyan:30-30.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (يَوْمَ تَجِدُ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ مَا عَمِلَتْ مِنْ خَيْرٍ مُحْضَرًا وَمَا عَمِلَتْ مِنْ سُوءٍ تَوَدُّ لَوْ أَنَّ بَيْنَهَا وَبَيْنَهُ أَمَدًا بَعِيدًا وَيُحَذِّرُكُمُ اللَّهُ نَفْسَهُ وَاللَّهُ رَءُوفٌ بِالْعِبَادِ (٣٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يَوْمَ تَجِدُ): يوم here is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. "remember". It has been said that it is an adverb (ẓarf) whose operator is «قدير». It has been said that its operator is «وإلى الله المصير».
And it has been said that its operator is «ويحذركم»; or "Allah warns you of His punishment on the day [each soul] finds", so that its operator is the punishment, not the warning. (مَا عَمِلَتْ): ما in it means الذي, the returning pronoun is omitted, and its position is accusative as the first object; (مُحْضَرًا) is the second object — so they have stated. The more likely view is that (مُحْضَرًا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and تجد is the one that takes a single object. (وَمَا عَمِلَتْ مِنْ سُوءٍ): there are two views on it. The first: it also means الذي, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the first, the implied form being: "and what it did of evil, also brought present". On this view (تَوَدُّ) is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, and the operator is تجد.
The second: that it is conditional, and تودّ is nominative on the basis that he intended the fāʾ, i.e. "then it wishes".
And it may be nominative without supposing any omission, because the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) here is past, and when the jussive form does not appear in the protasis, both the jussive and the nominative are permissible in the apodosis.

ukberi-tibyan:32-32.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قُلْ أَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ وَالرَّسُولَ فَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ الْكَافِرِينَ (٣٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا): it may be an address, the tāʾ having been dropped, i.e. فإن تتولّوا; it is an address like that before it.
And it may be for the third person, so its form is that of the past.

ukberi-tibyan:33-34.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنَّ اللَّهَ اصْطَفَى آدَمَ وَنُوحًا وَآلَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَآلَ عِمْرَانَ عَلَى الْعَالَمِينَ (٣٣) ذُرِّيَّةً بَعْضُهَا مِنْ بَعْضٍ وَاللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ (٣٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (ذُرِّيَّةً): we have mentioned its pattern and the readings it has. As for its accusative, it is as a badal (substitute) from نوح and the names conjoined to it. It is not permissible for it to be a badal from آدم, because he is not a progeny. It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from them, its operator being اصطفى.
(بَعْضُهَا مِنْ بَعْضٍ): mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of ذرية.

ukberi-tibyan:35-35.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِذْ قَالَتِ امْرَأَةُ عِمْرَانَ رَبِّ إِنِّي نَذَرْتُ لَكَ مَا فِي بَطْنِي مُحَرَّرًا فَتَقَبَّلْ مِنِّي إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ (٣٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِذْ قَالَتِ): it has been said that its implied form is "remember". It has been said that it is an adverb (ẓarf) for عليم. And it has been said that its operator is اصطفى, implied along with آل عمران.
(مُحَرَّرًا): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «ما», which means الذي [and ما is used] because it had not yet become one of those endowed with reason. It has been said that it is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted noun, i.e. "a boy dedicated"; they supplied "boy" only because they used to devote only males to the Holy House (Bayt al-Maqdis).

ukberi-tibyan:36-36.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَلَمَّا وَضَعَتْهَا قَالَتْ رَبِّ إِنِّي وَضَعْتُهَا أُنْثَى وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا وَضَعَتْ وَلَيْسَ الذَّكَرُ كَالْأُنْثَى وَإِنِّي سَمَّيْتُهَا مَرْيَمَ وَإِنِّي أُعِيذُهَا بِكَ وَذُرِّيَّتَهَا مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيمِ (٣٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَضَعْتُهَا أُنْثَى): أنثى is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ, or a badal (substitute) from it.
(بِمَا وَضَعَتْ): it is read with fatḥa on the ʿayn and sukūn on the tāʾ, on the basis that it is not part of her speech but parenthetical; that was permissible because of the glorification of the Lord, Exalted is He, in it. And it is read with sukūn on the ʿayn and ḍamma on the tāʾ, on the basis that it is part of her speech. The first is stronger, because the proper way in such a case would be to say: "and You know best what I have borne".
The justification for its permissibility is that she put the overt noun in place of the pronoun, for magnification.
It is also read with sukūn on the ʿayn and kasra on the tāʾ, as though someone said that to her.
(سَمَّيْتُهَا مَرْيَمَ): this verb is one that reaches the second object sometimes by itself and sometimes by a preposition; the Arabs say سمّيتُك زيدًا and بزيد ("I named you Zayd").

ukberi-tibyan:193-193.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (رَبَّنَا إِنَّنَا سَمِعْنَا مُنَادِيًا يُنَادِي لِلْإِيمَانِ أَنْ آمِنُوا بِرَبِّكُمْ فَآمَنَّا رَبَّنَا فَاغْفِرْ لَنَا ذُنُوبَنَا وَكَفِّرْ عَنَّا سَيِّئَاتِنَا وَتَوَفَّنَا مَعَ الْأَبْرَارِ) (١٩٣).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يُنَادِي): an adjective of مُنَادِيًا, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in مُنَادِيًا.
If it is asked: what is the benefit of mentioning the verb when the noun مُنَادٍ ("a caller") already indicates it? It is answered: there are three views on it. The first: it is a tawkīd (emphasis), as you say قُمْ قَائِمًا ("stand, standing"). The second: that something was connected to it which made the repetition good, namely His saying «لِلْإِيمَانِ». The third: that had He confined Himself to the noun, it would have been possible that they heard someone known for calling saying something that was not a call; so when He said يُنَادِي, it was established that they heard his calling in that state.
The object of يُنَادِي is omitted, i.e. "he called the people". (أَنْ آمِنُوا): أَنْ here has the sense of أَيْ ("that is"), so the call is his saying آمِنُوا. It may also be the maṣdariyya أَنْ joined to the imperative, so the implied form on this view would be: "calling to faith with: believe" (يُنَادِي لِلْإِيمَانِ بِأَنْ آمِنُوا). (مَعَ الْأَبْرَارِ): an adjective of the omitted object, its implied form being: "[take us] righteous along with the righteous" (أَبْرَارًا مَعَ الْأَبْرَارِ), and أَبْرَارًا on this view is a ḥāl. الْأَبْرَارُ is the plural of بَرٌّ, whose origin is بَرِرٌ, like كَتِفٌ and أَكْتَافٌ. Imāla (inclination of the vowel towards i) is permissible in الْأَبْرَار, giving preponderance to the kasra of the second rāʾ.

ukberi-tibyan:194-194.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (رَبَّنَا وَآتِنَا مَا وَعَدْتَنَا عَلَى رُسُلِكَ وَلَا تُخْزِنَا يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ إِنَّكَ لَا تُخْلِفُ الْمِيعَادَ) (١٩٤).
His saying, Exalted is He: (عَلَى رُسُلِكَ): i.e. "on the tongues of Your messengers"; «عَلَى» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to وَعَدْتَنَا, and it may be [attached] to آتِنَا. (الْمِيعَادَ): a maṣdar (verbal noun) meaning "promise" (al-waʿd).

ukberi-tibyan:195-195.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَاسْتَجَابَ لَهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ أَنِّي لَا أُضِيعُ عَمَلَ عَامِلٍ مِنْكُمْ مِنْ ذَكَرٍ أَوْ أُنْثَى بَعْضُكُمْ مِنْ بَعْضٍ فَالَّذِينَ هَاجَرُوا وَأُخْرِجُوا مِنْ دِيَارِهِمْ وَأُوذُوا فِي سَبِيلِي وَقَاتَلُوا وَقُتِلُوا لَأُكَفِّرَنَّ عَنْهُمْ سَيِّئَاتِهِمْ وَلَأُدْخِلَنَّهُمْ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ ثَوَابًا مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ وَاللَّهُ عِنْدَهُ حُسْنُ الثَّوَابِ) (١٩٥).
His saying, Exalted is He: (عَامِلٍ مِنْكُمْ): مِنْكُمْ is an adjective of عَامِلٍ. (مِنْ ذَكَرٍ أَوْ أُنْثَى): a badal (substitute) from «مِنْكُمْ», and it is the substitution of a thing for the [same] thing, the two referring to one and the same entity. It may also be that مِنْ ذَكَرٍ أَوْ أُنْثَى is another adjective of عَامِلٍ, intended for clarification. It may also be that مِنْ ذَكَرٍ is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in مِنْكُمْ, its implied form being: "settled from among you, being male or female". (بَعْضُكُمْ مِنْ بَعْضٍ): resumptive; it may also be a ḥāl or an adjective.
(فَالَّذِينَ هَاجَرُوا): a mubtadaʾ (subject), and (لَأُكَفِّرَنَّ) with what is connected to it is the khabar (predicate); it is the answer to an omitted oath. (ثَوَابًا): a maṣdar (verbal noun), whose verb is indicated by the preceding speech, because expiating misdeeds is a rewarding; so it is as though He said: "I shall surely reward you a reward". It is also said to be a ḥāl, and also said to be a tamyīz (specification); both views are Kufan.
الثَّوَابُ has the sense of "rewarding" (al-ithāba), and it may occur in the sense of the thing with which one is rewarded, as in your saying "this dirham is your reward". On this view it may be a ḥāl from الْجَنَّات, i.e. "given as a reward", or a ḥāl from the object pronoun in لَأُدْخِلَنَّهُمْ, i.e. "rewarded".
It may also be a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), because the meaning of أُدْخِلَنَّهُمْ is "I shall surely give them"; on this view it is a badal from جَنَّاتٍ. It may also be resumptive, i.e. "He gives them a reward".

ukberi-tibyan:197-197.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (مَتَاعٌ قَلِيلٌ ثُمَّ مَأْوَاهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ وَبِئْسَ الْمِهَادُ) (١٩٧).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَتَاعٌ قَلِيلٌ): i.e. "their moving about is an enjoyment", so the mubtadaʾ (subject) is omitted.

ukberi-tibyan:198-198.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَكِنِ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا رَبَّهُمْ لَهُمْ جَنَّاتٌ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا نُزُلًا مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ وَمَا عِنْدَ اللَّهِ خَيْرٌ لِلْأَبْرَارِ) (١٩٨).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَكِنِ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا): the majority read it with the nūn undoubled; it was also read with it doubled (لَكِنَّ), and the i'rab is clear. (خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in لَهُمْ, the governing element being the sense of settledness (istiqrār); «جَنَّاتٌ» is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), or by the preposition. (نُزُلًا): a maṣdar (verbal noun), accusative by the meaning, because the meaning of "they will have gardens" is "their hospitality [is gardens]". According to the Kufans it is a ḥāl or a tamyīz (specification).
It may also be the plural of نَازِلٌ ("one who alights"), as al-Aʿshā said:
أَوْ يَنْزِلُونَ فَإِنَّا مَعْشَرٌ نُزُلُ
("…or if they alight, then we are a company who alight [to fight on foot]")
Abū ʿAlī mentioned that in al-Tadhkira. On this view it may be a ḥāl from the pronoun in خَالِدِينَ. If you make it a maṣdar, it may also have the sense of a passive participle, so it is a ḥāl from the genitive pronoun in فِيهَا, i.e. "alighted in" (مَنْزُولَةً).
(مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ): if you make نُزُلًا a maṣdar, مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ is an adjective of it; if you make it a plural, there are two views on it. The first: it is a ḥāl from the omitted object, because the implied form is: "alighting in them" (نُزُلًا إِيَّاهَا). The second: that it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "that is from Allah", i.e. by His bounty.
(مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ) [Translator's note: so in the text; the words discussed are (وَمَا عِنْدَ اللَّهِ)]: مَا has the sense of الَّذِي ("that which"), and it is a mubtadaʾ. On the khabar there are two views. The first: it is خَيْرٌ, and «لِلْأَبْرَارِ» is a naʿt (adjective) of (خَيْرٌ). The second: that the khabar is (لِلْأَبْرَارِ), intended as placed first, i.e. "that which is with Allah is settled for the righteous", and خَيْرٌ on this view is a second khabar.
Some said: لِلْأَبْرَارِ is a ḥāl from the pronoun in the adverb (ẓarf), and (خَيْرٌ) is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ. This is far-fetched, because it involves separating the mubtadaʾ and the khabar by a ḥāl belonging to something else, and separating the ḥāl and the one it describes (ṣāḥib al-ḥāl) by the khabar of the mubtadaʾ; and that is not permissible in chosen [i.e. non-poetic] usage.

ukberi-tibyan:199-199.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِنَّ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ لَمَنْ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَمَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكُمْ وَمَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْهِمْ خَاشِعِينَ لِلَّهِ لَا يَشْتَرُونَ بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ ثَمَنًا قَلِيلًا أُولَئِكَ لَهُمْ أَجْرُهُمْ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَرِيعُ الْحِسَابِ) (١٩٩).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَمَنْ يُؤْمِنُ): «مَنْ» is in the position of the accusative as the noun (ism) of إِنَّ; مَنْ is an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective, or a relative noun.
(خَاشِعِينَ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in يُؤْمِنُ; it came in the plural according to the meaning of «مَنْ». It may also be a ḥāl from the hāʾ and mīm in إِلَيْهِمْ, so that the governing word is أُنْزِلَ. (لِلَّهِ): attached (mutaʿalliq) to خَاشِعِينَ. It is also said that it is attached to His saying «لَا يَشْتَرُونَ», intended as placed later, i.e. "they do not sell the signs of Allah for a small price, for the sake of Allah".
(أُولَئِكَ): a mubtadaʾ (subject); and on «لَهُمْ أَجْرُهُمْ» there are several views. The first: that His saying لَهُمْ is the khabar (predicate) of أَجْرُ, and the clause is the khabar of the first; «عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ» is an adverb (ẓarf) for الْأَجْر, because the implied sense is "they are to be rewarded with their Lord"; it may also be a ḥāl from the pronoun in لَهُمْ, which is the pronoun of الْأَجْر. The other: that الْأَجْر is nominative by the adverbial phrase, as the agent is nominative by its verb; on this view عِنْدَ may be an adverb for الْأَجْر or a ḥāl from it. The third view: that أَجْرُهُمْ is a mubtadaʾ and عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ its khabar, and لَهُمْ is attached to the settledness and permanence that the speech indicates, because it has the status of an adverb.

ukberi-tibyan:97-97.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فِيهِ آيَاتٌ بَيِّنَاتٌ مَقَامُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَمَنْ دَخَلَهُ كَانَ آمِنًا وَلِلَّهِ عَلَى النَّاسِ حِجُّ الْبَيْتِ مَنِ اسْتَطَاعَ إِلَيْهِ سَبِيلًا وَمَنْ كَفَرَ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ غَنِيٌّ عَنِ الْعَالَمِينَ (٩٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فِيهِ آيَاتٌ بَيِّنَاتٌ): the clause may be a new sentence, implicitly explaining the meaning of blessing and guidance. Its position may also be that of another ḥāl (circumstantial). It may also be a ḥāl of the pronoun in His saying «لِلْعَالَمِينَ», governed by «هُدًى». It may also be a ḥāl of the pronoun in «مُبَارَكًا», which is what governs it.
It may also be an adjective of «هُدًى», just as «لِلْعَالَمِينَ» is. And (مَقَامُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, i.e. "among them is the Station of Ibrāhīm". (وَمَنْ دَخَلَهُ) is conjoined to it, i.e. "and among them is the safety of whoever enters it". It is also said: it (مَقَامُ) is a khabar, its implied form being "they are the Station". It is also said: it is a badal (substitute). On these two views, the signs have been expressed by the Station and by the safety of the one who enters. It is also said: (وَمَنْ دَخَلَهُ) is a new sentence, and «مَنْ» is conditional. And (حِجُّ الْبَيْتِ) is a maṣdar (verbal noun) read with fatḥa and with kasra; they are two dialectal forms. It is also said: the form with kasra is a noun of the maṣdar (ism al-maṣdar). It is a mubtadaʾ, and its khabar is «عَلَى النَّاسِ». «لِلَّهِ» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to the notion of settledness (al-istiqrār) in «عَلَى», its implied form being "it is established, for Allah, upon people". The khabar may also be «لِلَّهِ», with «عَلَى النَّاسِ» attached to it, either as a ḥāl or as an object. «لِلَّهِ» cannot be a ḥāl, because on that view what governs the ḥāl would be an abstract (maʿnawī) governor, and a ḥāl does not precede an abstract governor. «الْحَجّ» may also be made nominative by the first preposition or by the second. «الْحَجّ» is a maṣdar put in construct with its object. (مَنِ اسْتَطَاعَ): a badal of «النَّاس», a badal of part from whole. It is also said: it is in the position of the nominative, its implied form being "they are whoever is able", "and the one on whom it is obligatory is whoever is able", the clause also being a badal. It is also said: it is nominative as the agent of «الْحَجّ», its implied form being "and it is due to Allah from people that whoever is able should perform pilgrimage to the House". On this view there is an omission in the wording, its implied form being "whoever is able among them", so that the clause contains a pronoun referring back to the first (noun). It is also said: «مَنْ» is a conditional mubtadaʾ and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, its implied form being "whoever is able, let him perform the pilgrimage"; this is indicated by His saying (وَمَنْ كَفَرَ) and its apodosis.

ukberi-tibyan:99-99.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قُلْ يَا أَهْلَ الْكِتَابِ لِمَ تَصُدُّونَ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ مَنْ آمَنَ تَبْغُونَهَا عِوَجًا وَأَنْتُمْ شُهَدَاءُ وَمَا اللَّهُ بِغَافِلٍ عَمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ (٩٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لِمَ تَصُدُّونَ): the lām is attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb, and «مَنْ» is its object. [Translator's note: the source prints «مِنْ»; the word in the verse is «مَنْ».] And (تَبْغُونَهَا) may be a new sentence, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in «تَصُدُّونَ», or of «السَّبِيل», because it contains two pronouns referring back to them both; that is why it is valid to make it a ḥāl of each of them.
And (عِوَجًا) is a ḥāl.

ukberi-tibyan:100-100.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِنْ تُطِيعُوا فَرِيقًا مِنَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ يَرُدُّوكُمْ بَعْدَ إِيمَانِكُمْ كَافِرِينَ (١٠٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بَعْدَ إِيمَانِكُمْ): it may be an adverb (ẓarf) of «يَرُدُّوكُمْ», or an adverb of (كَافِرِينَ); in meaning it is like His saying (كَفَرُوا بَعْدَ إِيمَانِهِمْ).

ukberi-tibyan:103-103.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَاعْتَصِمُوا بِحَبْلِ اللَّهِ جَمِيعًا وَلَا تَفَرَّقُوا وَاذْكُرُوا نِعْمَةَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ إِذْ كُنْتُمْ أَعْدَاءً فَأَلَّفَ بَيْنَ قُلُوبِكُمْ فَأَصْبَحْتُمْ بِنِعْمَتِهِ إِخْوَانًا وَكُنْتُمْ عَلَى شَفَا حُفْرَةٍ مِنَ النَّارِ فَأَنْقَذَكُمْ مِنْهَا كَذَلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ آيَاتِهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَهْتَدُونَ (١٠٣)).
On His saying (وَلَا تَفَرَّقُوا): the original is «تَتَفَرَّقُوا»; the second tāʾ was dropped, and the reasoning for this has been mentioned in al-Baqara. It is also read with a doubled tāʾ, and the explanation is that (the reader) gave the first tāʾ a sukūn, treating it as joined to the (preceding) alif, and then assimilated. (نِعْمَةَ اللَّهِ): it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) put in construct with its agent. And (عَلَيْكُمْ) may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to it, as you say «أَنْعَمْتُ عَلَيْكَ» ("I bestowed favour upon you"); or it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «النِّعْمَة», in which case it is attached to something omitted. (إِذْ كُنْتُمْ): it may be an adverb (ẓarf) of «النِّعْمَة», or an adverb of the notion of settledness (al-istiqrār) in «عَلَيْكُمْ», if you make that a ḥāl. (فَأَصْبَحْتُمْ): it may be the incomplete (nāqiṣa) verb; on this view the khabar (predicate) may be «بِنِعْمَتِهِ», the meaning being "and you came to be in His favour", or "involved in His favour", or "encompassed (by it)". (إِخْوَانًا) is then a ḥāl, governed by «أَصْبَحَ» or by what the preposition is attached to. (إِخْوَانًا) may also be the khabar of «أَصْبَحَ», with the prepositional phrase a ḥāl governed by «أَصْبَحَ», or a ḥāl of «إِخْوَان», because it is an adjective of it put before it; or attached to «أَصْبَحَ», because the incomplete verb governs prepositional phrases. It may also be attached to (إِخْوَانًا), because the implied wording is "you became brothers through His favour". «أَصْبَحَ» may also be complete (tāmma), in which case the discussion of «بِنِعْمَتِهِ إِخْوَانًا» is close to the discussion under the incomplete verb.
«الْإِخْوَان» is the plural of «أَخ» in the sense of friendship, not of kinship.
«الشَّفَا» is written with alif, and it is from wāw (as the final radical); its dual is «شَفَوَانِ».
And {مِنَ النَّارِ} is an adjective of «حُفْرَة»; «مِنْ» is partitive, and the pronoun in {مِنْهَا} refers to the Fire or to the pit.

ukberi-tibyan:104-104.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلْتَكُنْ مِنْكُمْ أُمَّةٌ يَدْعُونَ إِلَى الْخَيْرِ وَيَأْمُرُونَ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ وَيَنْهَوْنَ عَنِ الْمُنْكَرِ وَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ (١٠٤)).
(وَلْتَكُنْ مِنْكُمْ): «كَانَ» here may be the complete (tāmma) one, in which case «أُمَّةٌ» is the fāʿil (agent) and «يَدْعُونَ» its adjective; and «مِنْكُمْ» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «تَكُنْ», or to something omitted, on the view that it is an adjective of «أُمَّة» put before it, which thereby became a ḥāl (circumstantial).
It may also be the incomplete (nāqiṣa) one, with «أُمَّةٌ» its noun and «يَدْعُونَ» the khabar (predicate); «مِنْكُمْ» is then either a ḥāl of «أُمَّة» or attached to the incomplete «كَانَ». «يَدْعُونَ» may also be an adjective, with «مِنْكُمْ» the khabar.

ukberi-tibyan:105-105.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَا تَكُونُوا كَالَّذِينَ تَفَرَّقُوا وَاخْتَلَفُوا مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا جَاءَهُمُ الْبَيِّنَاتُ وَأُولَئِكَ لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ (١٠٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَجَاءَهُمُ الْبَيِّنَاتُ): the tāʾ (of the feminine) was dropped only because the femininity of «الْبَيِّنَة» is not real, and because it has the sense of «الدَّلِيل» ("the proof"). [Translator's note: the source quotes the words with «وَ»; in this verse they read «مَا جَاءَهُمُ الْبَيِّنَاتُ».]

ukberi-tibyan:106-106.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَوْمَ تَبْيَضُّ وُجُوهٌ وَتَسْوَدُّ وُجُوهٌ فَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ اسْوَدَّتْ وُجُوهُهُمْ أَكَفَرْتُمْ بَعْدَ إِيمَانِكُمْ فَذُوقُوا الْعَذَابَ بِمَا كُنْتُمْ تَكْفُرُونَ (١٠٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يَوْمَ تَبْيَضُّ): it is an adverb (ẓarf) of «عَظِيم», or of the notion of settledness (al-istiqrār) in «لَهُمْ». In «تَبْيَضُّ» there are four dialectal forms: fatḥa and kasra on the tāʾ without alif, and «تَبْيَاضُّ» with alif, with fatḥa and kasra on the tāʾ; and likewise «تَسْوَدُّ».
(أَكَفَرْتُمْ): its implied form is "then it will be said to them: did you disbelieve?", and what is omitted is the khabar (predicate) (of «الَّذِينَ»).

ukberi-tibyan:108-108.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (تِلْكَ آيَاتُ اللَّهِ نَتْلُوهَا عَلَيْكَ بِالْحَقِّ وَمَا اللَّهُ يُرِيدُ ظُلْمًا لِلْعَالَمِينَ (١٠٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (تِلْكَ آيَاتُ اللَّهِ): this has been mentioned in al-Baqara.

ukberi-tibyan:110-110.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (كُنْتُمْ خَيْرَ أُمَّةٍ أُخْرِجَتْ لِلنَّاسِ تَأْمُرُونَ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ وَتَنْهَوْنَ عَنِ الْمُنْكَرِ وَتُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَلَوْ آمَنَ أَهْلُ الْكِتَابِ لَكَانَ خَيْرًا لَهُمْ مِنْهُمُ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ وَأَكْثَرُهُمُ الْفَاسِقُونَ (١١٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (كُنْتُمْ خَيْرَ أُمَّةٍ): it is said: "you were (so) in My knowledge". It is also said: it means "you have become". It is also said: «كَانَ» is redundant (zāʾida), the implied wording being «أَنْتُمْ خَيْرَ» — and this is a mistake, because «كَانَ» is not added as redundant at the beginning of a sentence, nor (if redundant) would it govern «خَيْر» (in the accusative). (تَأْمُرُونَ): a second khabar (predicate), or an explanation of the khabar, or a new sentence.
(لَكَانَ خَيْرًا لَهُمْ): i.e. "belief would have been (better)": the form of the verb (آمَنَ) with the maṣdar (verbal noun) intended. (مِنْهُمُ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ): it is a new sentence.

ukberi-tibyan:111-111.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَنْ يَضُرُّوكُمْ إِلَّا أَذًى وَإِنْ يُقَاتِلُوكُمْ يُوَلُّوكُمُ الْأَدْبَارَ ثُمَّ لَا يُنْصَرُونَ (١١١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِلَّا أَذًى): «أَذًى» is a maṣdar (verbal noun) from the meaning of «يَضُرُّوكُمْ», because «الْأَذَى» (hurt) and «الضَّرَر» (harm) are close in meaning; on this view the exception is connected (muttaṣil). It is also said: it is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ), because the meaning is "they will not harm you with defeat, but they will hurt you when you set out to fight them". (يُوَلُّوكُمُ الْأَدْبَارَ): «الْأَدْبَار» is a second object, and the meaning is "they will make their backs face you".
(ثُمَّ لَا يُنْصَرُونَ): a new sentence. According to some of them, the jussive is not permissible here by conjunction to the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), because the apodosis occurs immediately after what is conditioned, while «ثُمَّ» is for delay; for that reason it is not fit for the apodosis, and what is conjoined to the apodosis is like the apodosis. This is a mistake, because the jussive in the like of it has come in His saying (ثُمَّ لَا يَكُونُوا أَمْثَالَكُمْ). It was made a new sentence here only to indicate that Allah will not help them, whether they fight or do not fight.

ukberi-tibyan:112-112.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ضُرِبَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ الذِّلَّةُ أَيْنَ مَا ثُقِفُوا إِلَّا بِحَبْلٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَحَبْلٍ مِنَ النَّاسِ وَبَاءُوا بِغَضَبٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَضُرِبَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ الْمَسْكَنَةُ ذَلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ كَانُوا يَكْفُرُونَ بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ وَيَقْتُلُونَ الْأَنْبِيَاءَ بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ ذَلِكَ بِمَا عَصَوْا وَكَانُوا يَعْتَدُونَ (١١٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِلَّا بِحَبْلٍ): in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), its implied form being: "humiliation has been laid upon them in every state, except in the state of a covenant being concluded for them". So the bāʾ is attached (mutaʿalliq) to something omitted, its implied form being "except holding fast to a rope".

ukberi-tibyan:113-113.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَيْسُوا سَوَاءً مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ أُمَّةٌ قَائِمَةٌ يَتْلُونَ آيَاتِ اللَّهِ آنَاءَ اللَّيْلِ وَهُمْ يَسْجُدُونَ (١١٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَيْسُوا): the wāw is the noun of «لَيْسَ», referring back to those mentioned before it, and (سَوَاءً) is its khabar (predicate), i.e. "they are not equal". Then He began anew, saying (مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ أُمَّةٌ قَائِمَةٌ): «أُمَّةٌ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), «قَائِمَةٌ» a naʿt (adjective) of it, and the prepositional phrase before it is its khabar. «أُمَّةٌ» may also be the agent of the prepositional phrase. The overt noun has been put here in the place of the pronoun, the original being «مِنْهُمْ أُمَّةٌ». It is also said: «أُمَّةٌ» is made nominative by «سَوَاء»; this is weak in meaning and in iʿrāb, because it is cut off from what precedes it, and the clause cannot validly be the khabar of «لَيْسَ». It is also said: «أُمَّةٌ» is the noun of «لَيْسَ», and the wāw in it is a particle indicating plurality, as they said «أَكَلُونِي الْبَرَاغِيثُ» ("the fleas ate me"), with «سَوَاء» the khabar. This is weak, since the purpose is not to show disparity within the upright community that recites the signs of Allah; rather the purpose is that among the People of the Book there are believers and disbelievers. (يَتْلُونَ): another adjective of «أُمَّة». It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in «قَائِمَة», or of «الْأُمَّة», because it has been qualified; on this view what governs it is the notion of settledness (al-istiqrār).
And (آنَاءَ اللَّيْلِ) is an adverb (ẓarf) of «يَتْلُونَ», not of «قَائِمَة», because «قَائِمَة» has been qualified, so it does not govern what comes after the adjective. The singular of «الْآنَاء» is «إِنًى», like «مِعًى»; some pronounce the hamza with fatḥa, so it becomes on the pattern of «عَصًا» (أَنًى); and some say «إِنْيٌ» with yāʾ and kasra on the hamza. (وَهُمْ يَسْجُدُونَ): a ḥāl of the pronoun in «يَتْلُونَ» or in «قَائِمَةٌ». It may also be a new sentence. Likewise «يُؤْمِنُونَ», «وَيَأْمُرُونَ» and «وَيَنْهَوْنَ» (in the next verse): if you wish you may make them ḥāls, and if you wish you may make them new sentences.

ukberi-tibyan:115-115.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا يَفْعَلُوا مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَلَنْ يُكْفَرُوهُ وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِالْمُتَّقِينَ (١١٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَمَا يَفْعَلُوا): it is read with tāʾ, in the second person, and with yāʾ, by analogy with what precedes it.

ukberi-tibyan:117-117.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (مَثَلُ مَا يُنْفِقُونَ فِي هَذِهِ الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا كَمَثَلِ رِيحٍ فِيهَا صِرٌّ أَصَابَتْ حَرْثَ قَوْمٍ ظَلَمُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ فَأَهْلَكَتْهُ وَمَا ظَلَمَهُمُ اللَّهُ وَلَكِنْ أَنْفُسَهُمْ يَظْلِمُونَ (١١٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (كَمَثَلِ رِيحٍ): there is an omitted muḍāf in it, its implied form being "like the likeness of what a wind destroys", i.e. what they spend perishes like that which it destroys. (فِيهَا صِرٌّ): a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) in the position of an adjective of «الرِّيح». You may also make «صِرٌّ» nominative by the adverbial phrase, because it is supported by what precedes it. And (أَصَابَتْ) is likewise in the position of the genitive as an adjective of «رِيح»; it cannot be an adjective of (صِرٌّ), because «الصِّرّ» is masculine while the pronoun in «أَصَابَتْ» is feminine. It is also said: there is no omitted muḍāf in the phrase; rather, what they spent is likened by the meaning of the whole phrase. That is because His saying (كَمَثَلِ رِيحٍ. . . .) up to His saying (فَأَهْلَكَتْهُ) is connected, one part with another, so the meanings in it are blended and the meaning is understood. (ظَلَمُوا): an adjective of «قَوْم».

ukberi-tibyan:118-118.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تَتَّخِذُوا بِطَانَةً مِنْ دُونِكُمْ لَا يَأْلُونَكُمْ خَبَالًا وَدُّوا مَا عَنِتُّمْ قَدْ بَدَتِ الْبَغْضَاءُ مِنْ أَفْوَاهِهِمْ وَمَا تُخْفِي صُدُورُهُمْ أَكْبَرُ قَدْ بَيَّنَّا لَكُمُ الْآيَاتِ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ (١١٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْ دُونِكُمْ): an adjective of «بِطَانَة». It is said that «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida), because the meaning is "intimates other than you (or: beneath you) in practice and faith". (لَا يَأْلُونَكُمْ): in the position of a naʿt (adjective) of «بِطَانَة», or of a ḥāl (circumstantial) of what «مِنْ» is attached to. «يَأْلُو» takes one object. And (خَبَالًا) is by way of tamyīz (specification). It may also have become accusative through the dropping of the preposition, its implied form being "they will spare no effort against you in corrupting you". It may also be a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl. (وَدُّوا): a new sentence. It may also be a ḥāl of the pronoun in «يَأْلُونَكُمْ», with «قَدْ» intended along with it; and «مَا» is maṣdariyya (verbal-noun-forming), i.e. "your distress". (قَدْ بَدَتِ الْبَغْضَاءُ): also a ḥāl; and it may be a new sentence. (مِنْ أَفْوَاهِهِمْ): an object of «بَدَتْ», and «مِنْ» is for the starting point (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya). It may also be a ḥāl, i.e. "it has appeared, coming out of their mouths".

ukberi-tibyan:119-119.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (هَا أَنْتُمْ أُولَاءِ تُحِبُّونَهُمْ وَلَا يُحِبُّونَكُمْ وَتُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْكِتَابِ كُلِّهِ وَإِذَا لَقُوكُمْ قَالُوا آمَنَّا وَإِذَا خَلَوْا عَضُّوا عَلَيْكُمُ الْأَنَامِلَ مِنَ الْغَيْظِ قُلْ مُوتُوا بِغَيْظِكُمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ بِذَاتِ الصُّدُورِ (١١٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (هَا أَنْتُمْ أُولَاءِ تُحِبُّونَهُمْ): its iʿrāb has been mentioned under His saying (ثُمَّ أَنْتُمْ هَؤُلَاءِ تَقْتُلُونَ أَنْفُسَكُمْ). (بِالْكِتَابِ كُلِّهِ): «الْكِتَاب» here is generic, i.e. "in all the Books"; it is also said: it is a single (Book). (عَضُّوا عَلَيْكُمُ): «عَلَيْكُمْ» is an object of «عَضُّوا». It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "furious against you". (مِنَ الْغَيْظِ): also attached (mutaʿalliq) to «عَضُّوا», and «مِنْ» is for the starting point, i.e. "on account of rage"; it may also be a ḥāl, i.e. "enraged".
