(بِغَيْظِكُمْ): it may be an object, as you say «مَاتَ بِالسُّمِّ» ("he died of poison"), i.e. because of it; it may also be a ḥāl, i.e. "die enraged".

ukberi-tibyan:120-120.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنْ تَمْسَسْكُمْ حَسَنَةٌ تَسُؤْهُمْ وَإِنْ تُصِبْكُمْ سَيِّئَةٌ يَفْرَحُوا بِهَا وَإِنْ تَصْبِرُوا وَتَتَّقُوا لَا يَضُرُّكُمْ كَيْدُهُمْ شَيْئًا إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِمَا يَعْمَلُونَ مُحِيطٌ (١٢٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَا يَضُرُّكُمْ): it is read with kasra on the ḍād and a sukūn on the rāʾ (لَا يَضِرْكُمْ), as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); it is from «ضَارَ يَضِيرُ ضَيْرًا», meaning "to harm", and one also says «ضَارَّهُ يَضُورُهُ» with wāw. [Translator's note: the form with wāw is normally given as «ضَارَهُ يَضُورُهُ», without doubling.] It is also read with ḍamma on the ḍād and a doubled rāʾ with ḍamma, from «ضَرَّ يَضُرُّ», and there are three views on its being nominative. The first: that it is intended to be placed earlier, i.e. "their scheming will not harm you at all if you are God-fearing"; this is the view of Sībawayh. The second: that it involves the omission of the fāʾ (of the apodosis); this is the view of al-Mubarrad. On these two views the ḍamma is an inflectional ending. The third: that it is not an inflectional ending; rather, when (the speaker) was forced to give (the final rāʾ) a vowel, he gave it ḍamma to harmonise with the ḍamma of the ḍād. It is also said: he vowelled it with the inflectional vowel to which it was originally entitled. It is also read with fatḥa on the rāʾ, as a jussive that was given fatḥa because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, since fatḥa is lighter than ḍamma and kasra. (شَيْئًا): a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "(any) harm".

ukberi-tibyan:37-37.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَتَقَبَّلَهَا رَبُّهَا بِقَبُولٍ حَسَنٍ وَأَنْبَتَهَا نَبَاتًا حَسَنًا وَكَفَّلَهَا زَكَرِيَّا كُلَّمَا دَخَلَ عَلَيْهَا زَكَرِيَّا الْمِحْرَابَ وَجَدَ عِنْدَهَا رِزْقًا قَالَ يَا مَرْيَمُ أَنَّى لَكِ هَذَا قَالَتْ هُوَ مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَرْزُقُ مَنْ يَشَاءُ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ (٣٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَأَنْبَتَهَا نَبَاتًا حَسَنًا): here it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) not on the wording of the verb mentioned, and it stands in for إثبات [Translator's note: so in the text; the sense requires إنبات, "causing to grow"].
It has been said that the implied form is "so she grew a growing"; النَّبْت and النَّبات have the same meaning, and both are sometimes used for that which grows.
تقبّلها: i.e. "He accepted her". It is read in the form of a supplication in تقبَّلْها, أنبِتْها and كفِّلْها, with ربَّها in the accusative, i.e. "O her Lord", and «زكريا» as the second object.
In the well-known [reading] كفَلها is read with fatḥa on the fāʾ. It has also been read with kasra on it, which is a dialectal form; one says كفِل يكفَل like علِم يعلَم.
And it is read with doubling of the fāʾ, the fāʿil (agent) being Allah and زكريا the object.
The hamza of زكرياء is for the feminine, since it is neither converted, nor extra for amplification, nor for attachment (ilḥāq).
There are four dialectal forms of it: this is one of them. The second: the shortened form [زكريّا]. The third: زكريّ, with a doubled yāʾ and without alif. The fourth: زكر, without yāʾ. (كُلَّمَا): we have mentioned its i'rab at the beginning of al-Baqara.
(الْمِحْرَابَ) is the object of دخل. The proper way for «دخل» is to be made transitive with في or إلى, but latitude was taken with it, so it was made to reach the object by itself. (عِنْدَهَا) may be an adverb (ẓarf) for وجد, and may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الرزق, being originally a naʿt (adjective) of it, i.e. "provision being with her". (وَجَدَ) is the one that takes a single object, and it is the response of كلما.
As for (قَالَ يَامَرْيَمُ أَنَّى لَكِ), it is resumptive; for that reason He did not conjoin it with the fāʾ, and likewise «قالت هو من عند الله». It is not permissible for قال to be a badal (substitute) from وجد, because it does not have its meaning.
And the implied form may be فقال, the fāʾ being dropped as it is dropped in the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), as in His saying (وَإِنْ أَطَعْتُمُوهُمْ إِنَّكُمْ لَمُشْرِكُونَ), and likewise the saying of the poet:
مَنْ يَفْعَلِ الْحَسَنَاتِ اللَّهُ يَشْكُرُهَا
(Whoever does good deeds, Allah will be grateful for them.)
This place resembles the apodosis of a condition, because «كلما» resembles the condition in requiring a response.
(هَذَا) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and أنّى its khabar (predicate), the implied form being "from where", and «لكِ» is for clarification (tabyīn).
And هذا may be nominative by لك, with أنّى an adverb for the [implied] settledness (istiqrār).

ukberi-tibyan:38-38.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (هُنَالِكَ دَعَا زَكَرِيَّا رَبَّهُ قَالَ رَبِّ هَبْ لِي مِنْ لَدُنْكَ ذُرِّيَّةً طَيِّبَةً إِنَّكَ سَمِيعُ الدُّعَاءِ (٣٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (هُنَالِكَ): most often هنا occurs as an adverb of place (ẓarf makān), which is its origin; here it has occurred for time, so in that it is like عند, for you make it [refer to] time though its origin is place, as in your saying "I came to you at (عند) sunrise".
It has been said that هنا [here] is place, i.e. "in that place Zakariyyā prayed". The kāf is a particle of address, and by it هنا comes to denote the place far from you; the lām entered for added distance, and it was given kasra according to the basic rule for the meeting of two quiescent letters — it and the alif before it.
It has been said that it was given kasra so as not to be confused with the lām of possession. If you drop the kāf and say «هنا», it is for the present place. The operator on هنا is «دعا».
(قَالَ): like (قَالَ يَامَرْيَمُ أَنَّى لَكِ).
(مِنْ لَدُنْكَ) may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to هب لي, so «من» is for the starting point of the giving.
And it may originally be a naʿt (adjective) of (ذُرِّيَّةً), placed first and so made accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).
(سَمِيعُ) means سامع ("hearer").

ukberi-tibyan:39-39.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَنَادَتْهُ الْمَلَائِكَةُ وَهُوَ قَائِمٌ يُصَلِّي فِي الْمِحْرَابِ أَنَّ اللَّهَ يُبَشِّرُكَ بِيَحْيَى مُصَدِّقًا بِكَلِمَةٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَسَيِّدًا وَحَصُورًا وَنَبِيًّا مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ (٣٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَنَادَتْهُ): the majority keep the tāʾ of the feminine, because the angels are a group.
Some disliked the tāʾ because it is for the feminine, and the people of the Jāhiliyya claimed that the angels are females; therefore some read (فَنَادَاهُ) without tāʾ. The reading with it is good, because الملائكة is a plural; but what they gave as a reason is of no account, because there is consensus on keeping the tāʾ in His saying (وَإِذْ قَالَتِ الْمَلَائِكَةُ يَا مَرْيَمُ). وهو قائم is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ in نادته. (يُصَلِّي) is a ḥāl from the pronoun in قائم.
And it may be in the position of the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of قائم.
(أَنَّ اللَّهَ): it is read with fatḥa on the hamza, i.e. بأن الله, and with kasra on it, i.e. "she said: Allah…", because calling is speech. (يُبَشِّرُكَ): the majority read it with doubling.
It is read with fatḥa on the yāʾ and ḍamma on the shīn, without doubling, and with ḍamma on the yāʾ and kasra on the shīn, also without doubling; one says بَشَرْتُه, بشّرتُه and أبشرتُه, and from this is His saying (وَأَبْشِرُوا بِالْجَنَّةِ).
(يَحْيَى): a foreign name. It has been said that he was named with the verb whose past is حَيِيَ.
(مُصَدِّقًا) is a ḥāl from him. (وَسَيِّدًا وَحَصُورًا وَنَبِيًّا): likewise.

ukberi-tibyan:40-40.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ رَبِّ أَنَّى يَكُونُ لِي غُلَامٌ وَقَدْ بَلَغَنِيَ الْكِبَرُ وَامْرَأَتِي عَاقِرٌ قَالَ كَذَلِكَ اللَّهُ يَفْعَلُ مَا يَشَاءُ (٤٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (غُلَامٌ): the noun of يكون, and لي is its khabar (predicate).
And it may be the fāʿil (agent) of يكون, on the basis that it is complete (tāmma); then لي is attached (mutaʿalliq) to it or is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «غلام», i.e. "«أنّى» shall a boy come to be for me?" أنّى means "how" or "from where".
(بَلَغَنِيَ الْكِبَرُ), and in another place (بَلَغْتُ مِنَ الْكِبَرِ): the meaning is the same, because whatever has reached you, you have reached it. (عَاقِرٌ): i.e. possessed of barrenness, so it is by way of relation (nasab); in meaning it is passive, i.e. "made barren"; for that reason the tāʾ of the feminine was not attached. (كَذَلِكَ): in the position of the accusative, i.e. "He does what He wills, with a doing like that".

ukberi-tibyan:41-41.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ رَبِّ اجْعَلْ لِي آيَةً قَالَ آيَتُكَ أَلَّا تُكَلِّمَ النَّاسَ ثَلَاثَةَ أَيَّامٍ إِلَّا رَمْزًا وَاذْكُرْ رَبَّكَ كَثِيرًا وَسَبِّحْ بِالْعَشِيِّ وَالْإِبْكَارِ (٤١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (اجْعَلْ لِي آيَةً): i.e. "make for me", so آية is the first object and لي the second object.
(آيَتُكَ) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and (أَلَّا تُكَلِّمَ) is its khabar (predicate). If تكلّمُ has been read in the nominative, it is permissible on the implied form "that you will not speak", as in His saying (أَلَّا يَرْجِعُ إِلَيْهِمْ قَوْلًا).
(إِلَّا رَمْزًا): an exception from a different genus (istithnāʾ min ghayr al-jins), because gesturing is not speech.
The majority read it with fatḥa on the rāʾ and sukūn on the mīm, and it is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of رمز. It is read with ḍamma on it [رُمُزًا], and that is the plural of رُمُزة, with two ḍammas; that was retained in the plural.
And it may originally have had a quiescent mīm, the ḍamma only following the ḍamma [as vowel harmony].
And it may be a maṣdar, not a plural, given ḍamma for harmony (itbāʿ), like اليُسْر and اليُسُر.
(كَثِيرًا): i.e. a frequent remembrance. (الْعَشِيِّ) is singular; it has been said that it is the plural of عشيّة.
(وَالْإِبْكَارِ): a maṣdar, the implied form being "and the time of إبكار"; one says أبكر when one enters the early morning.

ukberi-tibyan:42-42.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَإِذْ قَالَتِ الْمَلَائِكَةُ يَا مَرْيَمُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ اصْطَفَاكِ وَطَهَّرَكِ وَاصْطَفَاكِ عَلَى نِسَاءِ الْعَالَمِينَ (٤٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَإِذْ قَالَتِ): its implied form is "and remember when [the angels] said"; or, if you wish, it is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to (إِذْ قَالَتِ امْرَأَةُ عِمْرَانَ). The origin of اصطفى is اصتفى; then the tāʾ was changed into ṭāʾ to agree with the ṣād in velarisation (iṭbāq).
اصطفى was repeated either for emphasis or to make clear over whom He chose her.

ukberi-tibyan:44-44.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (ذَلِكَ مِنْ أَنْبَاءِ الْغَيْبِ نُوحِيهِ إِلَيْكَ وَمَا كُنْتَ لَدَيْهِمْ إِذْ يُلْقُونَ أَقْلَامَهُمْ أَيُّهُمْ يَكْفُلُ مَرْيَمَ وَمَا كُنْتَ لَدَيْهِمْ إِذْ يَخْتَصِمُونَ (٤٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (ذَلِكَ مِنْ أَنْبَاءِ الْغَيْبِ): the implied form may be "the matter is that"; on this view «من أنباء الغيب» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from ذا. And ذلك may be a mubtadaʾ (subject) with من أنباء its khabar (predicate).
And «نوحيه» may be the khabar of ذلك, with (مِنْ أَنْبَاءِ) a ḥāl from the hāʾ in نوحيه.
And it may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to نوحيه, i.e. the revelation [of it] is begun from the tidings of the unseen.
(إِذْ يُلْقُونَ): an adverb (ẓarf) for كان; and it may be an adverb for the [implied] settledness (istiqrār) to which لديهم is attached.
الأقلام is the plural of قلم, and قلم means "that which is pared", i.e. cut, like النَّقْض meaning "the undone thing" and القَبْض meaning "the thing seized".
(أَيُّهُمْ يَكْفُلُ مَرْيَمَ): mubtadaʾ and khabar in the position of the accusative, i.e. "they cast lots [to determine] which of them…"; so its operator is what «يلقون» indicates. (إِذْ يَخْتَصِمُونَ) is like (إِذْ يُلْقُونَ).
يختصمون has the meaning of اختصموا ("they disputed"), and likewise يلقون, i.e. ألقوا ("they cast"). And it may be that He is narrating the situation [as present].

ukberi-tibyan:45-45.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِذْ قَالَتِ الْمَلَائِكَةُ يَا مَرْيَمُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُبَشِّرُكِ بِكَلِمَةٍ مِنْهُ اسْمُهُ الْمَسِيحُ عِيسَى ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ وَجِيهًا فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ وَمِنَ الْمُقَرَّبِينَ (٤٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِذْ قَالَتِ الْمَلَائِكَةُ): إذ is a badal (substitute) from the إذا before it [Translator's note: so in the text; the preceding word in verse 44 is إذ].
And it may be an adverb (ẓarf) for يختصمون, and the implied form may be "remember". (مِنْهُ): in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of الكلمة; من here is for the starting point.
(اسْمُهُ) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), «المسيح» its khabar (predicate), and «عيسى» a badal from it or an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition).
It is not permissible for it to be another khabar, because multiple khabars require a multiple mubtadaʾ [in meaning], whereas the mubtadaʾ here is singular, namely His saying اسمه; had عيسى been another khabar, it would have been أسماؤه, or أسماؤها with reference to the femininity of الكلمة. The clause is a naʿt of كلمة. (ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "he is the son of…".
It is not permissible for it to be a badal from what precedes it, nor a naʿt, because ابن مريم is not a name. Do you not see that you do not say "the name of this man is Ibn ʿAmr" unless it has been attached to him as a proper name?
The pronoun in اسمه was made masculine only according to the meaning of الكلمة, because what is meant by يبشرك is [tidings] of a being brought into existence, or a created one. (وَجِيهًا - وَمِنَ الْمُقَرَّبِينَ - وَيُكَلِّمُ): anticipated ḥāls (aḥwāl muqaddara), whose owner is the meaning of الكلمة, which is "one brought into existence" or "created". It is permissible for the ḥāl to be accusative from it though it is indefinite, because it has been qualified.
It is not permissible for them to be ḥāls from المسيح, nor from عيسى, nor from ابن مريم, because these are khabars, and the operator on them is the inception (ibtidāʾ), or the mubtadaʾ, or both, and none of these operates on a ḥāl.
Nor is it permissible for them to be ḥāls from the hāʾ in اسمه, because of the separation occurring between them and the absence of an operator for the ḥāl.

ukberi-tibyan:46-46.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَيُكَلِّمُ النَّاسَ فِي الْمَهْدِ وَكَهْلًا وَمِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ (٤٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فِي الْمَهْدِ): it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in يكلم, i.e. "he speaks to them while small"; and it may be an adverb (ẓarf).
(وَكَهْلًا): it may be a ḥāl conjoined to وجيهًا, and it may be conjoined to the position of «في المهد» if you make that a ḥāl. (وَمِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ): a ḥāl conjoined to وجيهًا.

ukberi-tibyan:121-121.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذْ غَدَوْتَ مِنْ أَهْلِكَ تُبَوِّئُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ مَقَاعِدَ لِلْقِتَالِ وَاللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ (١٢١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَإِذْ غَدَوْتَ): i.e. "and remember (when)". (مِنْ أَهْلِكَ): «مِنْ» is for the starting point (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya), and the implied wording is "from among your family"; its position is accusative, its implied form being "you left your family". And (تُبَوِّئُ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial). It takes one object directly, and another sometimes directly and sometimes through a preposition. Of the first kind is this verse: the first object is «الْمُؤْمِنِينَ» and the second «مَقَاعِدَ». Of the second kind is (وَإِذْ بَوَّأْنَا لِإِبْرَاهِيمَ مَكَانَ الْبَيْتِ); it is also said that the lām there is redundant (zāʾida). (لِلْقِتَالِ): attached (mutaʿalliq) to (تُبَوِّئُ). It may also be attached to something omitted, on the view that it is an adjective of «مَقَاعِد». It cannot be attached to «مَقَاعِد», because «الْمَقْعَد» here is the place, and that does not govern.

ukberi-tibyan:122-122.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِذْ هَمَّتْ طَائِفَتَانِ مِنْكُمْ أَنْ تَفْشَلَا وَاللَّهُ وَلِيُّهُمَا وَعَلَى اللَّهِ فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ (١٢٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِذْ هَمَّتْ): «إِذْ» is an adverb (ẓarf) of (عَلِيمٌ). It may also be an adverb of (تُبَوِّئُ), or of (غَدَوْتَ). (أَنْ تَفْشَلَا): its implied form is «بِأَنْ تَفْشَلَا»; so its position is accusative or genitive, according to the disagreement we have mentioned. (وَعَلَى): attached (mutaʿalliq) to «يَتَوَكَّلْ»; the fāʾ entered because of the meaning of condition, the meaning being: "if they lose heart, then you put your trust (in Allah)", and "if the matter becomes hard, then put your trust".

ukberi-tibyan:123-123.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَقَدْ نَصَرَكُمُ اللَّهُ بِبَدْرٍ وَأَنْتُمْ أَذِلَّةٌ فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ (١٢٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بِبَدْرٍ): an adverb (ẓarf), the bāʾ being in the sense of «فِي». It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial). And (أَذِلَّةً) is the plural of «ذَلِيل»; this pattern comes only to avoid the repetition of the lām that would occur in «ذُلُلًا». [Translator's note: the source quotes «أَذِلَّةً» in the accusative; in the verse it is «أَذِلَّةٌ».]

ukberi-tibyan:124-125.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِذْ تَقُولُ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَلَنْ يَكْفِيَكُمْ أَنْ يُمِدَّكُمْ رَبُّكُمْ بِثَلَاثَةِ آلَافٍ مِنَ الْمَلَائِكَةِ مُنْزَلِينَ (١٢٤) بَلَى إِنْ تَصْبِرُوا وَتَتَّقُوا وَيَأْتُوكُمْ مِنْ فَوْرِهِمْ هَذَا يُمْدِدْكُمْ رَبُّكُمْ بِخَمْسَةِ آلَافٍ مِنَ الْمَلَائِكَةِ مُسَوِّمِينَ (١٢٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِذْ) تَقُولُ: the implied wording may be "remember". It may also be a badal (substitute) of «إِذْ هَمَّتْ». It may also be an adverb (ẓarf) of «نَصَرَكُمْ». (أَلَنْ يَكْفِيَكُمْ): when the hamza of interrogation enters upon a negation, it turns it into an affirmation, while the tense of the verb remains as it was. [Translator's note: the source has «إِلَّا الْإِثْبَاتِ», evidently for «إِلَى الْإِثْبَاتِ».] And (أَنْ يُمِدَّكُمْ) is the fāʿil (agent) of «يَكْفِيَكُمْ». (بِثَلَاثَةِ آلَافٍ): the majority read with kasra on the fāʾ (i.e. the final letter of «ثَلَاثَةِ»). [Translator's note: the source says «الْفَاء»; the discussion concerns the tāʾ of «ثَلَاثَة», which is apparently what is meant.] It has been given a sukūn in the irregular readings (shawādhdh), on the basis that continuous speech was treated like the pause; when this tāʾ is paused upon, it is a substitute for the hāʾ on which one pauses, and some say that the feminine tāʾ itself is what is paused upon, and this is a dialectal form. It has also been read irregularly with a quiescent hāʾ; this too is treating continuous speech like the pause. Both are weak, because the muḍāf and the muḍāf ilayhi are like a single thing. (مُسَوِّمِينَ): with kasra on the wāw, i.e. "marking their horses" or "marking themselves", and with fatḥa on it (مُسَوَّمِينَ), as a passive.

ukberi-tibyan:126-126.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا جَعَلَهُ اللَّهُ إِلَّا بُشْرَى لَكُمْ وَلِتَطْمَئِنَّ قُلُوبُكُمْ بِهِ وَمَا النَّصْرُ إِلَّا مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ الْعَزِيزِ الْحَكِيمِ (١٢٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِلَّا بُشْرَى): the second object of «جَعَلَ». It may also be a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), with «جَعَلَ» being the one that takes a single object. The hāʾ in «جَعَلَهُ» refers back to the reinforcement (al-imdād), or to the marking (al-taswīm), or to the help (al-naṣr), or to the sending down (al-tanzīl).
(وَلِتَطْمَئِنَّ): conjoined to «بُشْرَى» if you make that an object of purpose, its implied form being "so that He may give you glad tidings and so that (your hearts) may be at rest". It may also be attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted verb, its implied form being "and so that your hearts may be at rest, He gave you glad tidings". [Translator's note: the source text is garbled here: «وَيَجُوزُ يَتَعَلَّقُ أَنْ يَتَعَلَّقَ» — a duplicated word.]

ukberi-tibyan:127-127.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لِيَقْطَعَ طَرَفًا مِنَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا أَوْ يَكْبِتَهُمْ فَيَنْقَلِبُوا خَائِبِينَ (١٢٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لِيَقْطَعَ طَرَفًا): the lām is attached (mutaʿalliq) to something omitted, its implied form being "in order to cut off a section, He reinforced you with the angels" or "He helped you". (أَوْ يَكْبِتَهُمْ): it is said that «أَوْ» is in the sense of the wāw. It is also said that it is for distribution (tafṣīl), i.e. the cutting off was for some of them and the humiliation (al-kabt) for others. The tāʾ in «يَكْبِتَهُمْ» is original (radical); it is also said that it is a substitute for dāl, from «كَبَدْتُهُ» "I struck his liver". (فَتَنْقَلِبُوا): conjoined to «يَقْطَعَ» or «يَكْبِتَهُمْ». [Translator's note: the source quotes «فَتَنْقَلِبُوا» with tāʾ; the verse has «فَيَنْقَلِبُوا».]

ukberi-tibyan:128-128.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَيْسَ لَكَ مِنَ الْأَمْرِ شَيْءٌ أَوْ يَتُوبَ عَلَيْهِمْ أَوْ يُعَذِّبَهُمْ فَإِنَّهُمْ ظَالِمُونَ (١٢٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَيْسَ لَكَ): the noun of «لَيْسَ» is «شَيْءٌ» and «لَكَ» is the khabar (predicate). «مِنَ الْأَمْرِ» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «شَيْء», because it is an adjective placed before it. (أَوْ يَتُوبَ عَلَيْهِمْ أَوْ يُعَذِّبَهُمْ): both are conjoined to «يَقْطَعَ». It is also said: «أَوْ» is in the sense of «إِلَّا أَنْ» ("unless").

ukberi-tibyan:130-130.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تَأْكُلُوا الرِّبَا أَضْعَافًا مُضَاعَفَةً وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ (١٣٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَضْعَافًا): a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «الرِّبَا», its implied form being «مُضَاعَفًا» ("multiplied").

ukberi-tibyan:133-133.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَسَارِعُوا إِلَى مَغْفِرَةٍ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ وَجَنَّةٍ عَرْضُهَا السَّمَوَاتُ وَالْأَرْضُ أُعِدَّتْ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ (١٣٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَسَارِعُوا): it is read with the wāw and without it. Whoever keeps it conjoins it to the commands before it, and whoever does not keep it begins a new sentence. Inclining (imāla) of the alif is permissible here because of the kasra of the rāʾ.
(عَرْضُهَا السَّمَاوَاتُ): the clause is in the position of the genitive (as an adjective of «جَنَّة»), and there is an omission in the wording, its implied form being "its breadth is like the breadth of the heavens". (أُعِدَّتْ): it may be in the position of the genitive as an adjective of «الْجَنَّة», or a ḥāl (circumstantial) of it, because it has been qualified, or a new sentence. It cannot be a ḥāl of the muḍāf ilayhi (i.e. the hāʾ in «عَرْضُهَا») for three reasons. First: that there is nothing to govern it, and what has come of that kind is interpreted, despite its weakness. Second: that «الْعَرْض» here is not meant as a real maṣdar (verbal noun), but rather means the extent (al-masāfa). Third: that it would entail separating the ḥāl from its owner (ṣāḥib al-ḥāl) by the khabar (predicate).

ukberi-tibyan:134-134.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الَّذِينَ يُنْفِقُونَ فِي السَّرَّاءِ وَالضَّرَّاءِ وَالْكَاظِمِينَ الْغَيْظَ وَالْعَافِينَ عَنِ النَّاسِ وَاللَّهُ يُحِبُّ الْمُحْسِنِينَ (١٣٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الَّذِينَ يُنْفِقُونَ): it may be an adjective of «الْمُتَّقِينَ»; or accusative by an implied «أَعْنِي» ("I mean"); or nominative by an implied «هُمْ» ("they are").
As for (الْكَاظِمِينَ), it is on (the views of) the genitive and the accusative.

ukberi-tibyan:135-135.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَالَّذِينَ إِذَا فَعَلُوا فَاحِشَةً أَوْ ظَلَمُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ ذَكَرُوا اللَّهَ فَاسْتَغْفَرُوا لِذُنُوبِهِمْ وَمَنْ يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَلَمْ يُصِرُّوا عَلَى مَا فَعَلُوا وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ (١٣٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَالَّذِينَ إِذَا فَعَلُوا): it may be conjoined to «الَّذِينَ يُنْفِقُونَ» under its three views. It may also be a mubtadaʾ (subject), with «أُولَئِكَ» a second mubtadaʾ, «جَزَاؤُهُمْ» a third, and «مَغْفِرَةٌ» the khabar (predicate) of the third, the whole being the khabar of «الَّذِينَ». And (ذَكَرُوا) is the answer of «إِذَا». (وَمَنْ): a mubtadaʾ, and (يَغْفِرُ) its khabar. (إِلَّا اللَّهُ): the agent of «يَغْفِرُ», or a badal (substitute) of the pronoun latent in it; and this (the latter) is the correct view, because if you make «اللَّه» the agent you would need to assume a pronoun, i.e. "and who is there — other than Allah — who forgives him the sins?" (وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ): in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in «يُصِرُّوا», or of the pronoun in «اسْتَغْفَرُوا». The object of «يَعْلَمُونَ» is omitted, i.e. "they know that they are held to account for it", or "(they know) Allah's pardon of it".

ukberi-tibyan:136-136.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أُولَئِكَ جَزَاؤُهُمْ مَغْفِرَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ وَجَنَّاتٌ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا وَنِعْمَ أَجْرُ الْعَامِلِينَ (١٣٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَنِعْمَ أَجْرُ): the one specified for praise (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-madḥ) is omitted, i.e. "and excellent is the reward — the Garden".

ukberi-tibyan:137-137.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَدْ خَلَتْ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ سُنَنٌ فَسِيرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ فَانْظُرُوا كَيْفَ كَانَ عَاقِبَةُ الْمُكَذِّبِينَ (١٣٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ سُنَنٌ): it may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to «خَلَتْ», or be a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «سُنَن». The fāʾ entered «سِيرُوا» because the meaning is conditional, i.e. "if you are in doubt, then travel". (كَيْفَ): the khabar (predicate) of «كَانَ», and «عَاقِبَةُ» its noun.

ukberi-tibyan:139-139.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَا تَهِنُوا وَلَا تَحْزَنُوا وَأَنْتُمُ الْأَعْلَوْنَ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ (١٣٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَلَا تَهِنُوا): the past is «وَهَنَ», and the wāw was dropped in the imperfect because it falls between a yāʾ and a kasra. And (الْأَعْلَوْنَ): its singular is «أَعْلَى»; the alif was dropped from it because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, and the fatḥa remains to indicate it.

ukberi-tibyan:140-141.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنْ يَمْسَسْكُمْ قَرْحٌ فَقَدْ مَسَّ الْقَوْمَ قَرْحٌ مِثْلُهُ وَتِلْكَ الْأَيَّامُ نُدَاوِلُهَا بَيْنَ النَّاسِ وَلِيَعْلَمَ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَيَتَّخِذَ مِنْكُمْ شُهَدَاءَ وَاللَّهُ لَا يُحِبُّ الظَّالِمِينَ (١٤٠) وَلِيُمَحِّصَ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَيَمْحَقَ الْكَافِرِينَ (١٤١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (قَرْحٌ): it is read with fatḥa on the qāf and a sukūn on the rāʾ; it is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of «قَرَحْتُهُ», when you wound him. It is read with ḍamma on the qāf and a sukūn on the rāʾ (قُرْحٌ), and this too means "wound"; al-Farrāʾ said: with ḍamma, it is the pain of wounds. It is read with ḍamma on both (قُرُحٌ), by harmonisation (itbāʿ), like «الْيُسْر» and «الْيُسُر», and «الطُّنْب» and «الطُّنُب». And it is read with fatḥa on both (قَرَحٌ); this is the maṣdar of «قَرِحَ يَقْرَحُ», when he comes to have an ulcer (qurḥa), and it means "to bleed". [Translator's note: the source prints the past as «قَرُحَ» with ḍamma; the usual form with imperfect «يَقْرَحُ» is «قَرِحَ».] (وَتِلْكَ): a mubtadaʾ (subject), and (الْأَيَّامُ) its khabar (predicate); (نُدَاوِلُهَا) is a clause in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), governed by the meaning of pointing (in the demonstrative). «الْأَيَّام» may also be a badal (substitute) or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition), with «نُدَاوِلُهَا» the khabar. It is also read «يُدَاوِلُهَا» with yāʾ, and the meaning is understood.
And (بَيْنَ النَّاسِ) is an adverb (ẓarf). It may also be a ḥāl of the hāʾ. (وَلِيَعْلَمَ): the lām is attached (mutaʿalliq) to something omitted, its implied form being "and so that Allah may know (the reason), He alternates them". [Translator's note: the source has «دَوَالَهَا», apparently for «دَاوَلَهَا» ("He alternated them").] It is also said that the implied wording is "so that they may take heed, and so that Allah may know". It is also said: the wāw is redundant (zāʾida). And (مِنْكُمْ) may be attached to «يَتَّخِذَ», or be a ḥāl of «شُهَدَاءَ». (وَلِيُمَحِّصَ): conjoined to «وَلِيَعْلَمَ».

ukberi-tibyan:142-142.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَمْ حَسِبْتُمْ أَنْ تَدْخُلُوا الْجَنَّةَ وَلَمَّا يَعْلَمِ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا مِنْكُمْ وَيَعْلَمَ الصَّابِرِينَ (١٤٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَمْ حَسِبْتُمْ): «أَمْ» here is the disconnected one (munqaṭiʿa), i.e. "nay, did you think?" And (أَنْ تَدْخُلُوا): «أَنْ» and the verb stand in place of the two objects; al-Akhfash said: the second object is omitted. (وَيَعْلَمَ الصَّابِرِينَ): it is read with kasra on the mīm, conjoined to the first (jussive verb), and with ḍamma on it, on the implied wording "and He knows". The majority reading is with fatḥa, and there are two views on it. The first: that it is likewise jussive (majzūm), but when the mīm was given a vowel because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, it was given fatḥa to harmonise with the fatḥa before it. The second view: that it is accusative by an implied «أَنْ», the wāw here having the sense of combination (jamʿ), like the one in their saying «لَا تَأْكُلِ السَّمَكَ وَتَشْرَبِ اللَّبَنَ» ("do not eat fish and drink milk (together)"). The implied wording is: "did you suppose that you would enter the Garden before Allah knows those who strive, and (before) He knows the steadfast?" What brings this meaning closer for you is that if you take the wāw as meaning «مَعَ» ("with"), the meaning and the iʿrāb are sound.

ukberi-tibyan:143-143.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَقَدْ كُنْتُمْ تَمَنَّوْنَ الْمَوْتَ مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ تَلْقَوْهُ فَقَدْ رَأَيْتُمُوهُ وَأَنْتُمْ تَنْظُرُونَ (١٤٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ تَلْقَوْهُ): the majority read it with the genitive by «مِنْ», and with its being put in construct with the clause.
It has also been read with ḍamma on the lām (مِنْ قَبْلُ), and the implied wording is: "and you used to wish for death — that you should meet it — before". So «أَنْ تَلْقَوْهُ» is a badal (substitute) of «الْمَوْت», a badal of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl), and what is meant is meeting the causes of death, because He said «فَقَدْ رَأَيْتُمُوهُ وَأَنْتُمْ تَنْظُرُونَ», and when one sees death (itself), no life remains after it. It is also read «تُلَاقُوهُ»; this is of the mufāʿala form that takes place between two parties, because whatever has met you, you have met it. It may also be from a single party, like «سَافَرْتُ» ("I travelled").

ukberi-tibyan:144-144.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا مُحَمَّدٌ إِلَّا رَسُولٌ قَدْ خَلَتْ مِنْ قَبْلِهِ الرُّسُلُ أَفَإِنْ مَاتَ أَوْ قُتِلَ انْقَلَبْتُمْ عَلَى أَعْقَابِكُمْ وَمَنْ يَنْقَلِبْ عَلَى عَقِبَيْهِ فَلَنْ يَضُرَّ اللَّهَ شَيْئًا وَسَيَجْزِي اللَّهُ الشَّاكِرِينَ (١٤٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (قَدْ خَلَتْ مِنْ قَبْلِهِ الرُّسُلُ): in the position of the nominative as an adjective of «رَسُول».
It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in «رَسُول». Ibn ʿAbbās read «رُسُلٌ», indefinite, which is close in meaning to the definite. «مِنْ» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «خَلَتْ», and it may also be a ḥāl of «الرُّسُل». «أَفَإِنْ مَاتَ»: according to Sībawayh the hamza is in its proper place, and the fāʾ indicates the connection of the condition with what precedes it. Yūnus said: the hamza in a case like this ought to enter upon the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), its implied form being "will you turn back on your heels if he dies?", because the purpose is to call attention to, or rebuke, this conditioned act. The doctrine of Sībawayh is the right one, for two reasons. First: if you put the apodosis first, the fāʾ would have no justification, since it is not valid to say «أَتَزُورُنِي فَإِنْ زُرْتُكَ» ("will you visit me, so if I visit you"). Of this kind is His saying (أَفَإِنْ مِتَّ فَهُمُ الْخَالِدُونَ). Second: that the hamza has the right to the head of the sentence, and «إِنْ» has the right to the head of the sentence, and both have occurred in their places; and the meaning is complete with the hamza entering upon the whole of the condition and apodosis, because the two are like a single thing.
(عَلَى أَعْقَابِكُمْ): a ḥāl, i.e. "returning".

ukberi-tibyan:145-145.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا كَانَ لِنَفْسٍ أَنْ تَمُوتَ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ كِتَابًا مُؤَجَّلًا وَمَنْ يُرِدْ ثَوَابَ الدُّنْيَا نُؤْتِهِ مِنْهَا وَمَنْ يُرِدْ ثَوَابَ الْآخِرَةِ نُؤْتِهِ مِنْهَا وَسَنَجْزِي الشَّاكِرِينَ (١٤٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَمَا كَانَ لِنَفْسٍ أَنْ تَمُوتَ): «أَنْ تَمُوتَ» is the noun of «كَانَ», and «إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ» the khabar (predicate); the lām is for clarification (tabyīn), attached (mutaʿalliq) to «كَانَ». It is also said: it is attached to something omitted, its implied form being "death (is) for a soul", with «أَنْ تَمُوتَ» a clarification of what is omitted. The lām cannot be attached to «تَمُوتَ», because that would involve putting the ṣila before the mawṣūl (i.e. part of the clause of «أَنْ» before «أَنْ»). Al-Zajjāj said: the implied wording is «وَمَا كَانَ نَفْسٌ لِتَمُوتَ» ("and no soul was to die"), then the lām was moved forward. (كِتَابًا): a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "He wrote that as a writing". (وَمَنْ يُرِدْ ثَوَابَ الدُّنْيَا): (read) with distinct pronunciation (of the dāl), according to the original, and with assimilation (of the dāl into the thāʾ), because the two are close. (نُؤْتِهِ مِنْهَا): like (يُؤَدِّهِ إِلَيْكَ). (وَسَنَجْزِي): with nūn and with yāʾ, and the meaning is understood.

ukberi-tibyan:146-146.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ نَبِيٍّ قَاتَلَ مَعَهُ رِبِّيُّونَ كَثِيرٌ فَمَا وَهَنُوا لِمَا أَصَابَهُمْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَمَا ضَعُفُوا وَمَا اسْتَكَانُوا وَاللَّهُ يُحِبُّ الصَّابِرِينَ (١٤٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَكَأَيِّنْ): its origin is «أَيّ», which denotes a part of a whole; the kāf of comparison was brought in upon it, and it came to have the meaning of «كَمْ» that is for (expressing) a large number — just as the kāf with «ذَا» in their word «كَذَا» was made to have a meaning that neither of the two had (separately), and just as the meaning of «لَوْلَا» after the combination did not belong to its two parts before it. There are five forms of it, all of which have been read. The well-known one is «كَأَيِّنْ», with a hamza followed by a doubled yāʾ; this is the original.
The second: «كَائِنٌ», with an alif followed by a hamza with kasra, without yāʾ. There are two views on it. The first: it is the active participle (fāʿil) of «كَانَ يَكُونُ»; this is related from al-Mubarrad, and it is far from correct, because were that so it would be declinable (muʿrab) and would not contain the meaning of large number. The second: that its origin is «كَأَيِّنْ»; the doubled yāʾ was moved before the hamza, so it became «كَيِّئٍ», whose measure is now «كَعْلِفٍ», because you have moved the second radical (ʿayn) and the third radical (lām) forward. Then the second yāʾ was dropped because of its heaviness with the vowel and the doubling, as they said «أَيْهُمَا» for «أَيِّهِمَا»; then the quiescent yāʾ was changed to alif, as it was changed in «آيَة» and «طَائِيّ». It is also said: the quiescent yāʾ was dropped and the vowelled one was moved forward, so it turned into alif. It is also said: nothing was dropped from it, but the vowelled (yāʾ) was moved forward and the other remained quiescent, and was dropped because of the tanwīn, like «قَاضٍ».
The third form: «كَإٍ», on the measure of «كَعٍ». There are two views on it. The first: that one of the two yāʾs was dropped as explained above, then the other was dropped because of the tanwīn. The second: that both yāʾs were dropped at once, and this was tolerated because the two words (particles) were blended together.
The fourth form: «كَأْيٌ», with a light yāʾ after the hamza. Its explanation is that he dropped the second yāʾ and gave the hamza a sukūn because of the blending of the two words, treating them as a single word — just as they gave the hāʾ a sukūn in «لَهْوَ» and «فَهْوَ» — and he gave the yāʾ a vowel because the letter before it is quiescent. The fifth: «كَيْئٌ», with a quiescent yāʾ before the hamza; this is the origin of «كَائِن», and it has been mentioned.
As for the tanwīn, it was kept in the word according to what it was originally entitled to. Some drop it in the pause, because it is a tanwīn, and some keep it in the pause, because the rule changed with the blending of the two words.
As for «أَيّ», Ibn Jinnī said: it is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of «أَوَى يَأْوِي», when (a thing) is gathered and joined together. Its original form is «أَوْيٌ»; the wāw and the yāʾ came together, the first of them preceding with a sukūn, so it was changed (to yāʾ) and assimilated, like «طَيّ» and «شَيّ». [Translator's note: the source prints the original form as «أَوَى»; the argument requires «أَوْيٌ» with a quiescent wāw.]
As for the position of «كَأَيِّنْ», it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); it is hardly ever used without «مِنْ» after it. On its khabar (predicate) there are three views. The first: «قُتِلَ», with the pronoun in «قُتِلَ» referring to the prophet, and it refers back to «كَأَيِّنْ», because «كَأَيِّنْ» has the meaning of "prophet". The better course is for the pronoun to refer back to the word «كَأَيِّنْ», as you say «مِائَةُ نَبِيٍّ قُتِلَ» ("a hundred prophets were killed"), the pronoun being for «الْمِائَة», since it is the mubtadaʾ.
If you say: were that so, you would make it feminine and say «قُتِلَتْ», it is answered: this is construed according to the meaning, because the implied wording is "many a man was killed". On this view «مَعَهُ رِبِّيُّونَ» is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in «قُتِلَ». The second: that «قُتِلَ» is in the position of the genitive as an adjective of «نَبِيّ», and «مَعَهُ رِبِّيُّونَ» is the khabar, as when you say «كَمْ مِنْ رَجُلٍ صَالِحٍ مَعَهُ مَالٌ» ("how many a righteous man has wealth with him"). The third view: that the khabar is omitted, i.e. "in the world", or "existing (صَائِرٌ)", and the like. On this view «قُتِلَ» may be an adjective of «نَبِيّ», and «مَعَهُ رِبِّيُّونَ» a ḥāl as explained above.
It is also possible that «قُتِلَ» is (predicated) of «رِبِّيُّونَ», so on this view there is no pronoun in it, and the clause is an adjective of «نَبِيّ»; or it may be a khabar, so that there come to be four views on the khabar.
It may also be an adjective of «نَبِيّ», with the khabar omitted, as we have mentioned.
It is also read «قَاتَلَ»; on this view the agent may be a latent pronoun, with what follows it a ḥāl, or the agent may be «رِبِّيُّونَ». [Translator's note: the author takes «قُتِلَ» (the reading of Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr) as his base text and «قَاتَلَ» as the other reading, although the verse quoted at the head of this entry has «قَاتَلَ».]
It is also read (قَتَّلَ) with doubling; on this view there is no pronoun in the verb, because of the (sense of) multiplicity, and a single person has no multiplicity in him — so Ibn Jinnī mentioned. But it is not impossible for it to contain the pronoun of the first (noun), because it has the meaning of a group.
«رِبِّيُّونَ» with kasra on the rāʾ is a relative adjective (nisba) from «الرِّبَّة», which is the group (al-jamāʿa). Ḍamma on the rāʾ in «الرُّبَّة» is also permissible, and on this «رُبِّيُّونَ» has been read with ḍamma. It is also said: whoever uses kasra is harmonising, and fatḥa is the original, it being a nisba to «الرَّبّ» ("the Lord"); and it has been read so (رَبِّيُّونَ). (فَمَا وَهَنُوا): the majority read with fatḥa on the hāʾ; it has been read with kasra on it, which is a dialectal form, though fatḥa is better known. It has also been read with a sukūn on it, as a lightening of the form with kasra.
And (اسْتَكَانُوا) is istafʿalū from «الْكَوْن», which is abasement. It is related from al-Farrāʾ that its origin is «اسْتَكَنُوا», the fatḥa being lengthened so that the alif arose. This is a mistake, because the second radical of the word is firm in all its inflections: you say «اسْتَكَانَ يَسْتَكِينُ اسْتِكَانَةً», so he is «مُسْتَكِينٌ» and «مُسْتَكَانٌ لَهُ»; and lengthening (ishbāʿ) does not happen to this extent.
